<file path="mycelium-ai-main/code_worker/main.py">
"""Mycelium OpenCode worker: register -> heartbeat -> claim task ->
fetch context -> run OpenCode locally -> complete -> poll again.

Executor, never authority. This worker only ever talks to the
coordinator through an explicit endpoint allow-list (read task
queue state, claim its own work, report its own results). It never
calls approval, write-approval, physical-execution, verification,
desktop-dispatch or task-creation endpoints: human YES, fingerprint
and safety gates stay fully owned by the existing backend routes.
Task payloads are goal descriptions, never commands: payload strings
are never executed as shell, never used as paths, and never become
Python code. Local OpenCode runs without --auto, so its own
permission system stays in charge on the worker machine.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import logging
import os
import re
import socket
import subprocess
import uuid

import httpx

logger = logging.getLogger("code_worker")

NODE_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$")

DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES = ["code.patch", "code.review", "code.test"]
DEFAULT_EXECUTORS = ["exec:code"]

# Explicit OpenCode model for every local run. Operator configuration
# only (--opencode-model); task payloads never select the model.
DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL = "opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free"

ALLOWED_KIND_PREFIXES = ("code.",)

# (method, path rule): path rule is either an exact prefix that must
# match fully, or a (prefix, suffix) pair. Anything else is refused
# BEFORE any network I/O, so this module cannot approve, write,
# execute physically, verify, dispatch desktop actions, or create
# tasks even if a task payload asked for it.
ALLOWED_CALLS = (
    ("POST", "/api/v1/nodes/register", None),
    ("POST", "/api/v1/nodes/", "/heartbeat"),
    ("POST", "/api/v1/tasks/claim/", None),
    ("POST", "/api/v1/tasks/", "/complete"),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/context/packet", None),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/project/package", None),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/missions/", None),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/tasks", None),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/presence", None),
    ("GET", "/api/v1/guide", None),
)


class WorkerRefusedError(ValueError):
    """Local policy refused an action; nothing was sent or run."""


def check_call(method: str, path: str) -> str:
    """Fail-closed endpoint gate. Returns the path when allowed."""
    clean = str(path or "").split("?", 1)[0]
    for allowed_method, prefix, suffix in ALLOWED_CALLS:
        if str(method or "").upper() != allowed_method:
            continue
        if not clean.startswith(prefix):
            continue
        if suffix is not None and not clean.endswith(suffix):
            continue
        if prefix == "/api/v1/tasks" and suffix is None:
            continue  # GET list only; POST create must match /complete
        return clean
    raise WorkerRefusedError(
        f"Worker never calls {method} {clean}; refusing")


def check_node_id(node_id: str) -> str:
    """Same identity alphabet as the coordinator registration."""
    cleaned = str(node_id or "").strip()[:80]
    if not cleaned or not NODE_ID_PATTERN.match(cleaned):
        raise WorkerRefusedError(
            "node_id must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$")
    return cleaned


MODEL_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$")


def check_model(model: str) -> str:
    """Operator-configured model id only, `provider/name` shape.
    Task payloads never reach this function; anything else is
    refused BEFORE any OpenCode run, so the effective model stays
    explicit and deterministic."""
    cleaned = str(model or "").strip()[:200]
    if not cleaned or not MODEL_PATTERN.match(cleaned):
        raise WorkerRefusedError(
            "opencode model must look like provider/name")
    return cleaned


def default_node_id() -> str:
    """opencode-<host>, sanitized into the coordinator alphabet."""
    host = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]", "-",
                  socket.gethostname() or "host").strip(".-")
    return check_node_id(f"opencode-{host or 'host'}")


def node_token_from(config: argparse.Namespace) -> str | None:
    """Local credential only: CLI flag or MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN env.
    Never hardcoded, never sent anywhere except the coordinator
    register/heartbeat/claim calls over the configured base URL."""
    token = config.node_token or os.environ.get(
        "MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN", "")
    return token.strip() or None


async def api_call(client: httpx.AsyncClient, method: str,
                   url: str, json: dict | None = None):
    """Single gated HTTP call. Policy first, network second."""
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit
    check_call(method, urlsplit(url).path)
    if method.upper() == "GET":
        response = await client.get(url)
    else:
        response = await client.post(url, json=json or {})
    response.raise_for_status()
    if not response.content:
        return None
    return response.json()


async def register(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                   registration: dict) -> None:
    await api_call(client, "POST",
                   f"{base_url}/nodes/register",
                   json=registration)


async def send_heartbeat(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                         node_id: str, token: str | None) -> None:
    heartbeat: dict = {"available": True}
    if token:
        heartbeat["node_token"] = token
    await api_call(client, "POST",
                   f"{base_url}/nodes/{node_id}/heartbeat",
                   json=heartbeat)


async def claim_task(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                     node_id: str, token: str | None) -> dict | None:
    url = f"{base_url}/tasks/claim/{node_id}"
    if token:
        from urllib.parse import quote
        url += f"?node_token={quote(token, safe='')}"
    return await api_call(client, "POST", url)


async def fetch_context(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                        goal: str,
                        conversation_id: str = "") -> dict:
    from urllib.parse import quote
    url = f"{base_url}/context/packet?goal={quote(goal[:500])}"
    scope = str(conversation_id or "").strip()[:80]
    if scope:
        url += f"&conversation_id={quote(scope, safe='')}"
    return await api_call(client, "GET", url) or {}


async def fetch_package(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                        goal: str,
                        conversation_id: str = "") -> dict:
    """Bounded project package (server caps; never file contents,
    never secrets, never permissions). Best-effort: callers proceed
    without it rather than refusing work over context."""
    from urllib.parse import quote
    url = f"{base_url}/project/package?q={quote(goal[:200])}"
    scope = str(conversation_id or "").strip()[:80]
    if scope:
        url += f"&conversation_id={quote(scope, safe='')}"
    return await api_call(client, "GET", url) or {}


async def fetch_mission_conversation(client: httpx.AsyncClient,
                                     base_url: str,
                                     mission_id: str) -> str:
    """conversation_id for a claimed mission, or "". Read-only,
    fail-soft: unknown missions simply yield no extra scope."""
    cleaned = str(mission_id or "").strip()[:80]
    if not cleaned:
        return ""
    from urllib.parse import quote
    try:
        mission = await api_call(
            client, "GET",
            f"{base_url}/missions/{quote(cleaned, safe='')}")
    except WorkerRefusedError:
        return ""
    except Exception:
        return ""
    if not isinstance(mission, dict):
        return ""
    return str(mission.get("conversation_id", "") or "").strip()[:80]


CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET = 1500


def render_task_context(packet: dict | None,
                        package: dict | None,
                        budget: int = CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET) -> str:
    """Render worker prompt context from allow-listed metadata only.

    Picks: package summary, packet constraints, open missions and
    research titles. Unknown keys, health content, file contents and
    anything secret-shaped never reach the prompt: only these four
    capped fields are read, everything else is dropped, and the
    total is truncated to budget. Pure function, no I/O.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []

    def _text(value) -> str:
        return str(value or "").strip()

    if isinstance(package, dict):
        summary = _text(package.get("summary"))[:600]
        if summary:
            lines.append(summary)
    if isinstance(packet, dict):
        constraints = packet.get("constraints")
        if isinstance(constraints, list):
            for entry in constraints[:5]:
                text = _text(entry)[:200]
                if text:
                    lines.append(f"- {text}")
        missions = packet.get("open_missions")
        if isinstance(missions, list):
            for entry in missions[:3]:
                if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                    continue
                text = (f"{_text(entry.get('id'))[:40]} "
                        f"{_text(entry.get('goal'))[:120]} "
                        f"[{_text(entry.get('status'))[:20]}]").strip()
                if text.strip("[] "):
                    lines.append(f"- {text}")
        research = packet.get("research")
        if isinstance(research, list):
            for entry in research[:3]:
                if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                    continue
                text = _text(entry.get("title"))[:120]
                if text:
                    lines.append(f"- research: {text}")
    rendered = "\n".join(lines).strip()
    return rendered[:max(1, int(budget or CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET))]


async def complete_task(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                        task_id: int, node_id: str, success: bool,
                        result: dict | None = None,
                        error: str | None = None) -> None:
    body: dict = {"success": bool(success),
                  "result": dict(result or {}),
                  "error": (str(error or "")[:2000] if error
                            else None),
                  "node_id": node_id}
    await api_call(client, "POST",
                   f"{base_url}/tasks/{task_id}/complete",
                   json=body)


def git_changed_files(workdir: str) -> list[str]:
    """Read-only git status scan for the result report."""
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z"],
            cwd=workdir, capture_output=True, timeout=30)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return []
    if completed.returncode != 0:
        return []
    files = []
    for entry in completed.stdout.split(b"\0"):
        text = entry.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
        if len(text) > 3:
            files.append(text[3:][:200])
    return sorted(set(files))[:50]


def build_opencode_argv(binary: str, prompt: str,
                          workdir: str,
                          model: str = DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL,
                          platform_name: str | None = None,
                          comspec: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Argv for one local OpenCode run, list form (never shell).

    The model is always passed explicitly with -m, so the run never
    depends on OpenCode's implicit default. The model is operator
    configuration (--opencode-model); task payloads never select it.

    On Windows a .cmd/.bat binary cannot start directly from
    CreateProcess, so it is launched explicitly through COMSPEC
    (`cmd /d /c`). The binary itself stays operator configuration
    (--opencode-bin); task payloads never select the executable.
    """
    argv = [binary, "run", prompt[:4000], "-m", check_model(model),
            "--format", "json", "--dir", target(workdir)]
    system = platform_name if platform_name is not None else os.name
    if system == "nt" and binary.lower().endswith((".cmd", ".bat")):
        shell = (comspec if comspec is not None
                 else os.environ.get("COMSPEC", ""))
        if not str(shell or "").strip():
            raise WorkerRefusedError(
                "COMSPEC is not set; refusing to guess the shell")
        return [shell, "/d", "/c"] + argv
    return argv


def target(workdir: str) -> str:
    """Validated local folder OpenCode runs in."""
    cleaned = str(workdir or "").strip()
    if not cleaned or not os.path.isdir(cleaned):
        raise WorkerRefusedError("workdir must be a local folder")
    return cleaned


def run_opencode(prompt: str, workdir: str,
                 binary: str = "opencode",
                 model: str = DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL,
                 timeout_seconds: int = 240) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Run local OpenCode once, non-interactively.

    Never passes --auto: the local OpenCode permission system stays
    in charge. Returns (ok, combined_output). Raises on transport
    failure so the caller reports failed, never fake success.
    """
    if not str(prompt or "").strip():
        raise WorkerRefusedError("OpenCode prompt must be text")
    folder = target(workdir)
    argv = build_opencode_argv(binary, prompt, folder, model=model)
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            argv, capture_output=True, timeout=int(timeout_seconds))
    except FileNotFoundError as error:
        raise WorkerRefusedError(
            f"OpenCode binary not found: {binary}") from error
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        raise WorkerRefusedError(
            f"OpenCode timed out after {timeout_seconds}s") from error
    output = (completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
              + completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))[-4000:]
    return completed.returncode == 0, output


def run_tests(command: str, workdir: str,
              timeout_seconds: int = 600) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Run the worker's FIXED local test command (never from the
    task payload: payload strings never become commands). Empty
    command means no tests; reported honestly as skipped."""
    if not str(command or "").strip():
        return True, "skipped: no --test-cmd configured"
    import shlex
    try:
        argv = shlex.split(command, posix=False)
    except ValueError as error:
        return False, f"test command refused: {error}"
    if not argv:
        return True, "skipped: no --test-cmd configured"
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            argv, cwd=workdir, capture_output=True,
            timeout=int(timeout_seconds))
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        return False, f"test run failed: {error}"[:1000]
    output = (completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
              + completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))[-2000:]
    return completed.returncode == 0, output


def check_task_kind(kind: str) -> str:
    """Only explicitly allowed kinds execute. Everything else is
    reported as failed/unsupported, never run silently."""
    cleaned = str(kind or "").strip()
    if any(cleaned.startswith(prefix)
           for prefix in ALLOWED_KIND_PREFIXES):
        return cleaned
    raise WorkerRefusedError(
        f"Task kind '{cleaned}' is not an allowed worker kind "
        f"(allowed prefixes: {list(ALLOWED_KIND_PREFIXES)}); "
        "refusing instead of executing")


def execute_code_task(task: dict, workdir: str,
                      opencode_binary: str = "opencode",
                      opencode_model: str = DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL,
                      test_command: str = "",
                      context: str = "",
                      runner=run_opencode) -> tuple[bool, dict, str | None]:
    """Execute one claimed task. Returns (success, result, error)
    in exactly the coordinator complete-contract shape."""
    try:
        kind = check_task_kind(str(task.get("kind", "")))
    except WorkerRefusedError as error:
        return False, {}, str(error)
    payload = task.get("payload", {})
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return False, {}, "task payload must be an object"
    goal = str(payload.get("goal", "") or "").strip()
    if not goal:
        return False, {}, "task has no goal; nothing to do"
    prompt = (f"Mycelium task #{task.get('id')} "
              f"({kind}): {goal}".strip())
    section = str(context or "").strip()[:CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET]
    if section:
        prompt = (f"{prompt}\n\nProject context (read-only, "
                  f"bounded):\n{section}")
    before = set(git_changed_files(workdir))
    try:
        ok, output = runner(prompt, workdir,
                            binary=opencode_binary,
                            model=check_model(opencode_model))
    except WorkerRefusedError as error:
        return False, {}, str(error)
    except Exception as error:
        return False, {}, f"OpenCode run failed: {error}"[:1000]
    after = set(git_changed_files(workdir))
    tests_ok, tests_output = run_tests(test_command, workdir)
    summary = (f"OpenCode {kind} finished "
               f"({'ok' if ok else 'non-zero exit'}); "
               f"tests {'passed' if tests_ok else 'failed'}; "
               f"{len(after - before)} file(s) changed.")
    result = {"files_changed": sorted(after - before)[:50],
              "tests": [{"command": test_command or "skipped",
                         "passed": tests_ok,
                         "output": tests_output[:2000]}],
              "summary": summary[:1000],
              "opencode_output": output[-2000:]}
    if not ok:
        return False, result, "OpenCode exited non-zero"
    if not tests_ok and test_command.strip():
        return False, result, "local tests failed"
    return True, result, None


def arguments() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Mycelium OpenCode worker (executor, not authority)")
    parser.add_argument("--coordinator",
                        default="http://localhost:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--node-id", default=None,
                        help="Defaults to opencode-<hostname>")
    parser.add_argument("--tier", choices=["seed", "worker", "core"],
                        default="worker")
    parser.add_argument("--capability", action="append",
                        default=[],
                        help="Can be supplied more than once")
    parser.add_argument("--executor", action="append", default=[],
                        help="Executors to advertise, exec:<kind>")
    parser.add_argument("--node-token", default=None,
                        help="Node credential (or MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN)")
    parser.add_argument("--workdir", default=os.getcwd(),
                        help="Local folder OpenCode runs in")
    parser.add_argument("--opencode-bin", default="opencode",
                        help="Local OpenCode binary")
    parser.add_argument("--opencode-model",
                        default=DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL,
                        help="Explicit OpenCode model (provider/name)")
    parser.add_argument("--test-cmd", default="",
                        help="Fixed local test command (never from payload)")
    parser.add_argument("--poll-seconds", type=float, default=10.0)
    parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true",
                        help="Single poll iteration, then exit")
    return parser.parse_args()


async def run_once(client: httpx.AsyncClient, base_url: str,
                   node_id: str, token: str | None,
                   workdir: str, opencode_binary: str,
                   test_command: str,
                   opencode_model: str = DEFAULT_OPENCODE_MODEL,
                   runner=run_opencode) -> str:
    """One poll iteration: heartbeat, claim, context, execute,
    complete. Returns a short status word for logs."""
    await send_heartbeat(client, base_url, node_id, token)
    task = await claim_task(client, base_url, node_id, token)
    if not task:
        return "idle"
    goal = ""
    try:
        payload = task.get("payload", {})
        if isinstance(payload, dict):
            goal = str(payload.get("goal", "") or "")
        conversation_id = ""
        try:
            mission_id = task.get("mission_id", "")
            if isinstance(mission_id, str) and mission_id.strip():
                conversation_id = await fetch_mission_conversation(
                    client, base_url, mission_id)
        except Exception:
            conversation_id = ""
        packet: dict = {}
        package: dict = {}
        try:
            packet = await fetch_context(
                client, base_url, goal or str(task.get(
                    "kind", "")),
                conversation_id=conversation_id)
        except Exception:
            packet = {}
        try:
            package = await fetch_package(
                client, base_url, goal or str(task.get(
                    "kind", "")),
                conversation_id=conversation_id)
        except Exception:
            package = {}
        context = render_task_context(packet, package)
        success, result, error = execute_code_task(
            {"kind": task.get("kind"), "payload": payload,
             "mission_id": task.get("mission_id")},
            workdir, opencode_binary=opencode_binary,
            opencode_model=opencode_model,
            test_command=test_command, context=context,
            runner=runner)
    except WorkerRefusedError as error:
        success, result, error = False, {}, str(error)
    except Exception as error:
        success, result, error = (
            False, {}, f"worker error: {error}"[:1000])
    await complete_task(client, base_url, int(task.get("id")),
                        node_id, success, result, error)
    return "completed" if success else "failed"


async def run(config: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    base_url = config.coordinator.rstrip("/") + "/api/v1"
    token = node_token_from(config)
    node_id = check_node_id(config.node_id or default_node_id())
    capabilities = list(config.capability or DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES)
    executors = list(config.executor or DEFAULT_EXECUTORS)
    registration = {"node_id": node_id,
                    "hostname": socket.gethostname(),
                    "tier": config.tier,
                    "capabilities": capabilities,
                    "executors": executors}
    if token:
        registration["node_token"] = token
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10) as client:
        await register(client, base_url, registration)
        logger.info("code worker %s registered (%s)",
                    node_id, config.tier)
        while True:
            try:
                status = await run_once(
                    client, base_url, node_id, token,
                    str(config.workdir),
                    str(config.opencode_bin),
                    str(config.test_cmd or ""),
                    opencode_model=str(config.opencode_model))
                logger.info("poll: %s", status)
            except httpx.HTTPError as error:
                logger.warning("coordinator unavailable: %s", error)
            if config.once:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(config.poll_seconds)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    asyncio.run(run(arguments()))

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/code_worker/README.md">
# Mycelium OpenCode worker

External executor for code tasks. Registers as a normal Mycelium
node, polls the task queue, runs local OpenCode for `code.*` tasks
and reports results. Executor, never authority: it cannot approve,
write, execute physically, verify, or create tasks.

## Start

```powershell
python -m code_worker.main --coordinator http://127.0.0.1:8000 --workdir C:\path\to\repo --poll-seconds 10
```

Single iteration (no loop):

```powershell
python -m code_worker.main --coordinator http://127.0.0.1:8000 --workdir C:\path\to\repo --once
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN` | Node credential (or `--node-token`). Bound on first register, required afterwards. Never hardcoded. |
| `PATH` | Must contain the `opencode` binary (or `--opencode-bin`). |

No other secrets are read. Task results sent to the coordinator
contain only `files_changed`, `tests`, `summary` and a tail of
OpenCode output — never tokens or credentials.

## Node identity

- `node-id`: `opencode-<hostname>` by default (override with `--node-id`).
- `tier`: `worker` (override with `--tier seed|worker|core`).
- Capabilities: `code.patch`, `code.review`, `code.test` (override with `--capability`, repeatable).
- Executors: `exec:code` (override with `--executor`, repeatable).
- Heartbeat every poll with `available: True`; a node unseen for
  60s is stale and gets no work until it heartbeats again.

## Allowed task kinds

Only the `code.*` prefix executes (`code.patch`, `code.review`,
`code.test`, …). Any other kind is reported back as
`failed/unsupported` without running anything, never silently.

The worker calls exactly these coordinator endpoints (anything
else is refused locally before any network I/O):

- `POST /api/v1/nodes/register`, `POST /api/v1/nodes/{id}/heartbeat`
- `POST /api/v1/tasks/claim/{id}`, `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/complete`
- `GET /api/v1/context/packet`, `GET /api/v1/project/package`
- `GET /api/v1/tasks`, `GET /api/v1/presence`, `GET /api/v1/guide`

## Safety policy

- Task payloads are goal descriptions, never commands: payload
  strings never become shell, paths, or Python. The fixed local
  test command comes only from `--test-cmd`, never from a task.
- Local OpenCode runs as `opencode run <prompt> --format json
  --dir <workdir>`, **never with `--auto`**: the local OpenCode
  permission system stays in charge on the worker machine.
- The worker never calls mission-approve, write-approve/execute/
  verify, printer/robot/drone, desktop-dispatch, or task-create
  endpoints, and never sends a human YES. Existing gates stay the
  sole owners of human approval.
- Changed files are detected with read-only `git status`
  (non-git folders simply report none).

## Multiple workers

Run one process per machine with a distinct `--node-id`. The
coordinator distributes by capability subset + tier + priority;
claims are atomic, so two workers never get the same task. A
crashed worker's lease expires on the next claim (requeue below
3 attempts, failed at the limit, blocked for uncertain physical
work) — no coordinator action needed.

## Going offline

Stop the process or let heartbeats lapse: after 60s without a
heartbeat the node is stale and receives nothing. Assigned work
returns to the queue via lease expiry; nothing blocks the
coordinator.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/adapter_contracts.py">
"""Adapter data contracts for Mycelium (M6.1).

This module defines the REASON/PLAN half of a future sense–reason–plan–
approve–execute loop. It stops at PROPOSAL: there is no execution surface
here and nothing in this module performs I/O of any kind.

- AdapterRequest carries validated input plus its provenance.
- AdapterProposal carries a proposed action plus its own provenance, and
  always requires human approval (``requires_approval`` is forced True).

ID rules reuse the stable world-model prefixes where they apply: ``mod_``
for INVENTory models, ``task_`` for INVENTory tasks. Adapter and node IDs
follow the coordinator's safe identifier pattern. No INVENTory code is
imported; the local Provenance mirror in inventory_read is reused.
"""

from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator

from .inventory_read import Provenance

MODEL_ID_PREFIX = "mod_"
TASK_ID_PREFIX = "task_"
SAFE_ID_PATTERN = r"^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$"


class AdapterRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    request_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80, pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    adapter_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=80, pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    model_id: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=120)
    node_id: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=3, max_length=80,
                                pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    task_id: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=120)
    input: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    parameters: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    provenance: Provenance = Field(default_factory=Provenance)

    @field_validator("model_id")
    @classmethod
    def _check_model_id(cls, value):
        if value is not None and not value.startswith(MODEL_ID_PREFIX):
            raise ValueError(f"model_id must start with '{MODEL_ID_PREFIX}'")
        return value

    @field_validator("task_id")
    @classmethod
    def _check_task_id(cls, value):
        if value is not None and not value.startswith(TASK_ID_PREFIX):
            raise ValueError(f"task_id must start with '{TASK_ID_PREFIX}'")
        return value


class AdapterProposal(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    proposal_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80, pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    request_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80, pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    adapter_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=80, pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    model_id: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=120)
    node_id: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=3, max_length=80,
                                pattern=SAFE_ID_PATTERN)
    task_id: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=120)
    proposed_action: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    expected_output: str = Field(default="", max_length=2000)
    risks: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
    provenance: Provenance = Field(default_factory=Provenance)
    requires_approval: bool = True

    @field_validator("model_id")
    @classmethod
    def _check_model_id(cls, value):
        if value is not None and not value.startswith(MODEL_ID_PREFIX):
            raise ValueError(f"model_id must start with '{MODEL_ID_PREFIX}'")
        return value

    @field_validator("task_id")
    @classmethod
    def _check_task_id(cls, value):
        if value is not None and not value.startswith(TASK_ID_PREFIX):
            raise ValueError(f"task_id must start with '{TASK_ID_PREFIX}'")
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _force_approval(self) -> "AdapterProposal":
        if self.requires_approval is not True:
            raise ValueError("AdapterProposal always requires human approval")
        if self.provenance.human_verified:
            raise ValueError("AdapterProposal provenance must not claim human approval")
        return self
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/adapters.py">
"""Adapter interface and deterministic reference adapter (M6.1).

The Adapter protocol ends at PROPOSAL. This module offers data validation
and proposal construction only; it performs no side effects of any kind.

ReferenceNoopAdapter is mock-only and fully deterministic: given the same
request it always returns the same proposal. It performs no analysis; it
structures the input into an explicit proposal that a human must approve.
"""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

from .adapter_contracts import AdapterProposal, AdapterRequest
from .inventory_read import Provenance

REFERENCE_ADAPTER_ID = "reference-noop"


class Adapter(ABC):
    """Executionless adapter interface: validate in, proposal out."""

    adapter_id: str = ""

    @abstractmethod
    def propose(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> AdapterProposal:
        """Produce an AdapterProposal for a validated request. No side effects."""
        raise NotImplementedError


class ReferenceNoopAdapter(Adapter):
    """Deterministic mock adapter. Proposes only; never acts."""

    adapter_id = REFERENCE_ADAPTER_ID

    def propose(self, request: AdapterRequest) -> AdapterProposal:
        if request.adapter_id != self.adapter_id:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Request targets adapter '{request.adapter_id}', "
                f"this is '{self.adapter_id}'"
            )
        input_keys = sorted(str(key) for key in request.input.keys())
        discussed = ", ".join(input_keys) if input_keys else "no input fields"
        source = request.provenance
        proposal_id = f"prop-{request.request_id}"[:80]
        return AdapterProposal(
            proposal_id=proposal_id,
            request_id=request.request_id,
            adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
            model_id=request.model_id,
            node_id=request.node_id,
            task_id=request.task_id,
            proposed_action=(
                "No action taken. A human must review the input "
                f"({discussed}) and decide the next step."
            ),
            expected_output="A human-approved plan, or a rejection with a reason.",
            risks=["input has not been independently verified",
                   "no execution has been performed"],
            provenance=Provenance(
                source_type="ai-generated",
                creator_id=f"adapter:{self.adapter_id}",
                human_verified=False,
                notes=(f"proposal for request {request.request_id}; "
                       f"input provenance {source.source_type}/"
                       f"{source.creator_id} preserved without endorsement"),
            ),
            requires_approval=True,
        )

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/advisor_proposals.py">
"""Advice text to optional AdapterProposal (M8.2, untrusted input).

A model answer may carry one fenced ```json block describing a proposal.
Everything inside that block is UNTRUSTED: identities, provenance and
approval flags supplied by the model are never taken at face value.

Rules enforced here, on top of the M6.1 schema itself:

- proposal_id, request_id and adapter_id always come from the caller,
  never from the model. proposal_id derives deterministically.
- model_id, node_id and task_id from the block are accepted only when
  they pass M6.1 validation; anything else voids the whole proposal.
- provenance is always set by this module (ai-generated, unverified,
  referencing the advice); model-supplied provenance is ignored.
- requires_approval can only be True (M6.1 schema voids anything else).
- malformed blocks, missing actions and oversized text void the proposal
  and leave plain text advice standing alone (fail-closed, no fabrication).

No queue, no staging, no promotion, no approval, no dispatch. The result
is either a validated proposal or None.
"""

import json
import re
from typing import Any

from pydantic import ValidationError

from .adapter_contracts import AdapterProposal
from .inventory_read import Provenance

_FENCE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"```json\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```",
                            re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
MAX_BLOCK_CHARS = 2000
MAX_ACTION_CHARS = 2000
MAX_TEXT_LIST_ITEMS = 20
MAX_TEXT_ITEM_CHARS = 200


def _clean_text(value, max_chars: int) -> str | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None
    text = value.strip()
    if not text or len(text) > max_chars:
        return None
    return text


def _clean_text_list(value) -> list[str] | None:
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    cleaned: list[str] = []
    for item in value[:MAX_TEXT_LIST_ITEMS]:
        text = _clean_text(item, MAX_TEXT_ITEM_CHARS)
        if text is None:
            return None
        cleaned.append(text)
    return cleaned


def _proposal_id_for(request_id: str) -> str:
    return f"prop-{request_id}"[:80]


def extract_proposal(advice: str, *, adapter_id: str, request_id: str,
                     model_id: str | None = None, node_id: str | None = None,
                     task_id: str | None = None) -> AdapterProposal | None:
    """Build a validated proposal from advice text, or None.

    IDs come from explicit arguments (caller-controlled). The text block
    may only supply proposed_action, expected_output, risks, and the
    optional model/node/task links, each strictly validated.
    """
    if not isinstance(advice, str) or not advice.strip():
        return None
    match = _FENCE_PATTERN.search(advice)
    if match is None:
        return None
    raw = match.group(1)
    if len(raw) > MAX_BLOCK_CHARS:
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    if "requires_approval" in data and data["requires_approval"] is not True:
        return None
    claimed_provenance = data.get("provenance")
    if isinstance(claimed_provenance, dict) and claimed_provenance.get(
            "human_verified"):
        return None
    action = _clean_text(data.get("proposed_action"), MAX_ACTION_CHARS)
    if action is None:
        return None
    expected = _clean_text(data.get("expected_output", ""), MAX_ACTION_CHARS)
    if expected is None:
        return None
    risks = _clean_text_list(data.get("risks", []))
    if risks is None:
        return None
    links: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key in ("model_id", "node_id", "task_id"):
        present = key in data
        supplied = data.get(key)
        fallback = {"model_id": model_id, "node_id": node_id,
                    "task_id": task_id}[key]
        if present:
            if supplied is not None and not isinstance(supplied, str):
                return None
            links[key] = supplied
        else:
            links[key] = fallback
    try:
        return AdapterProposal(
            proposal_id=_proposal_id_for(request_id),
            request_id=request_id,
            adapter_id=adapter_id,
            model_id=links["model_id"],
            node_id=links["node_id"],
            task_id=links["task_id"],
            proposed_action=action,
            expected_output=expected,
            risks=risks,
            provenance=Provenance(
                source_type="ai-generated",
                creator_id=f"advisor:{adapter_id}",
                human_verified=False,
                notes="proposal parsed from untrusted model text; "
                      "identities validated, provenance set locally",
            ),
            requires_approval=True,
        )
    except (ValidationError, ValueError, TypeError):
        return None
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/agenda.py">
"""Local-first agenda importer (BIG #28 §15).

Generic ICS import with preview-before-import, UID-based
duplicate detection, and explicit source provenance. No Google
Calendar required; URL feeds only when explicitly configured
(and only loopback-safe fetching through the existing bridge
policy — remote ICS fetch is NOT implemented; paste or upload
the .ics text instead).

Model: ``agenda_sources`` (one row per import: label, origin,
imported_at) and ``agenda_events`` (uid, source, title,
start/end, location, description, recurrence, provenance).

Rules:

- Imported events are read-only world/context data. Editing
  goes through no write path at all in V1 (there is none).
- No invented events: every row comes from a parsed VEVENT
  with a UID (generated deterministically from content when
  the file omits one, labelled as derived).
- Duplicate = same UID within the same source; re-imports
  update the row instead of duplicating it.
- Parser is stdlib-only, bounded (MAX_EVENTS, MAX_CHARS),
  and refuses malformed input instead of guessing.
"""

import hashlib
import re
import secrets
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone

MAX_ICS_CHARS = 500_000
MAX_EVENTS = 500
MAX_FIELD_CHARS = 2000


class AgendaRefusedError(ValueError):
    """Agenda input refused; nothing stored."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AgendaEvent:
    event_id: str = ""
    uid: str = ""
    title: str = ""
    start: str = ""
    end: str = ""
    location: str = ""
    description: str = ""
    recurrence: str = ""
    source_label: str = ""
    provenance_note: str = ""


@dataclass
class AgendaPreview:
    source_label: str = ""
    events: list = field(default_factory=list)
    duplicates: int = 0
    refused: str = ""


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def parse_ics(text: str, *, source_label: str = "import") -> AgendaPreview:
    """Parse .ics text into a preview. Pure function, no storage."""
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        raise AgendaRefusedError("ICS import needs non-empty .ics text")
    if len(text) > MAX_ICS_CHARS:
        raise AgendaRefusedError(
            f"ICS text too large ({len(text)} chars, "
            f"max {MAX_ICS_CHARS})")
    unfolded = _unfold(text)
    if "BEGIN:VCALENDAR" not in unfolded:
        raise AgendaRefusedError(
            "Not an ICS calendar (missing BEGIN:VCALENDAR)")
    blocks = re.findall(
        r"BEGIN:VEVENT(.*?)END:VEVENT", unfolded,
        flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
    if not blocks:
        raise AgendaRefusedError("No VEVENT entries found")
    if len(blocks) > MAX_EVENTS:
        raise AgendaRefusedError(
            f"Too many events ({len(blocks)}, max {MAX_EVENTS})")
    label = (source_label or "import").strip()[:120] or "import"
    events: list[AgendaEvent] = []
    for block in blocks:
        props = _properties(block)
        uid = props.get("UID", "").strip()[:300]
        title = _clean(props.get("SUMMARY", ""))[:200] or "(no title)"
        start = _clean(props.get("DTSTART", ""))[:64]
        end = _clean(props.get("DTEND", ""))[:64]
        if not uid:
            derived = hashlib.sha256(
                f"{title}|{start}|{end}".encode(
                    "utf-8", "replace")).hexdigest()[:16]
            uid = f"derived-{derived}"
        events.append(AgendaEvent(
            event_id=f"evt_{secrets.token_hex(4)}",
            uid=uid, title=title, start=start, end=end,
            location=_clean(props.get("LOCATION", ""))[:300],
            description=_clean(props.get("DESCRIPTION", ""))[:2000],
            recurrence=_clean(props.get("RRULE", ""))[:300],
            source_label=label,
            provenance_note=(
                "ics-import; read-only context, never a commitment "
                "fact" + ("; uid derived from content"
                          if uid.startswith("derived-") else ""))))
    return AgendaPreview(source_label=label, events=events)


def _unfold(text: str) -> str:
    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").split("\n")
    merged: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        if line[:1] in (" ", "\t") and merged:
            merged[-1] += line[1:]
        else:
            merged.append(line)
    return "\n".join(merged)


def _properties(block: str) -> dict:
    props: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in block.split("\n"):
        if ":" not in line:
            continue
        name, _, value = line.partition(":")
        name = name.split(";")[0].strip().upper()
        if name and name not in props:
            props[name] = value.strip().replace("\\n", "\n").replace(
                "\\,", ",").replace("\\;", ";")[:MAX_FIELD_CHARS]
    return props


def _clean(value: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(str(value or "").split())


# -- storage (chat/agent database; additive tables, same discipline) --

def init_agenda_tables(db) -> None:
    db.executescript("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agenda_sources (
            source_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            label TEXT NOT NULL,
            origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ics-import',
            event_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            imported_at TEXT NOT NULL
        );
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agenda_events (
            event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            uid TEXT NOT NULL,
            title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            start TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            end_time TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            location TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            recurrence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            provenance TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
            created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
            UNIQUE(source_id, uid)
        );
        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agenda_start
            ON agenda_events(start);
        """)


def store_preview(db, preview: AgendaPreview,
                  *, origin: str = "ics-import") -> dict:
    """Store a previewed import with UID dedup. Re-importing the
    same label reuses the source row, so same-UID events update
    instead of duplicating. Returns counts."""
    if not preview.events:
        raise AgendaRefusedError("Nothing to import")
    existing_source = db.execute(
        "SELECT source_id FROM agenda_sources WHERE label=? "
        "ORDER BY imported_at DESC LIMIT 1",
        (preview.source_label,)).fetchone()
    if existing_source is None:
        source_id = f"agsrc_{secrets.token_hex(4)}"
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO agenda_sources (source_id, label, origin, "
            "event_count, imported_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (source_id, preview.source_label, origin[:80],
             len(preview.events), now()))
    else:
        source_id = existing_source["source_id"]
    inserted = 0
    updated = 0
    for event in preview.events:
        existing = db.execute(
            "SELECT event_id FROM agenda_events WHERE source_id=? "
            "AND uid=?", (source_id, event.uid)).fetchone()
        if existing is None:
            db.execute(
                """INSERT INTO agenda_events (event_id, source_id,
                uid, title, start, end_time, location, description,
                recurrence, provenance, created_at) VALUES
                (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                (event.event_id, source_id, event.uid,
                 event.title, event.start, event.end,
                 event.location, event.description,
                 event.recurrence, event.provenance_note, now()))
            inserted += 1
        else:
            db.execute(
                """UPDATE agenda_events SET title=?, start=?,
                end_time=?, location=?, description=?,
                recurrence=? WHERE event_id=?""",
                (event.title, event.start, event.end,
                 event.location, event.description,
                 event.recurrence, existing["event_id"]))
            updated += 1
    db.execute(
        "UPDATE agenda_sources SET event_count=?, imported_at=? "
        "WHERE source_id=?",
        (inserted + updated, now(), source_id))
    return {"source_id": source_id, "inserted": inserted,
            "updated": updated, "total": len(preview.events)}


def list_events(db, *, limit: int = 100,
                upcoming_only: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """List stored agenda events. Read-only context, never facts."""
    rows = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM agenda_events ORDER BY start ASC LIMIT ?",
        (max(1, min(int(limit or 100), 500)),)).fetchall()
    events = [dict(row) for row in rows]
    if upcoming_only:
        today = time.strftime("%Y%m%d")
        events = [row for row in events
                  if str(row.get("start", "")) >= today]
    return events


def list_sources(db) -> list[dict]:
    return [dict(row) for row in db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM agenda_sources ORDER BY imported_at DESC"
        " LIMIT 50").fetchall()]

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/agent_results.py">
"""Agent action results: what the desktop agent reports back (Fase J).

A result closes one ComputerAction. Statuses are completed, failed,
cancelled or blocked — never "verified": a result describes what
happened, and verification stays a separate human act. Provenance is
always agent-reported/unverified here.

Rules (tested):

- status must be known; unknown statuses fail closed.
- completed results carry no error; failed/blocked results must carry
  one (max 2000 chars, matching the coordinator TaskResult budget).
- cancelled results are terminal and operator-initiated.
- observation_reference, when present, must be a plain observation ID.
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from .inventory_read import Provenance

ResultStatus = Literal["completed", "failed", "cancelled", "blocked"]
VALID_STATUSES = frozenset({"completed", "failed", "cancelled", "blocked"})
MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 2000


class AgentActionResult(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    action_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80)
    status: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20)
    started_at: str = ""
    completed_at: str = ""
    error: str = Field(default="", max_length=MAX_ERROR_CHARS)
    observation_reference: str = Field(default="", max_length=80)
    provenance: Provenance = Field(default_factory=Provenance)


def new_result(action_id: str, status: str, *,
               error: str = "",
               observation_reference: str = "") -> AgentActionResult:
    if status not in VALID_STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown result status '{status}'")
    text = str(error or "")
    if status in ("failed", "blocked") and not text.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"Status '{status}' needs an error description")
    if status == "completed" and text.strip():
        raise ValueError("Completed results carry no error")
    reference = str(observation_reference or "").strip()
    if reference and not reference.startswith("obs-"):
        raise ValueError("observation_reference must be an observation ID")
    return AgentActionResult(
        action_id=action_id,
        status=status,
        error=text.strip()[:MAX_ERROR_CHARS],
        observation_reference=reference,
        provenance=Provenance(
            source_type="sensor-observed",
            creator_id="desktop-agent",
            human_verified=False,
            notes="agent-reported outcome; not human verified",
        ),
    )

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/approval.py">
"""Human approval gate for adapter proposals (M6.3).

Pure decision layer: a proposal is never approved automatically, and an
approval never starts anything. The outcome is a data record that a future
system may consult before treating a proposal as approved.

Policy (explicit, tested):

- Only an exact ``YES`` approves; only an exact ``NO`` is a deliberate
  rejection. Every other input denies. No normalization is applied.
- An approval binds to one specific proposal: both ``proposal_id`` and
  ``request_id`` must match, otherwise the call fails closed.
- ``requires_approval=False`` can never bypass this gate: proposals that
  lack it are refused outright.
- Approval records the decision; it never rewrites the proposal's
  provenance and never marks data as human-verified.
- No wall-clock values, no shared mutable state, no retries, no I/O.
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from .adapter_contracts import AdapterProposal
from .inventory_read import Provenance

ApprovalDecision = Literal["approved", "rejected"]
APPROVE_TEXT = "YES"
REJECT_TEXT = "NO"


class ApprovalRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    proposal_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80)
    request_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80)


class ApprovalResult(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    proposal_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80)
    request_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=80)
    decision: ApprovalDecision
    approved: bool
    decided_by: str = Field(default="human", min_length=1, max_length=80)
    note: str = Field(default="", max_length=500)
    proposal_provenance: Provenance = Field(default_factory=Provenance)


def request_approval(proposal: AdapterProposal) -> ApprovalRequest:
    """Open an approval request bound to one specific proposal."""
    if not isinstance(proposal, AdapterProposal):
        raise ValueError("Approval needs an AdapterProposal")
    if proposal.requires_approval is not True:
        raise ValueError("Proposals without requires_approval cannot enter the gate")
    return ApprovalRequest(proposal_id=proposal.proposal_id,
                           request_id=proposal.request_id)


def _bind(request: ApprovalRequest, proposal: AdapterProposal) -> None:
    if (request.proposal_id != proposal.proposal_id
            or request.request_id != proposal.request_id):
        raise ValueError("Approval request does not match this proposal")


def _result(request: ApprovalRequest, proposal: AdapterProposal,
            decision: ApprovalDecision, decided_by: str, note: str = "") -> ApprovalResult:
    return ApprovalResult(
        proposal_id=request.proposal_id,
        request_id=request.request_id,
        decision=decision,
        approved=(decision == "approved"),
        decided_by=decided_by,
        note=note,
        proposal_provenance=proposal.provenance,
    )


def decide(request: ApprovalRequest, proposal: AdapterProposal, response: str,
           decided_by: str = "human") -> ApprovalResult:
    """Resolve raw human input: exact YES approves, anything else denies."""
    _bind(request, proposal)
    if not isinstance(decided_by, str) or not decided_by.strip():
        raise ValueError("decided_by must be non-empty text")
    if response == APPROVE_TEXT:
        return _result(request, proposal, "approved", decided_by.strip())
    if response == REJECT_TEXT:
        return _result(request, proposal, "rejected", decided_by.strip(),
                       note="human answered NO")
    return _result(request, proposal, "rejected", decided_by.strip(),
                   note="unrecognized response; default deny")


def approve(request: ApprovalRequest, proposal: AdapterProposal,
            decided_by: str = "human") -> ApprovalResult:
    """Record an explicit human YES. Calling this IS the human decision."""
    _bind(request, proposal)
    if not isinstance(decided_by, str) or not decided_by.strip():
        raise ValueError("decided_by must be non-empty text")
    return _result(request, proposal, "approved", decided_by.strip())


def reject(request: ApprovalRequest, proposal: AdapterProposal,
           decided_by: str = "human", note: str = "") -> ApprovalResult:
    """Record an explicit human NO."""
    _bind(request, proposal)
    if not isinstance(decided_by, str) or not decided_by.strip():
        raise ValueError("decided_by must be non-empty text")
    if not isinstance(note, str):
        raise ValueError("note must be text")
    return _result(request, proposal, "rejected", decided_by.strip(),
                   note=note[:500])
