<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/3d-architecture.md">
# 3D & Physical Pipeline Architecture (BIG #7)

Van digitaal object naar fysiek object — door dezelfde poorten
als alles else in Mycelium:

```
INVENTory object / idea
  ↓ generate (deterministic test geometry, local only)
3D mesh bytes (never valid/printable/safe by themselves)
  ↓ validate (stdlib STL/OBJ parsing, finite, bounded)
MeshReport: valid / invalid / inconclusive
  ↓ printability assessment (heuristic, never permission)
  ↓ File proposal → exact YES → controlled write (BIG #5)
mesh File (file_, sha256 identity)
  ↓ slice (test slicer or explicit unavailable)
G-code bytes (never production unless reviewed runtime made it)
  ↓ safety assessment (safe / unsafe / inconclusive)
  ↓ File proposal → exact YES → controlled write (BIG #5)
G-code File (file_, sha256 identity)
  ↓ print proposal (printer.execute — SECOND, explicit YES)
PHYSICAL APPROVAL (mission YES never starts the machine)
  ↓ revalidation (binding + fingerprint + G-code hash + safety)
execution (adapter only)
  ↓ telemetry result (telemetry only, never verification)
observation (BIG #6 camera) + two-half verification
  ↓ only both halves passed promotes
WORLD MODEL (INVENTory update via BIG #5)
```

Grenzen die nooit vermengen:

- **digital artifact ≠ physical artifact** — bytes zijn geen object.
- **validation ≠ human approval** — `valid` is een parse-oordeel.
- **assessment ≠ permission** — er bestaat nergens een
  `safe_to_execute`-veld; `safe` + `printable` autoriseren niets.
- **approval ≠ verification** — YES staat beweging toe; alleen
  readback bewijst resultaat.
- **printer telemetry ≠ physical verification** — "printer
  meldt voltooid" en "camera bevestigt object" zijn aparte
  verificatiehelften; beide moeten passen.
- **software cancel ≠ physical emergency stop** — cancel is een
  statustransitie; echte e-stop vereist hardware die deze laag
  niet aanraakt (contractgrens + `estop_note` op elke job).

## Generatie (`mesh3d.py`)

Naast de BIG #5-contracten in `pipeline3d.py` (onaangeroerd:
feasibility blijft advies, fysieke methoden blijven geweigerd).
`ThreeDProvider`-interface met exact twee implementaties:
`ProceduralTestGenerator` (deterministische 20mm-kubus als
ASCII STL, altijd test-gemarkeerd) en `UnavailableGenerator`
(expliciete reden). Geen netwerk, geen downloads, geen CAD-kernel.

## Validatie (`mesh3d.py`, stdlib-only)

ASCII/binaire STL en minimale OBJ: suffix-allow-list,
fabrication-dir-boundary, 20 MiB-cap, vertex/face-caps,
finite-float-checks (NaN/Inf weigert), non-empty geometrie.
Verdict `valid` / `invalid` (concreet defect) /
`inconclusive` (onparseerbaar — nooit `valid`).
`assess_printability` toetst bounds tegen build-volume
(default 220×220×250mm); output is planning-advies.

## Slicing (`slicer3d.py`)

`SlicerProvider`-interface; `TestSlicer` (deterministische
synthetische G-code met never-for-printers-header) en
`UnavailableSlicer` (met integratie-eisen voor een reviewed
lokale runtime: gepinde binary, vaste argv-allow-list,
bounded profiles). Profielen uit een gesloten set
(draft/fine-PLA, draft-PETG). Geen arbitraire slicer-
commando's — het executie-oppervlak bestaat niet.

## G-code safety (`slicer3d.py`)

Commando-allow-list per regel, temperatuurgrenzen (nozzle
≤ 300°C, bed ≤ 120°C), size/line-caps, geen includes, geen
traversal. Onbekende commando's → `inconclusive`; M112 en
andere verborgen intentie → `unsafe`. Unsafe G-code wordt
nooit een File-voorstel. Vingerafdruk (sha256) bindt het
artefact aan het voorstel; gewijzigde bytes na approval
blokkeren bij uitvoering.

## Printers (`printer3d.py`)

Mycelium-eigen device-tabel (`printer_devices`, id's `prt-*`)
met optionele `hw_`-link naar een INVENTory-hardware-twin
(wereldgeheugen vs. uitvoeringsautoriteit — gedocumenteerd,
niet gesynchroniseerd, geen dubbele device-database).
Gesloten capabilities (`printer.status/telemetry/upload/
start/pause/stop/cancel`), per adapter gefilterd. Alleen
`SimulatedPrinterAdapter` (deterministische in-memory state
machine, expliciet gesimuleerd) en `UnavailablePrinterAdapter`
bestaan. Geen serieel, geen netwerk, geen vendor-SDK.

## Uitvoering (`fab_flow.py`)

`propose_print` bouwt het inerte `printer.execute`-voorstel
(weiteit bij safety `unsafe`). `execute_print` eist alles:
binding, geen staleness, G-code-hash, safety ≠ unsafe,
allow-list-profile, adapter met `printer.start`. Resultaat is
telemetrie. `FabricationRecord` traceert elke stap
(source → mesh → validatie → file → slice → safety → file →
job → observatie) met history.

## Verificatie

`verify_print_telemetry` (job completed + hash) en
`verify_print_camera` (BIG #6-observatiecheck) — verified
alleen als beide passen (`print_verdict`). Bestaande
`/writes/{id}/verify` dekt de telemetriehelft;
`/writes/{id}/verify-print` combineert met camera.

## Missies, chat, graph, UI

Stap-soorten `fabricate`/`slice`/`physical_print` via
geïnjecteerde runners (zonder wiring BLOCKt de stap);
`physical_print` voltooit nooit geverifieerd vanzelf.
`POST /api/v1/fab/assess` beantwoordt "kunnen we dit
printen?" met advies + volgende stap — print nooit.
World-graph-overlay met gesloten predicaten (derived_from,
sliced_to, executed_as, produced, observed_by). Minimale
`/fabrication`-pagina in bestaande stijl (runs, printers,
validatie-, safety- en verificatiestaten).

## Retentie & files

Fabrication-dir, 20 MiB mesh-cap / 50 MiB G-code-cap,
laatste 5 artefacten, sha256-verplicht voor File-registratie
(`file_kind` mesh/gcode, `human_verified=False`). Alleen
referenties en metadata reizen verder — nooit bytes in
chat/context/databases.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/3d-model-libraries.md">
# 3D-modelbibliotheken — bronnen voor import

Stand: 2026-10-05. Praktijkgeverifieerd: Wikimedia Commons API is live
bevraagd (zoek + licentievelden); NIH 3D en NASA via portal/ToS.
Regel: **"open", "free" of "open source" betekent nooit automatisch
verkoopbaar/remixbaar** — alleen de daadwerkelijke licentievoorwaarden
per model tellen (`workshop3d.ModelLicense`, `license_terms()`).

Importketen: bibliotheekmap (operator downloadt) of expliciete
download-actie → `register_library_model()` / download-import →
`ModelLicense` + sha256 → `library_file_fields()` →
`propose_inventory_write()` → bestaande YES/write-gate (`/writes`) →
INVENTory `file_` + workshop `mdl_`. Geen tweede database, geen
tweede registry, geen nieuwe approval-flow.

## 1. Wikimedia Commons

- **API/download-methode**: open MediaWiki API, geen key, geen login.
  Zoeken: `GET https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php`
  `?action=query&format=json&list=search&srsearch=<trefwoord>`
  `&srnamespace=6&srlimit=<n>`.
  Details per bestand: `?action=query&format=json`
  `&titles=File:<naam>&prop=imageinfo`
  `&iiprop=url|size|extmetadata`
  `&iiextmetadatafilter=Artist|LicenseShortName|LicenseUrl|`
  `UsageTerms|AttributionRequired`.
  Download: `imageinfo[0].url` (host `upload.wikimedia.org`).
- **3D-formaten (voorbeeld)**: `.stl` volop aanwezig
  (bv. `File:Moon elevation.stl`, `File:Apollo 11 landing site 3D.stl`);
  `.obj`/`.3mf` incidenteel. `size` in bytes via API.
- **Licentie-informatie**: `LicenseShortName` (bv. `CC BY-SA 4.0`),
  `LicenseUrl`, `UsageTerms`, `Artist` (HTML), `AttributionRequired`
  (`true`/`false`). Let op: multi-licenties zijn onbetrouwbaar
  per API-docs — bij twijfel de bestandspagina lezen.
- **commercial_use**: per licentie. Voorbeeld Moon elevation.stl:
  CC BY-SA 4.0 → JA (met share-alike bij remix).
- **remix_allowed**: per licentie (BY-SA: JA mits share-alike;
  BY-NC-ND: NEE).
- **attribution_required**: per `AttributionRequired` (meestal JA).
- **Bron-URL**: `https://commons.wikimedia.org/`
- **Originele model-URL**: `imageinfo[0].descriptionurl`
  (bv. `https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Moon_elevation.stl`).
- **Beperkingen**: 26 MB-voorbeeld past niet onder de
  `MAX_MESH_BYTES`-cap (20 MB) → zulke bestanden weigeren met reden;
  `Artist` is HTML (alleen tonen, nooit uitvoeren); multi-licenties
  handmatig controleren.
- **Automatisering verantwoord?**: JA voor zoeken + metadata +
  download van `upload.wikimedia.org` (vaste host-allowlist, timeout
  ≤ 5 s, byte-cap, 3D-content-types). Alleen via expliciete
  operatoractie (POST); nooit op de achtergrond.

## 2. NIH 3D (3d.nih.gov)

- **API/download-methode**: portal, geen stabiele publieke JSON-API
  zonder account. Zoeken + download handmatig via
  `https://3d.nih.gov/discover`; operator plakt model-URL en
  licentie in het importvoorstel.
- **3D-formaten (voorbeeld)**: `.stl`, `.glb`, `.x3d`, `.wrl`
  (meeste modellen downloadbaar in meerdere formaten).
- **Licentie-informatie**: per entry op de modelpagina; varieert
  (public domain, CC-BY, maar ook restrictievere voorwaarden).
  ToS: bezoeker moet de licentie per bestand lezen en naleven;
  NIH handhaaft niet namens uploaders.
- **commercial_use**: ONBEKEND tot de entry gelezen is — nooit
  aannemen (ook niet bij "open repository").
- **remix_allowed**: idem ONBEKEND tot gelezen.
- **attribution_required**: idem (CC-BY-entries: JA).
- **Bron-URL**: `https://3d.nih.gov/`
- **Originele model-URL**: de modelpagina op `3d.nih.gov` (operator
  plakt hem; hij wordt als `original_model_url` vastgelegd).
- **Beperkingen**: geen machineleesbare licentie-API; account nodig
  voor uploaden/geavanceerd (niet nodig voor downloaden).
- **Automatisering verantwoord?**: NEE voor zoeken/metadata
  (geen stabiele publieke API). Download van `3d.nih.gov` is
  technisch mogelijk met dezelfde hardening, maar zonder
  machineleesbare licentie blijft de operator verantwoordelijk
  voor het overnemen van de voorwaarden → voorlopig handmatig.

## 3. NASA 3D Resources

- **API/download-methode**: geen API; directe downloads via
  `https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/` (bv. Moon near/far side
  `.stl`) en GitHub-mirror `nasa/NASA-3D-Resources` (`.glb`,
  `.usdz`, textures). Operator downloadt, importeert via map of
  expliciete download-actie.
- **3D-formaten (voorbeeld)**: `.stl` (printbaar), `.glb`,
  `.usdz`, textures/images.
- **Licentie-informatie**: "free and without copyright"
  (US-overheidswerk); lees de Usage Guidelines op de site.
- **commercial_use**: JA (zonder copyright; guidelines blijven
  van toepassing).
- **remix_allowed**: JA.
- **attribution_required**: NEE (naamsvermelding gewaardeerd,
  niet wettelijk vereist).
- **Bron-URL**: `https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/`
- **Originele model-URL**: de modelpagina op science.nasa.gov
  (operator plakt hem).
- **Beperkingen**: geen API, geen per-model licentieveld
  (uniform beleid i.p.v. per-model metadata); GitHub-mirror is
  handig maar geen canonieke bron.
- **Automatisering verantwoord?**: DEELS — download van
  `science.nasa.gov` met dezelfde hardening is verantwoord;
  licentie blijft uniform beleid (`NASA` in `license_terms()`).
  GitHub-raw-hosts worden NIET automatisch toegelaten
  (allowlist blijft klein); mirror via handmatige download.

## Veldmapping (alle bronnen → ModelLicense)

| Veld | Commons | NIH 3D | NASA |
|---|---|---|---|
| source_library | `wikimedia-commons` | `nih-3d` | `nasa-3d` |
| source_url | API-aanvraag-URL of `commons.wikimedia.org` | modelpagina (operator) | modelpagina (operator) |
| author | `Artist` (tekst, HTML strippen) | entry-auteur (operator) | `NASA` |
| license | `LicenseShortName` | entry-licentie (operator) | `NASA` / `public domain` |
| commercial_use | via `license_terms()` | via `license_terms()` of ONBEKEND | JA |
| remix_allowed | via `license_terms()` | via `license_terms()` of ONBEKEND | JA |
| attribution_required | `AttributionRequired` + `license_terms()` | per entry | NEE |
| original_model_url | `descriptionurl` | modelpagina | modelpagina |
| imported_at | importtijdstip (server) | idem | idem |
| provenance | `file_`-metadata + description (executie-provenance via writes-flow) | idem | idem |
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/3d-workshop.md">
# 3D Workshop Ecosystem (BIG #35)

The 3D system is no longer an isolated page. Models are
living citizens of the workshop:

    MODEL ↔ OBJECT ↔ MATERIAL ↔ PROJECT ↔ IDEA ↔ MACHINE ↔
    FABRICATION ↔ OBSERVATION ↔ VERIFICATION ↔ KNOWLEDGE ↔
    SYMBIOSIS ↔ CRAFT TREE

A model is not a file. It can be part of a project, derived
from an idea, made from materials, produced by a machine, a
replacement part, a prototype, evidence — all through the
existing world model. No second 3D universe was built.

## Model lifecycle (all states explicit)

DISCOVER → IMPORT → INSPECT → UNDERSTAND → CONNECT →
MODIFY → PREPARE → SLICE → FABRICATE → OBSERVE → VERIFY →
LEARN → UPDATE WORLD.

- **Import** (`POST /api/v1/workshop/models`): the operator
  copies STL/OBJ/3MF/GLB/GLTF into the fabrication dir (like
  the camera inbox); registration records `mdl_…` id,
  filename, MIME, size, sha256, provenance, timestamp,
  source. Same bytes never register twice (replay refused).
  Traversal, unsupported formats, oversize and missing files
  refuse. Model bytes are parsed as data, never executed.
- **Inspect** (`POST .../inspect`): STL/OBJ get a geometric
  scan (triangles, vertices, bounding box) plus the existing
  mesh-validator verdict. Manifold, units and volume stay
  UNKNOWN unless actually determined — never invented.
  3MF/GLB/GLTF register metadata-only (inspection UNKNOWN).
- **Connect**: links are connection candidates (PROPOSED
  symbiosis) with a closed predicate set (`represents`,
  `requires`, `used_in`, `generated_from`, `fabricated_by`,
  `replacement_for`, `compatible_with`, `verified_by`,
  `part_of`, `related_to`). YES/NO/REVIEW via knowledge.
- **Modify**: existing procedural/test transform + preview
  flows (`/workshop/3d`, fab endpoints) — untouched.
- **Prepare/Slice**: fab-job `prepare` (mesh must be valid +
  printability assessment) and `slice` (TEST slicer labeled,
  anything else UNAVAILABLE → blocked with reason).
- **Fabricate**: print proposals go through the existing
  writes flow (`printer.execute`, exact YES). Fab-job stages
  DERIVE from the stored write record and PrintResult —
  the workshop never approves or executes. Simulated
  execution reports SIMULATED telemetry, never REAL.
- **Observe/Verify**: attach a real camera observation,
  then verify with both halves (execution telemetry +
  observation readback) and a named human verifier.
- **Learn/Update**: candidates, symbiosis, craft gaps, guide
  items and morning carry results back into the world.

## Materials (known / candidate / unknown)

`POST /api/v1/workshop/materials`: name, kind (closed set),
state, notes, linked entity. Suggestions (`.../suggest`)
rank known stock first — suggestions, never assignments.
Sustainability text is an operator note, never a verified
claim: no green claims by name.

## Fabrication honesty

REAL: preparation metadata, validation, TEST slicing,
workflow state, relationships, provenance. SIMULATED:
printer execution where explicitly marked (simulated
adapter only). UNAVAILABLE: real printer transport. A
SIMULATED print never becomes REAL. Software cancel is a
state transition (and refused once plastic exists); it is
never an e-stop.

## Camera verification (BIG #34 integration)

`observe` needs a stored camera observation;
`verify` needs completed telemetry + passed camera readback
+ a named human. Observation confirms the object; identity
becomes human-confirmed only through YES.

## Craft, guide, mobile, notifications, nodes, packets

- `/craft` picks models up through graph overlays;
  `GET /api/v1/workshop/presence` gives a per-entity
  checklist (✓ present / ? missing) with actionable gaps.
- Guide gains workshop items (bare model, awaiting
  verification, blocked job, reusable model).
- Mobile gains a Workbench panel (input only; YES gates
  intact). WEB_PUSH stays UNAVAILABLE.
- Notifications reuse `fabrication_ready`,
  `candidate_waiting`, `new_connection`, `camera_ready`.
- `/3d` shows mesh-capable nodes (read-only); delegation
  uses the existing mesh validate + task claims.
- `GET /api/v1/workshop/packet` emits a continuation
  section (model, stage, material, facts, blockers, next
  actions, provenance, approvals — no secrets) another AI
  can continue from.

## Progress + living background

`stage_progress()` renders real bars (`[██████░░░░] 60%`)
with ✓/○/■ checklists from backend states — no XP, no
levels. The spore canvas now scales density (8–48) with
24h ecosystem activity and tints amber while approvals
wait; ambient only, reduced-motion safe, never implying
events that did not happen.
</file>

# Advanced Workshop (BIG #11-15, Phase 4) — IMPLEMENTED

On top of the BIG #7/#10 pipeline: scene-level
interaction over objects, meshes, printers and tools
with select/inspect/group semantics in the UI, and
safe geometry ops behind preview-first endpoints.

## Mesh ops (pure, bounded, no code execution)

mirror, merge, translate/rotate/scale (existing),
extend (dimension ±, guarded against inversion),
orient (flattest side down, deterministic), volume
estimate, repair proposal (data only — the source
file is untouched).

## Prompt editing

"maak deze bracket 5mm langer" parses through closed
patterns to an explicit op (or refuses on ambiguity):
selected object → parsed intent → geometry proposal →
preview → before/after → derived artifact + hash +
provenance → human approval → persist. Persisting
always needs a named approver.

## Fabrication pipeline

IDEA → CAD → MESH → VALIDATION → SLICING → G-code →
PRINTER → PRINT → CAMERA → TELEMETRY → VERIFICATION
→ INVENTory, planned by `plan_pipeline` as data.
Preparation is actionable; the physical start stays
behind the existing proposal + exact-YES gates, and
verification still needs telemetry AND camera.
Filament spools are local resource records with
estimate-vs-remaining checks (estimates labelled,
never sensor-certain).

# Agenda import (local-first)

No Google Calendar required. Paste `.ics` text at `/agenda`,
preview it, confirm it. Events become read-only world/context
data with source provenance — never commitment facts.

## Flow

```
AGENDA → plak .ics → Preview → Bevestig import → events
```

- `POST /api/v1/agenda/import {"preview_only": true}` parses
  and returns up to 50 events without storing anything.
- `preview_only: false` stores with UID dedup: re-importing
  the same label reuses the source row; same-UID events
  update instead of duplicating.
- `GET /api/v1/agenda/events` / `/sources` — read-only lists.
- `GET /api/v1/agenda/events?upcoming_only=true` feeds the
  morning report and the “agenda” command.

## Parser

Stdlib-only, bounded (500k chars, 500 events): unfolding,
VEVENT blocks, SUMMARY / DTSTART / DTEND / LOCATION /
DESCRIPTION / UID / RRULE. Missing UIDs get a deterministic
`derived-` id labelled as derived. Malformed input refuses
instead of guessing; nothing is ever invented.

URL-based ICS feeds are intentionally NOT fetched by the
coordinator (no arbitrary network destinations). Paste or
upload the text instead; later n8n transport can poll an
explicitly configured feed.

## Project ↔ agenda ↔ mission

Agenda rows may be shown as context next to projects and
missions (e.g. an “UMZ wedstrijd” event beside the OZFK
project). Links are explicit and provenance-carrying; personal
commitments are never inferred as facts.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/architecture.md">
# Architectuur v0.1

Een Mycelium-installatie heeft één lokale coördinator en nul of meer nodes. De coördinator bewaart alleen node-metadata en taakstatus in SQLite. Elke node maakt zelf een uitgaande HTTP-verbinding, registreert zich en haalt vervolgens werk op. Dit werkt op een gewoon thuisnetwerk en blijft bruikbaar wanneer internet wegvalt.

## Datastroom

`node → registratie/heartbeat → coordinator → wachtrij → node claimt taak → resultaat`

Een taak bevat een type, JSON-payload en optionele capabilities. De node moet alle gevraagde capabilities hebben; een voorkeurs-tier is eveneens mogelijk. In deze versie is energie-informatie alleen metadata. Automatische energieplanning wordt pas toegevoegd wanneer we echte, uitlegbare metingen en een handmatige override hebben.

## Veiligheidsgrens

De server stuurt nooit uitvoerbare code. De meegeleverde node kent uitsluitend een allow-list met één niet-invasieve taak: `system_inventory`. Toekomstige executors moeten per taaksoort expliciet worden geïnstalleerd, met een beperkte map- en netwerktoegang. Dit voorkomt dat een taakqueue ongemerkt verandert in remote code execution.

## Toestemming en zichtbaarheid

De client meet CPU-cores en werkgeheugen op het eigen apparaat, maar verzint geen capabilities. Een eigenaar geeft bijvoorbeeld `--capability ocr` alleen op wanneer die node die concrete, gewenste executor heeft. Energiebron is eveneens een expliciete keuze. Deze scheiding voorkomt dat automatische inventarisatie verandert in stille controle of onverwachte taakuitvoering.

## Volgende kleine stappen

1. Voeg een optionele executor toe voor één veilige taak, bijvoorbeeld lokale systeeminventarisatie.
2. Toon node-status en wachtrij via een eenvoudige browserinterface.
3. Voeg API-tokens toe voordat nodes buiten het vertrouwde LAN verbinden.
4. Meet energie lokaal en laat mensen een energiebudget instellen voordat automatisch plannen wordt ingevoerd.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/automation-security.md">
# Automation Security (BIG #38)

Threat model, mitigations, and security invariants for the
living automation engine.

## Threat Model

Automation runs untrusted step definitions (from templates or
web forms) and drives them through existing functions. The
attacker controls:

- Step kinds and params (via `POST /api/v1/automation/runs` or
  `POST /web/automation/from-template`)
- Template arguments (goal, conversation_id)
- Conversation content (imported chats)
- Research questions and objectives

The attacker **cannot**:
- Execute arbitrary code (no shell, no eval, no exec)
- Bypass human gates (gates re-read live stores)
- Fabricate approvals (resume re-checks every time)
- Access secrets (redacted at import, never in payloads)
- Write to INVENTory without exact YES
- Spawn background threads
- Escalate capabilities beyond nodemesh allow-list

## Defense in Depth

### 1. Closed Step-Kind Allow-List (Creation + Drive)

```python
SAFE_STEP_KINDS = frozenset({
    "observe", "readout", "search", "research_queue",
    "research_execute", "conversation_analyze", "intel_analyze",
    "knowledge_candidate", "symbiosis_propose", "craft_update",
    "context_packet", "notify", "mission_tick", "mission_propose",
    "write_propose", "fab_prepare", "node_prepare",
    "camera_session", "wait",
})
```

Any other kind → `AutomationRefusedError` at creation AND at
drive time. Default-deny.

### 2. Overnight Subset

```python
OVERNIGHT_SAFE_KINDS = frozenset({
    "observe", "readout", "search", "research_queue",
    "research_execute", "conversation_analyze", "intel_analyze",
    "knowledge_candidate", "symbiosis_propose", "craft_update",
    "context_packet", "notify", "wait",
})
```

Overnight runs refuse mission ticks, proposals, fabrication,
camera, node prep.

### 3. Param Validation (Creation Time)

- Depth-limited recursive cleaning (≤3, covers mission steps)
- Text/number/bool/short list (≤10)/shallow object (≤12 keys)
- String values truncated to 2000 chars
- Step params limited to 12 keys
- Run steps limited to 20

### 4. Kind-Specific Static Checks

| Kind | Checks |
|------|--------|
| `node_prepare` | task_kind in allow-list, capability prefixed, no wildcard |
| `craft_update` | entity_id validates via `clean_entity` |
| `symbiosis_propose` | predicate in closed set, two valid entities |
| `mission_tick` | mission_id format or empty (resolves from draft) |
| `mission_propose` | goal required, steps read-only kinds only |
| `write_propose` | mutation_type in allow-list, target required, payload ≤12 keys, secret scan |
| `knowledge_candidate` | kind in allow-list, title+text required, health regex blocks |
| `camera_session` | op in {run, describe, propose} |
| `fab_prepare` | op in {prepare, slice, propose}, job_id required |
| `research_queue` | question required, priority in {HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW} |
| `research_execute` | run_id format `res_*` |
| `observe`/`readout` | source in allow-list |

### 5. Gate Validation (Creation + Live Re-Check)

```python
GATE_TYPES = frozenset({
    "mission_approved", "write_approved", "desktop_decided",
    "candidate_advanced", "research_completed", "time_elapsed",
})
```

Gate ref required (except `time_elapsed`). `write_approved`
carries fingerprint for extra integrity.

### 6. Live Gate Re-Check (Resume)

`check_gate_live()` re-reads the authoritative store:

- `mission_approved` → loads mission, checks status + approver
- `write_approved` → loads proposal, checks status + human decider
- `desktop_decided` → loads desktop action, checks status + decider
- `candidate_advanced` → loads candidate, checks state
- `research_completed` → loads run, checks dossier/status
- `time_elapsed` → wall clock compare

Missing records → unmet. Exceptions → unmet (fail-safe).

### 7. Secret Redaction

- Import: credential-like text redacted in conversation bridge
- Payloads: `_SECRET_HINTS` scan (token, secret, password,
  api_key, bearer, credential, private_key, client_secret)
- Packets: reuse existing redaction in `context_packet.py`
- Nodemesh: capability hints only, no secrets in task payloads

### 8. Health Isolation

`knowledge_candidate` and `symbiosis_propose` both run
through `candidate_from_finding` path which applies the
health regex (`_HEALTH_RE`) — health-related text **never**
becomes a candidate, even if automation tries.

### 9. No Shell / RCE Surface

Static analysis asserts no:
- `subprocess`, `os.system`, `os.popen`
- `eval(`, `exec(`, `__import__`
- `socket`, `urllib`

All execution goes through existing, audited functions.

### 10. Capability Escalation Refused

`node_prepare` validates:
- `task_kind` ∈ `ALLOWED_TASK_KINDS`
- `capability` starts with `ALLOWED_CAPABILITY_PREFIXES`
- No `*`, no oversized strings

### 11. Path Traversal Refused

`craft_update` and `symbiosis_propose` entity IDs validated
through `clean_entity()` which rejects `..`, `/`, `\`,
control chars.

### 12. Prompt Injection Containment

Injected text in conversation imports:
- Stored as-is (escaped on render)
- Analyzed by deterministic extractive engine (no LLM)
- Can become candidate text (labeled `ai-generated`,
  `human_verified=False`)
- **Cannot** approve, execute, verify, or change truth
- Test: `test_injection_never_executes` verifies

### 13. Provenance Discipline

Every automation-created record carries:
```python
Provenance(
    source_type="ai-generated",
    creator_id=f"automation:{run_id}",
    human_verified=False,
    notes="automation proposal; support/promote stay human"
)
```

Health content forces `human_verified=False` even if
someone tries to hand-set it.

## Invariants (Tested)

- `test_create_rejects_garbage`: closed kinds, bounds, gates,
  secrets, overnight, templates
- `test_health_never_becomes_candidate`: health regex blocks
- `test_stale_approval_never_wakes`: resume re-reads live
- `test_mission_tick_refuses_unapproved`: tick only in approved
- `test_write_prepare_then_human_yes_then_resume`: proposal →
  exact YES → resume
- `test_bounds_stop_runs`: max_steps, max_consecutive_failures
- `test_capability_escalation_refused`: wildcard, bad task_kind,
  path traversal, bad predicate
- `test_no_shell_surface_and_states_honest`: static scan +
  gate honesty
- `test_injection_never_executes`: hostile content contained

## What Jelles Approves

Every consequential step waits with an explicit gate:
- Mission approval → `/api/v1/missions/{id}/approve` (exact YES)
- Write approval → `/api/v1/writes/{id}/approve` (exact YES)
- Desktop action → `/api/v1/desktop/{id}/approve` (exact YES)
- Candidate support/promote → `/api/v1/candidates/{id}/support`
- Research completion → automatic (dossier exists)

Automation **never** writes an approval, never decides for
the human, never reuses a stale decision.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/autonomous-mission-loop.md">
# Autonomous Mission Loop (BIG #21) — IMPLEMENTED

One safe continuous runner over the existing executor:
chat intent → mission → tick → observe → evaluate →
continue → verify → complete. The loop adds no
execution power: it calls `executor.tick()`, reads the
gates, and stops at every one of them.

## What runs automatically from chat

1. Chat interprets the opdracht (existing advisor flow)
   and creates a mission (existing `POST /chat/{id}/
   missions` or `/missions`).
2. `POST /missions/{id}/run` (or the mission page's
   *Run loop* button) drives the approved plan:
   - readout steps (git/project/INVENTory) complete
     on their own, results recorded, observations
     linked;
   - analysis steps run through the advisor;
   - screenshot/wait desktop steps auto-dispatch and
     complete when the desktop agent claims, acts and
     reports through its existing loop;
   - camera_observe steps complete with observation
     references (metadata only, never auto-written).
3. Each terminal mission stores one episodic memory
   (observed truth, sensor-observed provenance, never
   a fact tier, never verified) and the run report
   names rounds, transitions and the memory id.

## Where Mycelium stops for Jelles

- **Plan approval**: `pending_approval` missions never
  tick (`needs_plan_approval`).
- **Desktop input**: any step with `requires_approval`
  stops with `needs_desktop_approval` + action_id; only
  an exact YES through `/desktop/actions/{id}/decision`
  unblocks it. Dispatched actions stop with
  `waiting_agent` until the agent reports.
- **Proposals**: drafted as data, completed as steps;
  the separate `/approvals` flow stays human.
- **Writes**: own exact YES + fingerprint revalidation.
- **Physical/fabrication**: own physical approval; a
  mission YES never starts a machine (verified: the
  loop stops, nothing executes).
- **Failure/block/pause/conflict**: halt, human
  reviews; never blind retry, never invented steps.
- Continuation ("herplan → vervolg") happens across
  runs: human/agent/observation changes state, the
  next run ticks further inside the approved plan.
  Replanning beyond approved steps needs a new
  approval. Rounds per call are capped at 10;
  concurrent runs lose the existing conditional race.

## Mock / test / unavailable inventory

- Lokaal uitvoerbaar: readout, analysis (met model),
  screenshot/wait steps, camera_observe (metadata),
  proposal-drafts, write/fabricate/slice/print *alleen*
  met hun eigen approvals + runners.
- Test: TestCameraAdapter, SimulatedPrinterAdapter,
  test-slicer — altijd gelabeld, nooit echt.
- Unavailable: echte printertransporten, echte
  drone/robot-hardware, live externe integraties.
  Fysieke executie blijft HARDWARE_REQUIRED.

## Contract

`POST /api/v1/missions/{id}/run {"max_rounds": 1..10}`
→ `{mission_id, status, outcome, stop_reason?, detail?,
action?, rounds, tick?, memory_id?}`. Unknown missions
422; never shell, network, or SQL surface in the
loop module itself.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/autonomous-missions.md">
# Autonomous missions (BIG #21 → #24 → #25)

## The loop

```
plan → execute → observe → evaluate → DECIDE → continue
```

`mission_loop.run_loop()` drives one mission until a gate, a
terminal state, or the round budget (max 10 per call). It adds
no execution power: it calls `executor.tick()`, reads the
gates, and stops at every one of them.

## Decisions (BIG #24, `decisions.py`)

After each observation the current step evaluates to one
explicit state:

| Decision | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CONTINUE | Step succeeded (or pending + read-only) — evaluate next |
| RETRY | Read-only step failed, attempts left — bounded backoff |
| REPLAN | Retries exhausted — revised plan needs a new human YES |
| WAITING_FOR_HUMAN | Exact gate named (desktop YES, write YES, physical YES…) |
| WAITING_FOR_AGENT | Dispatched action is out — agent report unblocks |
| BLOCKED | Cannot proceed safely — human reviews |
| FAILED / COMPLETED / CANCELLED | Mirrors terminal executor state only |

`decide()` is a pure function: it never mutates, never
approves, and the LLM never decides — provider advice is
evidence at most. A failed step never fails the whole mission
by itself; `POST /api/v1/missions/{id}/decide` exposes the
evaluation read-only.

## Recovery (BIG #25, `recovery.py`, `recovery.md`)

Missions persist in SQLite, so they survive restarts. Recovery
makes resuming safe and explicit — see `recovery.md`.
</file>

# BIG #34 — Camera Ecosystem: final report

## 1. Wat gebouwd is

`coordinator/app/camera_ecosystem.py` (new, ~700 lines) plus
wiring in `main.py` (9 API + 5 web routes), `guide.py`
(camera items), `symbiosis.py` (camera ID prefixes),
camera detail + Camera Lab + mobile UI:

- **Multi-file ingest sessions**: `POST
  /api/v1/camera-sessions` + `.../{id}/run`, `cing_…` ids,
  ≤8 files, per-file states
  (queued/observed/duplicate/refused), sha256 dedupe across
  sessions, additive `camera_ingest_sessions` table.
- **VLM layer**: `POST /api/v1/observations/{id}/describe`
  — REAL Ollama analysis when the loopback backend answers,
  extractive fallback (`vlm_state: UNAVAILABLE`, empty
  labels, `model: ""`) otherwise. Stored distinguishably.
- **Candidates**: `POST
  /api/v1/observations/{id}/propose-candidates` — one
  idempotent candidate per REAL label; fallback yields none;
  no auto-promotion.
- **Matching + links**: `GET /api/v1/camera-match`
  (POSSIBLE MATCH evidence, bounded browse) and `POST
  /api/v1/camera-suggest-link` (closed predicates) → connection
  candidate → PROPOSED symbiosis; YES/NO/REVIEW via knowledge.
- **Timeline**: `GET /api/v1/camera-timeline` from the shared
  bus + notifications (no second event system).
- **UI**: Camera Lab (`/cameras` + 8-step Insta360 guide),
  detail page (session form, session list, per-observation
  Describe/Propose/Review buttons, suggest-link form,
  timeline), mobile camera flow panel.
- Tests: `tests/test_big34_camera_ecosystem.py` (13).
- Scripts: `scripts/b34_smoke.py` (full-chain smoke).
- Screenshots: `docs/r34-shots/` (4 PNGs).

## 2. Wat hergebruikt is

cameras.py (devices, observations, retention), vision_ingest
(FileIngestAdapter, media_facts, inbox, availability),
vision_provider (Ollama loopback, VisionUnavailable),
vision_flow (analysis store, inert proposals, verification),
knowledge (candidates, support/promote/reject, fencing),
symbiosis PROPOSED, craft overlays, guide, worldgraph,
events (`observation.created`, `candidate.observed`,
`relation.proposed` — no new types), notify_center IN_APP
types, mobile, morning/activity. No gate removed, no
provenance relaxed, no INVENTory change.

## 3. Camera flow

FILE → SESSION (`cing_…`) → OBSERVATION (`obs-…`) → VLM
REAL / fallback → CANDIDATE (`cand_…`, per label,
idempotent) → POSSIBLE MATCH → LINK PROPOSAL (YES) →
SYMBIOSIS → CRAFT → GUIDE → MEMORY (if allowed) →
MORNING / ACTIVITY / WORLD. Verified end-to-end by smoke.

## 4. Insta360 status

REAL: registratie, file ingest, metadata, sessions,
analyse van aangeleverde bestanden. UNAVAILABLE: directe
live transport, camera-control, proprietary protocol —
verified adapter vereist. REGISTERED ≠ CONNECTED, nooit
fake LIVE. Camera Guide op `/cameras` toont het 8-stappen
file-pad.

## 5. VLM status

REAL wanneer Ollama-loopback antwoordt (gestructureerde
labels + confidences + description + uncertainty, stored).
UNAVAILABLE fallback wanneer niet (geen labels, geen
confidences, expliciete uncertainty). Smoke bewees beide
(fallback live; REAL via MockTransport-test). VLM-output is
OBSERVATION, nooit FACT.

## 6. Candidates

Eén per REAL label, evidence aan observatie gebonden,
sensor/ai-provenance, `observation`-type, state
`observation`. Idempotent per (observation, label).
Mens beslist via support/promote/reject.

## 7. Symbiosis

Link-voorstellen zijn `connection`-candidates met

## 1. Status

## 3. Files changed

Extended:
- `coordinator/app/events.py` — additive `automation.*` bus types
- `coordinator/app/main.py` — automation API + web routes,
  `/automation` pages, mission-detail link, morning section,
  packet section
- `coordinator/app/living_state.py` — automation counts
- `coordinator/app/guide.py` — waiting/blocked/failed items
- `coordinator/app/mobile.py` — automation quests in progress
- `coordinator/app/ui.py` — subtle symbiosis/craft automation
  styling (reduced-motion safe)
- `coordinator/app/reports.py` — automation morning section
- `coordinator/app/context_packet.py` — automation sections
- `docs/NEXT-AI-CONTEXT.md`
- `docs/ROADMAP-V2.md`
- `README.md` (touch-up)

## 4. Living Automation Engine

`automation.py` implements the observe → research → propose →
wait-for-YES → act-inside-approved-plan → observe → verify →
record loop. Mycelium keeps going where work is already safe
and approved, and stops exactly where human authority begins.

**No new execution power** — steps execute only through
existing functions (research engine, knowledge, missions
executor, camera, workshop, conversation intel, packets,
notify).

**No background threads** — `drive` and `resume` are explicit
calls from API buttons only.

**Default-deny step kinds** — closed allow-list; anything else
refuses at creation AND at drive time.

**Consequential work waits** — preparation steps create inert
drafts/proposals and then the run WAITS with the exact gate
named. Resume re-reads live store state — approvals are never
fabricated, inferred, or reused stale.

**Bounds on every run** — steps, runtime, retries, consecutive
failures. Fail-closed with exact reasons.

## 5. Step Kinds (Closed Allow-List)

| Category | Kinds |
|----------|-------|
| Read-only (also overnight) | `observe`, `readout`, `search`, `research_queue`, `research_execute`, `conversation_analyze`, `intel_analyze`, `knowledge_candidate`, `symbiosis_propose`, `craft_update`, `context_packet`, `notify`, `wait` |
| Preparation (inert drafts → wait) | `mission_propose`, `write_propose`, `fab_prepare`, `node_prepare`, `camera_session` |
| Execution (inside approved only) | `mission_tick` |

## 6. Gates (Closed Set)

`mission_approved`, `write_approved`, `desktop_decided`,
`candidate_advanced`, `research_completed`, `time_elapsed`.

Resume re-checks live store every time — no cached verdicts.

## 7. Run Lifecycle

```
create_run(goal, steps[], bounds?, overnight?, mission_id?, template_id?)
    → run_id, state="running"
drive_run(run_id, budget_steps=10)
    → executes until gate/bound/completion
    → state: running | waiting_for_human | waiting_for_agent | blocked | failed | completed
resume_run(run_id, budget_steps=10)
    → re-checks ALL gates live, continues if met
cancel_run(run_id, reason)
    → terminal "cancelled"
```

## 8. Bounds (Validated at Creation)

| Bound | Default | Max |
|-------|---------|-----|
| max_steps | 10 | 20 |
| max_runtime_seconds | 600 | 3600 |
| max_retries | 2 | 5 |
| max_consecutive_failures | 3 | 5 |

## 9. Overnight Eligibility

Runs marked `overnight: true` must contain ONLY overnight-safe
kinds (read-only research/analysis/candidate/proposal/notify/
wait). Checked at creation and via `/overnight` endpoint.
Night shift observes and prepares; never advances executable
state. No self-start at night — explicit arming only.

## 10. Templates

Three built-in templates (API + web form):

1. `intel_to_research` (4 steps, overnight-safe):
   `intel_analyze` → `research_queue` → `knowledge_candidate` → `notify`
2. `observation_to_symbiosis` (4 steps, overnight-safe):
   `observe` candidates → `symbiosis_propose` → `craft_update` → `notify`
3. `missed_to_mission` (3 steps, NOT overnight):
   `intel_analyze` → `mission_propose` → `wait` (mission_approved)

## 11. API Surface

```
GET  /api/v1/automation/templates
POST /api/v1/automation/from-template
POST /api/v1/automation/runs
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/overnight
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/drive
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/resume
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/cancel
```

Web:
- `GET /automation` — overview + start from template
- `GET /automation/{run_id}` — quest trail, waiting bundle, drive/resume/cancel buttons

## 12. Surfaces

| Surface | Automation Integration |
|---------|------------------------|
| Guide (`/guide`, `/api/v1/guide`) | Waiting/blocked/failed items with WHAT/WHY/NEXT |
| Mobile (`/mobile`, `/api/v1/mobile/dashboard`) | Quests in progress panel |
| Morning report (`/api/v1/reports/morning`) | Automation section with runs, states, gates |
| Context packet (`/api/v1/context/packet`, `packet2`, `.md`) | Automation section with run_id, goal, state, waiting gate |
| Living state (`/api/v1/state`) | `automation_waiting`, `automation_running` counts |
| Notifications | Reuses `mission_waiting`, `research_finding`, `task_completed` |

## 13. Decision Vocabulary

From `decisions.py`: `CONTINUE`, `RETRY`, `REPLAN`,
`WAITING_FOR_HUMAN`, `WAITING_FOR_AGENT`, `BLOCKED`,
`FAILED`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`. Bus events use
`automation.*` types.

## 14. Security

See `docs/automation-security.md`. Key invariants:

- Closed step-kind allow-list (creation + drive)
- Gate re-checks live store on resume
- No approval fabrication
- Secret scan on write_propose payloads

- Path traversal refused (entity_id validation)

- Provenance: `ai-generated`, `human_verified=False`

## 4. Hardware Reality Layer

Nodes report what they really are; the coordinator validates,
stores, routes, guides, and shows — never executes, never
invents. Full contract in `docs/hardware-reality-layer.md`.

**Health** is derived live, never stored:
`disabled → OFFLINE`; `offline → OFFLINE`; `stale → STALE`;
online/busy with telemetry older than 5 min → DEGRADED;
otherwise ONLINE.

**Two wiring gaps found and fixed while testing** (both
fail-closed, both covered by new tests):
1. `_routing_candidates` never projected hardware/compute/
   telemetry-age/health into routing input, so every
   telemetry-aware requirement missed honestly but always.
   Now projected (validated store data, never credentials).
2. `_graph_data` never passed `include_hardware` /
   `include_compute` to the world builder despite the builder
   supporting them. Now wired to `show=…,hardware,compute`.

**Mobile nodes HTML** now renders the telemetry the JSON
panel already carried (health + cpu/mem + uptime + hardware
kinds + compute capabilities + energy per node).

## 5. API Surface

```
POST /api/v1/nodes/{node_id}/heartbeat   (extended: telemetry,
    hardware, compute_capabilities, energy_state)
GET  /api/v1/nodes  /  /api/v1/nodes/{node_id}
    (extended: telemetry, telemetry_timestamp, hardware,
     compute_capabilities, energy_state, health_status)
POST /api/v1/tasks/route  (extended: required_hardware,
    required_compute, max_telemetry_age_seconds, min_health)
GET  /world?show=missions,nodes,hardware,compute
```

Web: `/nodes` (cards + capability check + mesh),
`/mobile` (nodes panel with hardware detail), `/guide`
(hardware-aware items), `/world` (hardware/compute layers).

## 6. Security

- Unknown telemetry fields / hardware kinds / compute
  capabilities / energy sources → 422, nothing stored.
  Partial heartbeats keep prior good values (COALESCE);
  never partial-bad writes.
- Credential gates untouched: bad tokens 403, unknown nodes
  404, disabled refused, legacy freeze preserved. Wildcard
  and shell-shaped capabilities still refused (tripwires
  green, smoked).
- No new execution surface: telemetry is read-only state;
  no shell/RCE surface (static assert in tests); node
  subprocess calls bounded (3–5 s timeouts, truncated
  output, degrade-to-empty).
- Node-reported data never enters INVENTory, never becomes
  memory/candidate truth, never approves anything. World
  overlays carry `node-reported` + `human_verified=False`.
- Health is freshness-based, not diagnostic; hardware claims
  are advertisements (like capabilities), not attestations —
  documented, not hidden.

## 11. Limitations

- Health is freshness-based, not diagnostic.
- Hardware/compute are self-reported advertisements, not
  attestations; a lying node can claim a GPU.
- State is only as fresh as the last heartbeat (pull-only;
  coordinator never polls).
- Heartbeat emits no per-beat bus events (no spam); the four
  additive `node.*` bus types exist for consumers. Surfaces
  read live store state.
- World-graph hardware/compute overlay nodes covered by
  builder tests; the `/world` screenshot shows the layer UI
  with an honestly empty graph (no live INVENTory entity in
  the shot DB).

## 4. Implementation

Presence answers three questions over live stores: what
deserves attention, why (scored reasons), and what Jelles can
do (existing routes only). Full contract in
`docs/presence-ecosystem.md`.

Twelve collectors read approvals (desktop/write/mission),
missions (blocked/failed/paused), nodes (offline/stale/
degraded/hardware/compute), automation (human/agent/failed),
fabrication + 3D jobs, research dossiers + node-aware
readiness, candidates, contradictions + discoveries, camera
inbox, symbiosis, craft gaps, and 24h task/mission failures
from the bus. Each collector is best-effort and never raises.

Two fixes found while testing (both covered by new tests):
1. Candidate states are `observation/candidate/supported`
   (not `observed/proposed`) — collector filter corrected.
2. The notifications store carries the severity bucket in
   `type`, not the kind — fan-out dedup matches on
   (severity, title) via the new public `severity_for`.

## 7. Remote mesh

Pinned delegation with exact-capability checks, requester
authentication (legacy consistent with claim), 5–300s
timeout recorded/enforced-by-lease, clipped reason, secret
scan, 4KB payload cap. Preview dry-runs everything.
Delegate prechecks eligibility, creates + assigns, rolls
back on assign failure (nothing drifts), emits
`task.delegated` (requester → target + reason). Target must
still pull/claim; requester can never steal another pin;
reaching a node grants it nothing. Untargeted dispatch
stays `POST /api/v1/tasks`.

`current_task` on every node listing (one indexed query),
mobile panel + hardware detail line included.

## 9. Routing

Verdicts on every rejection; `prefer_idle` (+1 idle,
ordering-only, off by default); `explain_decision` groups
WHY ELIGIBLE/WAITING/BLOCKED/NOT AVAILABLE; route preview
returns it as `why`. Deterministic and inspectable — no
ranking beyond the existing score + node_id tie-break.
Existing reason wording preserved (`not live`).

`stage_states`: ✓ linked evidence present (never "work

# BIG #42 — eindrapport

## 1. What existed

BIG #41 V2 foundation, reused untouched: mesh preview/delegate

## 2. Human verification

`coordinator/app/hardware_links.py` (new): PROPOSED →
VERIFIED → REVOKED store in the chat DB (additive table).
Propose (`POST /api/v1/hardware/links`) always starts
PROPOSED. Verify (`POST .../verify`) needs the operator key —
node credentials are never accepted, so devices cannot
self-verify; REVOKED links refuse re-verification (422).
Audit events `hardware.linked/verified/revoked` name human,
node, device. `/nodes/{id}/reality` overlays VERIFIED only
for exact node+device matches; `hardware_trust()` still can
never return VERIFIED. `/hardware` page lists all three
states.

## 3. Finance

`coordinator/app/finance.py` (new): income/expense/budget,
DRAFT/CONFIRMED/ARCHIVED, amounts as minor units + currency.
Omitted amounts stay NULL → UNKNOWN (never zero). No fake
records — rows exist only via the explicit API. Amounts live
only in the store + `/finance` + project-scoped packets;
generic packets carry counts (`SCOPED` marker otherwise).

## 4. Energy

`coordinator/app/energy.py` (new): solar/battery/grid/machine/
other × production/consumption/storage/state. NULL values
stay UNKNOWN. `GET /api/v1/energy/state` derives current
state from latest state-kind rows. Nothing invented; routing
weights unchanged (data exposed honestly for later use).

## 5. Symbiosis

Prefixes `fin_`, `enr_`, `hv_`, `qst_` + closed predicates
`funds`, `funded_by`, `powers`, `powered_by`, `allocated_to`.

mission gates. No generic workflow executor; catalogue is
closed at 8.

## 7. Quest trails

read derives ✓/●/!/○ from missions, tasks, finance, energy,
hardware links (each step links to its record). Progress is
real done/total — no XP. Quest states READY/ACTIVE/WAITING/
BLOCKED/COMPLETED/FAILED. `/quests` page, JSON API, refresh
audits via `quest.updated`.

## 8. Remote mesh

`POST /api/v1/workflows/preview|dispatch`: max 6 pinned
steps (research on A, camera on B, compute on C) through the
existing task queue — validate → auth → eligibility precheck
→ create → assign per step, coordinator authoritative, nodes
pull-based. Failed step stops the workflow; queued steps keep
their lease lifecycle, never silently dropped. Same closed
contracts as `/mesh/delegate`.

## 9. Hardware-aware readiness

`quests.step_readiness()`: READY names the eligible node
(shared `research_readiness`), WAITING when the camera node
is offline / no researcher eligible, BLOCKED on failed
records, UNAVAILABLE for printer transport. Offline hardware
is never pretended available.

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/camera-ecosystem.md">
# Camera Ecosystem (BIG #34)

Camera input is a first-class entrance to the living
Mycelium ecosystem — never an authority. The chain:

FILE → INGEST SESSION → OBSERVATION → VLM (or honest
fallback) → CANDIDATE → POSSIBLE MATCH → LINK PROPOSAL
(YES) → SYMBIOSIS → CRAFT → GUIDE → MEMORY (only through
the existing truth flow) → MORNING / ACTIVITY / WORLD.

## Multi-file ingest sessions (REAL)

`POST /api/v1/camera-sessions` (`device_id` + up to 8 inbox
filenames) creates a `cing_…` session; `POST
/api/v1/camera-sessions/{id}/run` ingests every file through
the existing `FileIngestAdapter` validation (plain filename,
inside the camera dir, known suffix, capped size). Each file
gets an `obs-…` observation; states per item: `queued`,
`observed`, `duplicate`, `refused`. Dedupe is by sha256
across recent sessions: replays refuse as duplicates and
never create a second observation. Sessions live in the
additive `camera_ingest_sessions` table (chat DB, JSON dump
pattern like `vision_analyses`). No video is ever processed
whole — the operator extracts stills first.

## VLM layer (REAL / UNAVAILABLE)

`POST /api/v1/observations/{id}/describe` tries the local
Ollama loopback provider (`qwen3-vl:4b` default, loopback
only, no downloads, no cloud). Success stores a structured
analysis (labels, confidences, description, uncertainty) and
reports `vlm_state: REAL`. When the backend is unreachable
the call does NOT fail: it stores an extractive fallback
(media facts only, empty labels, `model: ""`, explicit
uncertainty) and reports `vlm_state: UNAVAILABLE`. The two
are distinguishable in storage, and the fallback never
claims a VLM ran.

## Observation → candidate (REAL, gated)

`POST /api/v1/observations/{id}/propose-candidates` turns
each REAL VLM label into one `observation`-type knowledge
candidate (suggested name, model confidence, evidence bound
to the observation, sensor/ai provenance). Idempotent per
(observation, label); fallback analyses yield nothing. No
auto-promotion: candidates mature through support → YES →
memory in `/knowledge` exactly like every other candidate.

## Entity matching (POSSIBLE MATCH, never merge)

`GET /api/v1/camera-match?q=…` returns bounded substring
evidence over inventory objects/projects/ideas. `POST
/api/v1/camera-suggest-link` (`observation_id`, `entity_id`,
closed predicate set: `used_in`, `component_of`,
`related_to`, `stored_at`, `supports`, `evidence_for`,
`part_of`) creates a `connection` candidate that surfaces
as PROPOSED in the symbiosis layer (`/symbiosis`). YES / NO
/ REVIEW run through the existing knowledge flow.

## Craft, guide, timeline, notifications

Camera observations already flow into world-graph overlays,
so `/craft` picks them up (present ✓ / missing ? /
uncertain ○ via gaps). The guide gains camera items
(inbox files, undescribed observations). `GET
/api/v1/camera-timeline` reads the shared bus (no second
event system). IN_APP notifications (`new_observation`,
`camera_ready`, `candidate_waiting`, `new_connection`) fan
out to registered nodes only; WEB_PUSH stays UNAVAILABLE.

## Insta360 status

REAL: registration, file ingest, metadata, sessions,
analysis of provided files. UNAVAILABLE: direct live
transport, camera control, proprietary protocol — until a
reviewed adapter exists. REGISTERED is never CONNECTED.
The Camera Guide on `/cameras` shows the 8-step file path.

## What Jelles does tomorrow

1. Register the X4 on `/cameras` (source `insta360`).
2. Shoot, export a still, copy it into the inbox
   (`GET /api/v1/camera-inbox` lists names).
3. Run a session from the camera detail page.
4. Describe (VLM), propose candidates, review.
5. YES keeps one; suggest a link to the solar project.
6. Watch it appear in symbiosis, craft, guide, morning.
</file>

# Startgids voor een kleine gemeenschap

Begin met één oude laptop als coördinator en één reserve-pc als worker. Installeer de coördinator lokaal, open het dashboard en geef de worker alleen de capabilities die hij echt mag uitvoeren. Houd een papieren of gedeelde lijst bij van eigenaar, stroomverbruik en doel van elk apparaat.

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/conversation-intelligence.md">
# Conversation Intelligence (BIG #37)

Conversations are traces of thought. Mycelium reads them as
structure — themes, decisions, promises, contradictions,
missed items, research questions, entity links, possible
symbioses — and routes everything through the existing
truth flow. Analysis is OBSERVATION or CANDIDATE, never
fact. Jelles decides.

## Pipeline (no second import system)

IMPORT (bridge) → NORMALIZE → SEGMENT → THEMES →
DECISIONS → PROMISES → QUESTIONS → CONTRADICTIONS →
MISSED → RESEARCH → ENTITY LINKS → SYMBIOSIS → HUMAN
REVIEW → ECOSYSTEM. All computation is deterministic and
extractive (`method: extractive-local`, no LLM involved),
stored as `conversation_intel` records keyed by sha256
fingerprint for cross-conversation dedupe.

## What each layer yields

- **Themes**: term frequency over content words (NL/EN
  stopwords), supporting messages, related entity mentions
  and inventory projects, heuristic confidence. OBSERVATION.
- **Decisions**: decision-marker findings with confidence
  (explicit markers = high), resolution UNRESOLVED.
  CONFIRM/REJECT/IGNORE run through candidate
  support/promote/reject — never silent truth.
- **Promises**: commitment markers with owner from role
  only (`user` → Jelles, else assistant — never invented
  names). Status UNKNOWN unless a mission/event mentions
  the same terms (then IN_PROGRESS with evidence).
  Completion is never claimed from mere mention.
- **Contradictions**: A/B sides with sources, status
  UNRESOLVED. No winner is picked; humans resolve via the
  knowledge flow.
- **Missed items**: bridge findings mapped to categories
  (PROJECT/TASK/QUESTION/RESEARCH/RELATIONSHIP/OBJECT/
  MATERIAL/MACHINE/DOCUMENTATION/DECISION/PROMISE/RISK/
  DEPENDENCY), each with evidence.
- **Research proposals**: open/investigative statements
  become question candidates plus queue-ready payloads; the
  RESEARCH button posts to the existing research queue
  (draft runs — execution still needs a mission YES).
- **Entity links**: entity mentions matched against a
  bounded inventory browse → LINK CANDIDATE connection
  candidates. Never silent merges.
- **Symbiosis**: co-mentioned entities/projects →
  PROPOSED connection candidates for the guarded YES flow.

## Materialize (explicit, idempotent)

`materialize(conversation_id, fingerprint, action)` with
actions `candidate` | `research-queue` | `link`. Replay
returns `already-materialized`. Health-flagged text
refuses. Wrong kind/action combinations refuse.

## Cross-conversation reasoning

`cross_conversation()` aggregates by fingerprint (no
duplicate observations), surfaces repeated themes, and
flags REVISIT observations when a theme recurs across
imports without mission/event progress. Timeline orders
intel by message index with real import stamps; unknown
stays unknown.

## Truth model + security

Imported content is untrusted: escaped data at render,
health-isolated, secrets redacted at import, oversized and
duplicate imports refused, fake IDs 404/422. Nothing
imported can approve, execute, verify, or change truth
tiers. No shell/RCE/eval; no URLs fetched; no credentials.

## UI + ecosystem wiring

- `/conversations` is the AI ARCHIVE (recent, themes,
  threads, decisions/promises, contradictions, missed,
  research, project links).
- Detail pages show every section with materialize buttons,
  a DISCOVERY banner (real unmaterialized counts), timeline,
  and the existing continue-elsewhere packet links.
- Packets carry an optional `intelligence` section
  (bounded, no history dumps).
- World graph gains an `intel` overlay (opt-in flag,
  dashed provenance, filterable).
- Guide, mobile Threads, and IN_APP notifications
  (`conversation_analyzed`) surface intel; craft and
  symbiosis consume materialized candidates.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/coordinator-failover.md">
# Coordinator Failover (BIG #10)

Eén actieve coordinator per epoch, zonder Raft, zonder
brokers, zonder cloud. Lease + epoch + fencing +
deterministische verkiezing + quorum/degraded-modus.

```
node (coordinator_capable, online, fresh)
        ↓  POST /api/v1/coordinator/campaign
quorum van stemgerechtigden? → epoch+1, leasehouder
geen quorum? → expliciete degraded-modus (geen stil
   leiderschap, geen split-brain-claim)
        ↓  assign/claim stempelen + weigeren op epoch
oude epoch schrijft → geweigerd (fencing)
```

## Regels

- Alleen nodes met operator-vlag `coordinator_capable`
  (default uit) mogen meedoen; onbekende/offline/disabled
  nodes tellen nooit mee.
- Verkiezing is deterministisch: laagste `node_id` wint bij
  gelijke geschiktheid — geen dobbelsteen, geen race.
- Lease met verval; `POST /api/v1/coordinator/release`
  geeft vrij. Een levende vreemde houder weigert een
  campagne (fail-closed).
- Elke `assign` stempelt de huidige epoch; `claim`
  revalideert epoch + lease + capabilities. Na een nieuwe
  epoch fence-en oude toewijzingen: claimen op de oude
  epoch levert niets op.
- Status: `GET /api/v1/coordinator/status` toont epoch,
  houder, verval, kiezers en modus (quorum/degraded).

## Wat dit niet is

Geen consensus-protocol, geen automatische failover naar
een willekeurige node, geen gedeelde schijf. Bij twijfel
staat het systeem stil in degraded-modus tot een mens of
een stemgerechtigde node een nieuwe epoch opent.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/desktop-hands.md">
# Desktop Agent Hands (BIG #22) — IMPLEMENTED

Mycelium is the brain, the desktop agent is the hands:
chat → mission → approved plan → desktop step →
desktop approval where required → claim → revalidate →
mouse/keyboard action → screenshot/observation →
result → mission loop → next step. Proven end to end
over real localhost HTTP with the real Windows backend
(screenshots verified byte-for-byte as 24-bit BMP).

## What runs where

- Coordinator: propose → approve (exact YES) → atomic
  dispatch with lease (300s) + attempt counting (max 3)
  → revalidation reads → result intake → mission
  continuation → verification → memory. Never input.
- Agent process (`python -m desktop_agent.main`):
  register → heartbeat → claim → revalidate (status +
  owner + lease + params, fail-closed) → observe →
  act → observe → report. Full capabilities, `--once`,
  `--read-only` and `--dry-run` modes; stops between
  actions, never mid-action.

## Lease, failure, recovery

- Dispatch stamps `lease_until` + `attempt_count`;
  re-dispatch past 3 attempts refuses.
- `expire_desktop_leases()` runs lazily on every claim:
  expired → approved while attempts remain (re-claim
  allowed), blocked when exhausted. Late reports still
  win their own conditional-update race.
- Agent revalidation blocks on expired leases; operator
  cancel revokes between actions; coordinator loss
  backs off; step limits bound every run.
- Mission loop reports `waiting_agent` while dispatched
  and continues after the result lands.

## Boundaries (unchanged, tested)

- Only allow-listed ComputerActions (screenshot, wait,
  move/click/scroll, type/key/hotkey); unknown types,
  out-of-range coordinates and shell-like actions
  refuse at validation.
- Mission approval never auto-approves desktop input;
  every input action needs its own exact YES.
- Physical actions are impossible through this chain:
  no printer/robot/drone path exists here, and the
  generic executors refuse them (HARDWARE_REQUIRED).
- Tokens/hashes never appear in nodes, status,
  actions or logs (tested).
- No shell, subprocess, code execution, cloud or
  inbound ports anywhere in the loop.

## Real vs simulated

- REAL on Windows: screenshots (GDI BitBlt → local
  BMP, retention-capped), mouse move/click/scroll,
  keyboard type/press/hotkey, active-window title —
  stdlib ctypes only, no new dependency. Verified:
  1920×1080 capture in ~0.15s, no-op cursor move,
  full claim→screenshot→report→mission-completion
  over live HTTP with zero desktop disturbance.
- Click/type/keypress paths execute ONLY from
  approved + dispatched actions in production; the
  smoke deliberately used screenshot steps so no
  real input landed. DryRun backend validates but
  executes nothing (tests default to fakes).
- Task-queue `expire_leases` remains uncalled in
  production (pre-existing; documented future work —
  assigned tasks with dead nodes wait for it).
</file>

# Digital Twin (BIG #11-15, Phase 5) — PARTIAL (foundation IMPLEMENTED)

physical entity ↔ digital entity ↔ observations ↔
sensors ↔ files ↔ events, as explicit links with
source, confidence and last-observed time. Home
structure (rooms/workshop/garden/camper/…) is
expressed through INVENTory locations +
relationships — this module links and scores
freshness, it does not hardcode a house.

Staleness is computed (configurable bound, default
24h) and reported as fresh/stale/unknown with the
method shown. "Fresh" means recently observed and
is never presented as automatically current.
Spatial mapping, live sensor binding and any
real-time twin behaviour are FUTURE.

Familiars (implemented alongside): one capability
model unifying desktop agent, phone, robot, drone,
camera, machine and future AR devices — identity +
kind + kind allow-list + link to the backing
entity, so no device becomes its own AI system.

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/distributed-architecture.md">
# Distributed Mycelium Architecture (BIG #8)

Pull-based, capability-gated task distribution over ordinary
local machines. **The coordinator never sends arbitrary
executable code to nodes**: nodes pull task kinds they
understand, execute only allow-listed local behavior, and
report results. Routing is scheduling logic — never a claim
that one model is "better".

```
task requirements (closed, declarative)
        ↓
route_task(requirements, advertised nodes, policy)
        ↓ RouteDecision (selected + eligible + rejected + why)
        ↓
assign (queued task → node constraint, still pull-only)
        ↓
node pulls / claims (revalidates caps, lease, attempts)
        ↓
execute (allow-listed local executor only)
        ↓
result → verification (existing rules)
```

## Nodes

Stable `node_id` (never display names). Statuses: unknown,
online, stale, offline, disabled (sticky — re-registration
never clears it). Freshness: heartbeat ≤ 60s. Node/runtime
state lives in the coordinator queue DB, never in INVENTory.

Advertisement (validated, closed, fail-closed):

- capabilities: explicit strings, no `*` wildcards, no
  inheritance. A task can never grant a capability.
- models: `mod_*` (INVENTory world-model link) or `model:`
  (node-local runtime). World records describe models;
  advertisements describe "this node has this available now".
- executors: `exec:<kind>` namespace only.
- resources: bounded hints (cpu/mem/gpu/storage/energy),
  never guarantees, never measurements.
- locality: closed label; equality match or `any`.
  Loopback-only transport stays the real boundary.

## Trust (minimal, local-first)

Per-node bearer token from local config (`--node-token` /
`MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN`, placeholder in `.env.example`, never
committed). The coordinator stores only a salted hash, never
the token; tokens never appear in logs or API output. First
registration binds, later calls must match (403 otherwise).
Nodes without a hash stay in legacy mode so existing clients
keep working. This proves secret possession on a trusted LAN
— it is NOT PKI. Rotation = register again with a new token.

## Routing

`route_task` in `coordinator/app/routing.py`. Hard gates:
fresh + live + authenticated (when required) + required
capabilities ⊆ advertised + model types + executor +
locality. Preferences only order: preferred model ids,
memory/GPU minimums, solar + energy-level policy. Energy
never disqualifies. Tie-break: lowest node_id (fully
deterministic). Every decision explains itself
(`selected … because …`, per-node rejection reasons).

Model routing reuses the requirement vocabulary (model type /
model id / vision capability) — never quality ranking, never
auto-invocation, never downloads, never cloud.

## Queue placement

`POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/assign` constrains a queued task to
a node (explicit id must prove eligible, or auto-route);
assignment never pushes work — the node still claims.
`POST /api/v1/tasks/route` is a dry run (no state change).
`GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}` exposes requirements, assignment
and the routing explanation for chat/mission clients.

Claim revalidates live: assignment ownership, capability
subset, model types, executor, token, freshness, attempts.
The desktop-action claim path (`/desktop/actions/next`)
checks tokens identically.

## Leases, retry, failure

Existing lease/attempt machinery is authoritative (300s
lease, max 3 attempts, atomic transitions). Lease expiry
requeues software tasks and fails exhausted ones — except
physical tasks (`requirements.physical_action`) with
uncertain execution, which become `blocked` for the operator
instead of silently requeueing. A printer start, click or
other physical action is therefore never duplicated because
a node disappeared. Retry stays bounded; counters never reset.

## Desktop agent

Unchanged behavior, token-aware: register/heartbeat/claim
send `MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN` when configured, omit it
otherwise (legacy mode). Pull-only, no shell, approval gate
and binding proof untouched.

## Energy

Optional hints (`energy_source`, `energy_level`,
`energy_priority`) feed ordering only. Explanations say
"policy-compatible hint", never "greener/better". No power
control, no shutdown, no autonomous energy decisions.

## Chat / missions

Assignment responses and task detail carry the routing
decision, so chat can say: "Ik stuur deze taak naar node X
omdat die de vereiste camera- en VLM-capabilities heeft."
Descriptive only — chat cannot pick node IDs to bypass
routing; explicit selection stays on the assign endpoint.

## UI

Dashboard nodes table shows derived status (incl. stale),
capability/model/executor counts. Detail lives in JSON
(`GET /api/v1/nodes`, `/api/v1/nodes/{id}`).

## Security model

Unknown/disabled/unauthenticated/stale nodes refused;
wildcards, paths, commands and URLs refused at every
boundary; credentials never logged/returned; identity bound
to tokens; lease ownership enforced; physical work never
auto-reroutes; fingerprints still gate approvals and
artifacts. No cloud fallback, no public bind, no open ports,
no inbound connections, no privilege escalation.

## Limitations (honest)

- Token auth is bearer-on-LAN, not PKI; no rotation protocol
  beyond re-register; legacy mode exists for compatibility.
- No encrypted transport; loopback-only by default.
- Locality labels are policy hints, not topology proof.
- Energy hints are self-reported, not measured.
- Simulated nodes (`sim_nodes.py`) test orchestration only.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/distributed-state.md">
# Distributed State (BIG #10)

Event/change-log-synchronisatie tussen coordinator-instanties.
**Nooit een DB-kopie**: alleen gevalideerde enveloppen gaan over
de lijn, via HTTP-pull, begrensd en idempotent.

```
lokale wijziging → DistEnvelope (dsevt_-id, revisie, epoch)
        ↓  append (durable log, dist_events)
pull: GET /api/v1/sync/changes?after=&limit= (≤100/page)
        ↓  apply_pulled: validate → idempotent apply
duplicaat → acknowledged (geen dubbele toepassing)
conflict  → expliciet record (dscon_-id, status open) — nooit
            stil gemerged, nooit last-write-wins
```

## Regels

- Envelop-ID's zijn `dsevt_`-prefixed; revisies zijn opaque
  strings die alleen op (on)gelijkheid worden vergeleken.
- Payloads: ≤20 keys, waarden ≤2000 tekens, alleen
  str/int/float/bool/None/list/dict. Sleutels als
  `command`, `shell`, `exec`, `script`, `sql`, `eval`
  weigeren — bij constructie én bij apply (pull-path
  omzeilt de constructor).
- `mergeable_update` kent een kleine allow-list voor
  technische metadata; alles daarbuiten bij gelijke
  basis-revisie → conflict, beide versies bewaard.
- Conflicten lossen alleen expliciet op
  (`POST /api/v1/dist/conflicts/{id}/resolve`); oplossen
  herschrijft geen versies, het markeert alleen.
- Cursor advancing: alleen applied/duplicates schuiven de
  cursor op; conflicts houden hun cursor voor review,
  failed items nooit.

## INVENTory-koppeling

Eén richting, read-only, over HTTP:
`GET /api/v1/inventory/changes?since=&limit=` leest de
INVENTory-eventlog via de bestaande bridge
(`events_since`), nooit het SQLite-bestand. INVENTory
kreeg daarvoor één additieve cursor:
`GET /api/v1/events?since=<ISO-timestamp>&limit=` (clamp
1..500). Geen dumps, geen SQL aan de buitenkant.
</file>

# Energy ecosystem (BIG #42)

Minimal energy domain: sources, production, consumption,
storage and current state, linked to projects/devices.

## Model

- Sources (closed): `solar` | `battery` | `grid` | `machine` |
  `other`.
- Kinds (closed): `production` | `consumption` | `storage` |
  `state`.
- **Unknown values stay NULL and render as UNKNOWN.**
  Measurements are never invented.
- Current state (`GET /api/v1/energy/state`) derives from the
  latest `state`-kind rows — never stored twice, explicit
  empty when nothing is recorded.

## Rules

- One observation per POST; `recorded_by` + observed_at +
  provenance on every row.
- Unknown energy honestly blocks energy-aware decisions
  (presence `energy_unknown`, guide items) instead of
  pretending availability.

## Symbiosis

Prefixes `enr_` + closed predicates `powers` / `powered_by`
(project↔energy, energy↔machine/node). Never merges entities.

## Future influence (not yet wired)

Routing, node availability, projects, machines, symbiosis,
guide and the morning report can read this store; BIG #42
exposes the data honestly but changes no routing weights.

## Surfaces

`/energy` page + API, presence `energy_unknown` (waiting),
guide energy items ("finance but no energy source"), morning
ENERGY section (only when records exist), overview `energy`,
packet-v2 energy block, mobile energy panel.
</file>

# Finance ecosystem (BIG #42)

Minimal, first-class finance records. This is NOT accounting
software: just enough to make money a real ecosystem entity.

## Model

- Kinds (closed): `income` | `expense` | `budget`.
- Status (closed): `DRAFT` → `CONFIRMED` | `ARCHIVED`.
- Amounts are minor units + 3-letter currency. **Omitted
  amounts stay NULL and render as UNKNOWN — never zero,
  never invented.**
- Every record carries `project_ref`, a note, and human-recorded
  provenance (`human_verified=False`; recording is not
  verification).

## Rules

- No fake records: rows exist only through the explicit API
  with operator-supplied figures.
- Privacy: amounts live ONLY in the finance store, its
  dedicated endpoints, and the scoped `/finance` page.
  Generic packets carry counts; amounts enter a packet ONLY
  when its `project_id` matches the record's `project_ref`
  (asserted in tests). Telemetry never carries finance data.

## Symbiosis

Prefixes `fin_` + closed predicates `funds` / `funded_by` /
`allocated_to` (strict at proposal input, `related` display
fallback for unknown stored verbs). Never merges entities.

## Surfaces

`/finance` page + API, `finance_pending` presence items
(DRAFT rows, waiting band), guide finance/energy items,
morning FINANCE section (only when records exist), overview
`finance` (counts + unknown-amount count), packet-v2 scoped
finance block, mobile finance panel (counts only).

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/first-node-blueprint.md">
# First Node Blueprint — eerste echte externe node (BIG #5)

Praktische blauwdruk voor de eerste node buiten de coordinator-
machine zelf (oude laptop, werkplaats-pc). Alleen wat het
huidige protocol al kan: registreren, heartbeat, pull, claim,
uitvoeren, rapporteren. Geen nieuw distributed runtime-systeem.

## Stroom (pull-only)

```
Coordinator (:8000)
    ↓  node pollt (outbound-only, geen inbound ports)
Node
    ↓  capability discovery (vrijwillig profiel + owner-capabilities)
claim (één bounded task, lease 300s, max 3 pogingen)
    ↓  revalidatie (capability-match op live data)
execute (alleen wat de taak beschrijft — nooit meer)
    ↓  result (completed/failed + observatie-referentie)
verification (coordinator/mens, los van het resultaat)
```

## Identity

- `node_id` bij registratie (`POST /api/v1/nodes/register`);
  een her-registratie met hetzelfde id upsert — gebruik bij
  twijfel over stale state een verse id (`seed-02`).
- Tier: `seed` (begin hier), later `worker`/`core`.
- Start-capability: `system_inventory` (read-only loop).
  Desktop-input weigert de node-client zonder expliciete
  menselijke approval; uitvoeren van input loopt uitsluitend
  via de standalone desktop-agent op een vertrouwde machine.

## Capabilities (geen escalatie)

- Capabilities worden door de eigenaar opgegeven, nooit door
  het netwerk verleend. Geen automatische uitbreiding: een node
  die `desktop.mouse.click` claimt zonder dat de owner het
  configureerde, krijgt geen taken (`exec:`-namespace,
  exacte match).
- Model-routing via capability-matching (`capability_matching.py`);
  twijfel = deny.

## Heartbeat & freshness

- Heartbeat (`POST /api/v1/nodes/{id}/heartbeat`); poll elke ~5s.
- Stale-grens 60s (`NODE_STALE_SECONDS`): oudere nodes gelden
  als offline en krijgen geen claims.
- Taken: lease 300s (`LEASE_SECONDS`), max 3 pogingen
  (`MAX_ATTEMPTS`); verlopen leases vallen terug in de queue.

## Claims & revalidatie

- Claim (`POST /api/v1/tasks/claim/{node_id}`) is atomair;
  staged proposal-taken zijn onbereikbaar voor claims (alleen
  `queued` claimt).
- Vóór uitvoering: capability-snapshot moet gelijk zijn aan de
  goedgekeurde snapshot (promotion-poort); verschil = deny.
- Resultaat (`POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/complete`) is een
  observatie, geen waarheid — verificatie gebeurt apart
  (BIG #5: readback, geen model-mening).

## Provenance & failure

- Elke taak draagt provenance; `ai-generated` wordt nooit
  automatisch `human_verified`.
- Failure-semantiek: completed/failed/cancelled/blocked met
  timing en error. Gefaalde pogingen tellen op tot het maximum;
  daarna menselijke review, geen stille retry.
- Stale nodes: hun leases verlopen, hun taken worden opnieuw
  verdeeld, hun oude registratie blijft zichtbaar als offline.

## Harde grenzen voor de eerste node

- Geen inbound ports op de node (alleen outbound polls).
- Geen arbitrary shell, geen arbitraire code-uitvoering.
- Geen credential-opslag op de node.
- Geen push/merge/commit via de node (git writes alleen via
  de gecontroleerde coordinator-capability met allow-list).
- Geen automatische capability-escalatie.
- Cloud is additief, nooit vereist; LAN volstaat.

## Startcommando's

Coordinator eerst, daarna de node (twee terminals):

```powershell
python -m uvicorn coordinator.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
python -m node_client.main --coordinator http://127.0.0.1:8000 --node-id seed-01 --tier seed --capability system_inventory --poll-seconds 5
```

Zichtbaar in de UI onder Nodes als `seed-01`/`seed`/`online`
na enkele seconden. Lukt dat, dan werkt de basis; alles
daarna (writes, missies, verificatie) loopt via dezelfde
voorstel → approval → uitvoering → verificatie-keten.
</file>
