<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/hardware-reality-layer.md">
# Hardware Reality Layer (BIG #39)

The coordinator knows what its nodes really are: live telemetry,
connected hardware, compute capabilities, and energy state —
reported by the nodes themselves, validated fail-closed, and
used for routing, guidance, and display. Nothing is executed,
nothing is inferred, nothing is promised.

## Philosophy

```
Node reports → coordinator validates → stores → routes,
guides, and shows. Never executes, never invents.
```

- **No new execution power**: telemetry is read-only state.
  The coordinator never drives hardware, runs inference, or
  starts work on a node. Tasks still route by advertised
  capabilities; telemetry only adds honest gates and ordering.
- **Fail-closed validation**: unknown telemetry fields, hardware
  kinds, compute capabilities, and energy sources are refused
  with 422. Nothing unknown is ever stored.
- **No wildcards, no shell**: capability rules from BIG #8 are
  untouched. Telemetry adds no executable surface (static
  assert in tests).
- **Node-reported, never verified**: hardware and compute are
  what the node claims. They appear as `node-reported`,
  `human_verified=False` provenance in the world graph — never
  as INVENTory world truth.
- **Provenance always**: overlays carry `source_type:
  node-reported` with the reporting node as creator.

## Data model

Six additive nullable columns on `nodes` (migration in
`_ensure_node_columns`, existing rows keep working):

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| `telemetry` | JSON object | CPU/memory/disk percents, counts, uptime, temperature, load average, interfaces, boot time |
| `telemetry_timestamp` | ISO text | When the last telemetry heartbeat arrived |
| `hardware` | JSON list | `{kind, identifier, details, status, connected_since}` |
| `compute_capabilities` | JSON list | `{capability, details, status, since}` |
| `energy_state` | JSON object | `{source, level_percent, charging, details, since}` |
| `health` | text | Reserved; health is derived live, not stored |

`Heartbeat` schema accepts the four new optional fields with
pydantic bounds (hardware ≤ 50, compute ≤ 20). Validation lives
in `nodes.py`: `check_telemetry`, `check_hardware`,
`check_compute_capabilities`, `check_energy_state`.

### Closed sets

- Telemetry: 16 known fields, bounded numbers (percents
  0–100, temperature −50–150 °C, non-negative counters).
- Hardware kinds: `camera`, `usb`, `printer_3d`, `sensor`,
  `storage`, `gpu`, `display`, `audio`, `network`, `other`.
- Compute capabilities: `ollama`, `local_models`,
  `cpu_inference`, `gpu_available`, `vram_mb`, `research`,
  `vision`, `inventory`, `analysis`.
- Energy sources: `grid`, `solar`, `battery`, `unknown`.
- Hardware status: `connected` / `disconnected` / `error` /
  `unknown` (normalized, never refused).
- Compute status: `available` / `busy` / `unavailable` /
  `unknown` (normalized, never refused).

## Health: ONLINE / DEGRADED / STALE / OFFLINE / UNKNOWN

Derived live in `_compute_health_status` (and
`compute_node_health` for pure use) from stored status +
telemetry freshness:

- `disabled` → OFFLINE (sticky, wins over everything)
- `offline` → OFFLINE, `stale` → STALE
- online/busy with telemetry older than 5 minutes → DEGRADED
- online/busy otherwise → ONLINE

Health never disqualifies silently: routing treats it as an
explicit `min_health` requirement with inspectable reasons.

## Telemetry-aware routing

`routing.py` gains hard gates (any failure rejects with an
exact reason) and preferences (score only, never requirements):

Hard gates:
- `required_hardware`: every kind must be `connected` on the
  node right now. Disconnected hardware does not count.
- `required_compute`: every capability must be `available`.
  Busy does not count.
- `max_telemetry_age_seconds`: telemetry timestamp must be
  fresh enough; missing/invalid timestamps reject.
- `min_health`: `ONLINE(4) > DEGRADED(3) > STALE(2) >
  OFFLINE(1) > UNKNOWN(0)`.

Preferences (`RoutingPolicy`):
- `prefer_fresh_telemetry` (+1 for telemetry < 60 s)
- `prefer_connected_hardware` (+1 when any connected)
- `prefer_compute_capabilities` (+1 when any available)

Energy and resources stay preferences, never disqualifiers —
unchanged from BIG #8.

## Surfaces

| Surface | Hardware Reality integration |
|---------|------------------------------|
| Nodes API (`/api/v1/nodes`, `/api/v1/nodes/{id}`) | Telemetry, hardware, compute, energy, `health_status`, `telemetry_timestamp` |
| `/nodes` page + capability check | Existing cards; routing dry-run answers capability questions |
| Route dry-run (`POST /api/v1/tasks/route`) | Hardware/compute/health/telemetry-age requirements honored |
| Mobile (`/api/v1/mobile/dashboard`, `/mobile`) | Nodes panel: health + cpu/mem/disk/temp/uptime + hardware counts/kinds + compute counts/capabilities + energy |
| Guide (`/api/v1/guide`, `/guide`) | Ollama-online, GPU-available, camera-connected, printer-connected, offline-node, disconnected-hardware, research-waiting items (all link to `/nodes`) |
| World graph (`/world?show=…,hardware,compute`) | Node overlay carries health/telemetry/hardware/compute counts; `hw_<node>_<id>` nodes (HAS edges) for connected hardware; `compute_<node>_<cap>` nodes (PROVIDES edges) for available compute |
| Notifications | Additive bus types `node.health_changed`, `node.hardware_changed`, `node.compute_changed`, `node.telemetry_received`; additive IN_APP kinds `node_online/degraded/stale`, `hardware_connected/disconnected`, `capability_available/unavailable`, `telemetry_stale`, `mission_blocked_hardware`. WEB_PUSH stays UNAVAILABLE |

## Node client

`node_client/main.py` collects read-only state with psutil
(best-effort, every call guarded) and sends it on every
heartbeat:

- `collect_telemetry()` — hostname, OS, CPU/memory/disk,
  uptime, temperature (Linux), load average (Unix), interface
  names only. No process lists, no credentials, no paths.
- `collect_hardware()` — v4l2 cameras, `lsusb` devices,
  serial 3D-printer ports, NVIDIA GPUs. Detection only.
- `collect_compute_capabilities()` — `ollama list` models,
  always-on `cpu_inference`, `nvidia-smi` GPU/VRAM, derived
  `research`/`analysis`/`vision`/`inventory` flags.
- `collect_energy_state()` — battery level/charging or
  grid assumption; `unknown` on failure.

Subprocess calls are bounded (`timeout=3–5 s`), output
truncated, and failures degrade to empty — a node never
fails to heartbeat because detection failed.

## Security

- Unknown fields/kinds/capabilities/sources → 422, nothing
  stored (partial updates keep prior good values via
  `COALESCE`, never partial-bad writes).
- Credential gates untouched: bad tokens 403, unknown nodes
  404, disabled nodes refused, legacy freeze preserved.
- No wildcard capabilities, no shell metacharacters, no
  URLs/credentials in providers — existing tripwires all
  still green.
- Node-reported data never enters INVENTory, never becomes
  memory/candidate truth, never approves anything.
- Labels: node-reported state is REAL (measured locally);
  disconnected/stale data is shown as such, never hidden;
  printer transport stays UNAVAILABLE; fab execution stays
  SIMULATED. See the final report §REAL/TEST/SIMULATED.

## Limitations

- Health is freshness-based, not diagnostic: DEGRADED means
  "telemetry older than 5 minutes", nothing more.
- Hardware/compute are self-reported claims; a lying node
  can claim a GPU. Routing treats them as advertisements
  (like capabilities), not attestations.
- No push: the coordinator never polls nodes; state is only
  as fresh as the last heartbeat.
- Bus event types exist additively; heartbeat does not emit
  per-beat events (no spam). Surfaces read live store state.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/hardware-verification.md">
# Hardware verification (BIG #42)

Human-controlled trust for node/device claims. Trust levels
(see `nodes.hardware_trust`):

- ADVERTISED — the node said so. Default, never a fact.
- OBSERVED — connected + fresh telemetry (<300s). Derived.
- VERIFIED — a live row in the hardware-links store with status
  VERIFIED. **No automated path may ever derive it.**

## Flow

1. PROPOSE — anyone: `POST /api/v1/hardware/links`
   (human_ref, node_id, device_ref, kind, capability, evidence).
   The row always starts PROPOSED. Proposing verifies nothing.
2. VERIFY — operator key only:
   `POST /api/v1/hardware/links/{id}/verify`
   (verified_by + operator_key). Node credentials are never
   accepted here, so a device cannot self-verify.
3. REVOKE — operator key only:
   `POST /api/v1/hardware/links/{id}/revoke`. REVOKED sticks:
   re-verification is refused (422).

## Rules

- VERIFY requires status PROPOSED + a non-empty human
  verified_by. Re-verifying an already-VERIFIED link is a
  no-op returning the link; verifying a REVOKED link refuses.
- Audit trail: `hardware.linked` / `hardware.verified` /
  `hardware.revoked` bus events name human, node, device —
  never secrets.
- The `/nodes/{id}/reality` endpoint overlays VERIFIED only
  when a live VERIFIED link names that exact node + device
  ref. `hardware_trust()` itself can never return VERIFIED
  (asserted in tests).
- Unknown nodes cannot be linked (404). Fake link ids 404.
  Empty/unknown statuses refuse (422). Everything fails closed.

## Surfaces

`/hardware` page, nodes reality, guide (unverified-GPU/camera
items → /hardware), presence `hardware_unverified` (waiting),
morning HARDWARE section (only when links exist), packet-v2
hardware block (verified counts per node), overview `hardware`.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/health.md">
# Health (BIG #11-15, Phase 2) — IMPLEMENTED (tracking only)

Personal tracking and trends. This is not a medical
engine: no illness assessment exists anywhere in the
module, no hidden score, no medical claims.

## Measurements

Closed metric list (sleep, steps, activity, training,
recovery, hydration, meals, weight/BMI/waist/hip,
energy, stress, heart rate, calories) with per-metric
plausibility bounds. Six source adapters: manual,
wearable, sensor, inventory-derived, external,
file-import. Every row carries source + provenance;
wearable/external values are marked, never trusted.
Dedup on metric/source/moment.

## Personal Health Index

Transparent per-dimension ratios (sleep, activity,
recovery, hydration, nutrition, body, habits, training
consistency) with raw values, calculation method,
missing-data counts and completeness on every
dimension. The overall is a plain mean of available
dimensions, labelled with coverage. Gaps render as
"no data", never as zero.

Health data reaches Live/AI only through the explicit
`health.read` capability plus an `include_health` scope
flag. Real wearable integrations beyond the Garmin mock
are FUTURE.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/human-interface-architecture.md">
# Human Interface Architecture (BIG #9)

The living-workshop interface: how Jelles talks to Mycelium —
by text, by voice, from a phone browser — without ever
creating a second coordinator.

```
Human
  ↓ text / voice / phone browser
Interface Adapter (envelope + session, no decisions)
  ↓ converged conversation turn
Mycelium Coordinator (chat → advice → proposal → approval)
  ↓ mission / task / BIG #8 routing
Node (pull-only, capability-gated)
  ↓ result / observation
Coordinator (verification, events)
  ↓ text / spoken / notification rendering
Human
```

Two sentences that never mix:

- **The human interface is not a second coordinator.**
  Adapters carry turns; they decide nothing, execute nothing,
  approve nothing.
- **Voice recognition is not authorization.** Transcription
  is interpretation input; only a bound, unexpired, exact
  approval word on exactly one pending request resolves —
  and never for physical execution.

## Interface layer (`interface.py`)

`InterfaceAdapter` contract with `TextInterface` (real) and
`VoiceInterface` (architecture: transcribed text in, reply
text out; no microphone/speaker coupling). `InterfaceMessage`
envelopes converge voice and text as early as possible: after
STT a spoken turn IS a text turn with voice provenance.
Closed input/output types, capped content, no executable
content. `InterfaceSession` tracks presence (active/idle/
expired/revoked, 24h default, 7d cap) — sessions are not
credentials and never double as node identity.

## Voice (`voice.py`, `voice_approval.py`)

STT: `SpeechToTextProvider` with `LocalSTTProvider` (loopback
backend, configured never installed), `UnavailableSTTProvider`
and deterministic `TestSTTProvider`. TTS mirrors it
(`TestTTSProvider` writes a local marker file).
Transcription carries sensor-observed/unverified provenance;
confidence is informational and flows into no gate.

Audio security: one local root (`mycelium-audio`), plain
filenames (`.wav`/`.mp3`/`.ogg`), boundary checks, 25 MiB
cap, retention of 5, explicit delete. No upload, no cloud, no
public URLs, no background recording — capture sessions
(`cap-*`) open explicitly, bounded in time, close explicitly,
and only on nodes advertising `phone.microphone.read`.

Voice approval (`voice_approval.py`): spoken words resolve
only with exactly one pending request, unexpired, target
still pending with unchanged binding, exact YES/NO word —
otherwise refusal (retryable for a non-matching transcript
only). `physical` kinds can never resolve by voice; the
existing exact-YES dialect and fingerprint rules are reused,
and on YES the EXISTING decide path runs (no second
framework).

## Phone as node

Phones register through the normal BIG #8 node flow (stable
id, token, heartbeat, freshness, disabled state) with the
closed `phone.*` capability set (screen, notification,
camera, microphone, speaker). Roles stay explicit:
capabilities authorize, device type never implies permission.
Phone cameras register as `source=phone` devices and capture
through the existing ingest path; phone notifications are
informational records. Pull-only: the phone polls heartbeat,
events and notifications; no inbound ports, no port
forwarding, no public server.

## Events + notifications (`events.py`)

Bounded structured bus (`conversation.message`,
`mission.*`, `task.*`, `observation.created`,
`approval.required/resolved`, `node.*`, ...) with cursor
polling (`GET /api/v1/events?after=`), type filter and
retention. Payloads are small capped dicts; executable keys
(command/exec/url/approved/...) refuse. Notifications are
recipient-bound, expiring, markable-read — reading one
performs nothing. An event is never a command and can never
approve or execute.

## Realtime + status

Polling is the transport (`/events`, `/notifications`,
`/status`); no SSE/websocket/Redis was needed. `/api/v1/
status` returns counts and states only — no secrets, no
dumps, no paths. The mobile page (`/mobile`, responsive,
server-rendered, no framework) shows chat, status, missions,
approvals, notifications and nodes for a phone browser on
the LAN. The desktop chat page gained a compact live panel;
no redesign.

## Chat + routing convergence

Text and voice turns run the same `chat()` (provenance marks
voice origin; counts and sources unchanged when no options
are passed). "Analyseer wat er op mijn bureau ligt" flows:
chat → camera/vision requirements → BIG #8 routing → node
claim → observation → VLM → answer, with writes only
through controlled approval. Task detail
(`/tasks/by-id/{id}`) exposes assignment + routing
explanation so chat can describe where work goes and why.

## Provenance

voice input → STT provider/model → message → advice/proposal
→ approval → task → node → executor/model → result →
verification; TTS renders response text with its own
provenance. Nothing here is ever auto-`human_verified`.

## Privacy

Audio and transcripts stay local; media by reference only in
context; absolute paths redacted where existing redaction
applies; no background capture; no hidden activation;
explicit expiry for audio; sessions carry no credentials.

## Limitations (honest)

- No real STT/TTS backend ships (loopback contract only);
  no microphone/speaker hardware touched by the coordinator.
- No native app, no push infrastructure, no always-on
  microphone, no continuous camera streaming.
- Voice approval covers write/mission/desktop kinds only;
  physical approval stays fully manual.
- Sessions are presence, not auth; tokens stay the node
  credential (BIG #8, reused unchanged).
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/knowledge-lifecycle.md">
# Knowledge Lifecycle (BIG #32)

Information matures visibly instead of appearing as fact:

OBSERVATION → CANDIDATE → SUPPORTED → PROMOTED MEMORY
(and REJECTED as an explicit terminal state).

## Store

`coordinator/app/knowledge.py`, table `knowledge_candidates`
(additive). IDs `cand_...`. Types: idea, observation, claim,
question, connection, task, note. States: observation,
candidate, supported, promoted, rejected.

No numeric confidence is invented: support is a count of
distinct supporters/sources, shown as-is (`♥ n`).

## Intake (all provenance-backed, health refuses)

- Conversation finding → candidate (`POST
  /api/v1/conversation-imports/{id}/findings/{i}/candidate`,
  "Remember as candidate" buttons, `candidate_from_finding()`).
  Health-flagged text refuses — health stays scoped.
- Research open question → candidate (dossier buttons,
  `POST /api/v1/research/dossiers/{id}/questions/{i}/candidate`).
- Camera observation → candidate ("Review as candidate" buttons,
  `POST /api/v1/observations/{id}/candidate` and
  `/web/observations/{id}/candidate`).
- Manual: `/knowledge` form, mobile "Remember this",
  `POST /api/v1/candidates`.

## Support

`POST /api/v1/candidates/{id}/support {supporter, rationale}`.
Same supporter twice is a no-op. Two distinct supporters move
observation/candidate → supported. Terminal states refuse.

## Promotion (explicit, conflict-safe, idempotent)

`POST /api/v1/candidates/{id}/promote {truth?, verified_by?,
importance?}`:

- Default truth per type (observation→observed,
  claim/connection→ai_inference, rest→ai_suggestion).
- Fact tiers (`verified`, `user_fact`) require `verified_by` (a
  human) and go through `verify_memory()` semantics.
- Overlapping `verified`/`user_fact` memories refuse with the
  conflict list — never overwritten.
- Provenance, source refs, evidence, counter-evidence,
  contradictions and origin survive in the memory
  (`data.origin`, `derived_from=[candidate_id]`).
- Idempotent: re-promoting returns the existing memory
  (`deduped: true`); fingerprint dedupe included.
- Revision fencing on every mutation (`expected_revision`).
- Emits `candidate.promoted` (also `.supported`, `.observed`,
  `.rejected`); visible in `/activity` and the morning.

The AI may recommend promotion. The human remains authority.

## UI

`/knowledge`: pipeline counts, filters (state/type), candidate
cards (title, summary, type, provenance, sources, evidence,
counter-evidence, entities, origin, supporters, truth, next
action) with Inspect (card) / Find evidence (search link) /
Research (queue) / Link (writes) / Promote / Reject / Keep.
Empty state explains the lifecycle with actions.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/LINUX_NODE_INSTALL.md">
# Mycelium Linux Node

Turn a Debian/Ubuntu-style laptop into a pull-only Mycelium node.
No root, no Docker, no cloud account, no inbound ports.

## Install

```bash
git clone <repo-url> mycelium-ai-main
cd mycelium-ai-main
./scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1
```

(If the execute bit got lost in transit: `bash
scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1`.)

This checks Python (>= 3.11) and git, creates `.venv`, installs the
project, probes Ollama/NVIDIA (both optional), and writes the local
config to `~/.config/mycelium/node.env` (chmod 600). Re-running is
safe: existing node id and token are always preserved.

Useful flags (all optional):

```bash
./scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1 --tier worker \
  --coordinator http://127.0.0.1:8000 --poll-seconds 5 \
  --capability node.status --capability inventory.read
./scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1 --with-systemd
./scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1 --bootstrap
```

`--bootstrap` performs the one-time registration + heartbeat against a
running coordinator. Without it, nothing touches the network.

## Configure

The installer owns `~/.config/mycelium/node.env`:

```text
MYCELIUM_COORDINATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
MYCELIUM_NODE_ID=linux-laptop-1
MYCELIUM_NODE_TIER=worker
MYCELIUM_NODE_TOKEN=<generated, never shown>
MYCELIUM_NODE_CAPABILITIES=node.status,research.fetch,inventory.read
MYCELIUM_NODE_POLL_SECONDS=10.0
```

First run generates the token (64 hex chars, same format as
`coordinator/app/nodes.py::generate_token`); later runs keep it.
First registration binds it server-side; afterwards the same token is
required for heartbeat and task claims. Rotate via the existing
`POST /api/v1/nodes/{id}/rotate-token` flow, never by reinstalling.

## Start

Manual:

```bash
source ~/.config/mycelium/node.env
.venv/bin/python -m node_client.main --coordinator "$MYCELIUM_COORDINATOR_URL" \
  --node-id "$MYCELIUM_NODE_ID" --tier worker \
  --capability node.status --capability research.fetch \
  --capability inventory.read --poll-seconds 10
```

As a user service (survives reboot, logs via journalctl):

```bash
./scripts/install_linux_node.sh --node-id linux-laptop-1 --with-systemd
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now mycelium-node
journalctl --user -u mycelium-node -f
```

## Check

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m node_client.install doctor
```

Shows OS / Python / Git / Config / Identity / Coordinator /
Registration / Heartbeat / Ollama / NVIDIA / Capabilities. Secrets are
never printed. The node is healthy when it appears under **Nodes** in
the coordinator UI (`http://127.0.0.1:8000/`) with status ONLINE.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Coordinator unreachable` | Start the coordinator first: `python -m uvicorn coordinator.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000` |
| `not registered yet` | Run install once with `--bootstrap`, or just start the node (it registers itself) |
| Node `STALE` in UI | No heartbeat for 60s: check the node process / `journalctl` |
| No tasks claimed | Task `required_capabilities` must be a subset of the node's; check `Capabilities` in doctor |
| `Ollama OPTIONAL` | Normal without Ollama; node still does status/inventory/fetch work |

Uninstall locally (server-side identity and audit are always kept):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m node_client.install uninstall
systemctl --user disable --now mycelium-node  # if enabled
```

## Security

- Outbound-only: the node polls (`register → heartbeat → claim →
  complete`); the coordinator never connects to the node, never sends
  shell commands. Only `system_inventory`, `desktop_screenshot` and
  `research.fetch_url` auto-execute; desktop input always needs explicit
  human approval and never runs in the claim loop.
- The token lives in one chmod-600 file and the process environment.
  It is never logged, never returned by any API, and only its salted
  hash is stored coordinator-side. Never commit it.
- Capabilities are fail-closed against the starter set
  (`coordinator/app/linux_node.py`): no wildcards, no shell, nothing
  the local executors cannot actually do.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/living-automation.md">
# Living Automation (BIG #38)

Mycelium's automation keeps the workshop going where work is
already safe and approved, and stops exactly where human
authority begins.

## Philosophy

```
Observe → Research → Propose → Wait-for-YES →
Act inside approved plan → Observe → Verify → Record
```

- **No new execution power**: automation uses only existing
  functions (research engine, missions executor, knowledge,
  camera, workshop, conversation intel, packets, notifications).
- **No background threads**: `drive` and `resume` are explicit
  calls from API buttons only.
- **Default-deny step kinds**: a closed allow-list; anything
  else refuses at creation AND at drive time.
- **Consequential work waits**: preparation steps create inert
  drafts/proposals and then the run WAITS with the exact gate
  named. Resume re-reads live store state — approvals are never
  fabricated, inferred, or reused stale.
- **Bounds on every run**: steps, runtime, retries, consecutive
  failures. Fail-closed with exact reasons.
- **Health content never enters candidates**: reuses
  `candidate_from_finding` gate.
- **Secrets never in payloads/packets**: reuses redaction +
  nodemesh hints.

## Step Kinds (Closed Allow-List)

### Read-Only (run freely, also overnight)
- `observe` — missions, candidates, research, nodes, inbox, events
- `readout` — project context, inventory search
- `search` — inventory GET-only bridge
- `research_queue` — queue a research question (draft)
- `research_execute` — execute a queued research run
- `conversation_analyze` — extractive intelligence
- `intel_analyze` — conversation intel summary
- `knowledge_candidate` — propose a candidate (ai-generated, unverified)
- `symbiosis_propose` — propose a connection candidate
- `craft_update` — compute craft tree gaps
- `context_packet` — build a bounded context packet
- `notify` — in-app notification fan-out
- `wait` — explicit pause with a gate

### Preparation (create inert drafts, then wait)
- `mission_propose` — draft mission (read-only steps only)
- `write_propose` — propose a controlled write
- `fab_prepare` — prepare/slice/propose a fabrication job
- `node_prepare` — prepare a node task (capability-routed)
- `camera_session` — run/describe/propose camera session
- `mission_tick` — tick an APPROVED mission only

## Gates (Closed Set)

Every `wait` step carries a gate. Resume re-checks the live store:

- `mission_approved` — mission status is `approved` or `running`
- `write_approved` — proposal status `approved`, decided by human
- `desktop_decided` — desktop action `approved`/`completed`
- `candidate_advanced` — candidate state `supported`/`promoted`
- `research_completed` — research run has dossier or completed
- `time_elapsed` — wall-clock wait until ISO timestamp

## Run Lifecycle

```
create_run(goal, steps, bounds?, overnight?, mission_id?, template_id?)
    → run_id, state="running"
drive_run(run_id, budget_steps=10)
    → executes safe steps until gate, bound, or completion
    → state: running | waiting_for_human | waiting_for_agent | blocked | failed | completed
resume_run(run_id, budget_steps=10)
    → re-checks ALL gates live, continues if met
cancel_run(run_id, reason)
    → terminal state "cancelled"
```

## Bounds (Validated at Creation)

| Bound | Default | Max |
|-------|---------|-----|
| max_steps | 10 | 20 |
| max_runtime_seconds | 600 | 3600 |
| max_retries | 2 | 5 |
| max_consecutive_failures | 3 | 5 |

Exceeding bounds → `blocked` or `failed` with exact reason.

## Overnight Eligibility

A run can be marked `overnight: true` only if ALL steps are in
`OVERNIGHT_SAFE_KINDS` (read-only research/analysis/candidate/
proposal/notify/wait). The night shift observes and prepares;
it never advances executable state.

## Templates

Three built-in templates (JSON + web form):

- `intel_to_research` — analyze conversation → queue research →
  candidate → notify (4 steps, overnight-safe)
- `observation_to_symbiosis` — observe candidates → propose
  symbiosis → craft update → notify (4 steps, overnight-safe)
- `missed_to_mission` — observe intel missed items → propose
  mission → wait for approval → tick (3 steps, NOT overnight)

## API Surface

```
GET  /api/v1/automation/templates
POST /api/v1/automation/from-template
POST /api/v1/automation/runs
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}
GET  /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/overnight
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/drive
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/resume
POST /api/v1/automation/runs/{run_id}/cancel
```

Web routes:
- `GET /automation` — overview + start from template
- `GET /automation/{run_id}` — quest trail, waiting bundle, actions

## Surfaces

- **Guide** (`/api/v1/guide`, `/guide`): waiting/blocked/failed
  automation items with WHAT/WHY/NEXT
- **Mobile** (`/api/v1/mobile/dashboard`, `/mobile`): automation
  quests in progress panel
- **Morning report** (`/api/v1/reports/morning`): automation
  section with runs, states, gates
- **Context packet** (`/api/v1/context/packet`, `packet2`):
  automation section with run_id, goal, state, waiting gate
- **Living state** (`/api/v1/state`): `automation_waiting`,
  `automation_running` counts

## Notifications

Reuses existing notify_center kinds:
- `mission_waiting` — run started, stops at first gate
- `research_finding` — research completed
- `task_completed` — run completed

## Decision Vocabulary

From `decisions.py`:
- `CONTINUE` — safe step done, drive next
- `RETRY` — step failed, within retries
- `REPLAN` — gate unmet, different path needed
- `WAITING_FOR_HUMAN` — gate needs human YES
- `WAITING_FOR_AGENT` — gate needs node/desktop
- `BLOCKED` — bounds exceeded
- `FAILED` — step failed, no retries left
- `COMPLETED` — all steps done
- `CANCELLED` — operator stop

## Security

See `docs/automation-security.md` for threat model, injection
defense, capability escalation refusal, and provenance discipline.

## REAL / TEST / SIMULATED / UNAVAILABLE

| Aspect | Label |
|--------|-------|
| Safe step execution | REAL |
| Gate re-check (live store) | REAL |
| Research queue/execute | REAL (provider REAL/TEST/UNAVAILABLE) |
| Mission propose/tick | REAL (tick only inside approved) |
| Write propose | REAL (inert proposal, human gate) |
| Node prepare | REAL (capability-routed, no execution) |
| Camera session | REAL (describe/propose), UNAVAILABLE (live Insta360) |
| Fab prepare | REAL (prepare/slice/propose), SIMULATED (execute) |
| Overnight runs | FUTURE (armed explicitly, no self-start) |
| Background threads | NEVER |
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/living-game-layer.md">
# Living Game Layer (BIG #43)

Terraria-like progression + solarpunk workshop + Ori-like
atmosphere — as a presentation layer over real Mycelium
state. Architecture first: every game concept is a VIEW over
existing stores. No XP, no rewards, no second database.

## Campaigns

`campaigns.py`: a campaign stores only title, description,
and ordered quest ids (`cmp_` + `campaigns` table). All
progress derives live via `quests.quest_detail`:

- per-quest states, completed/total/blocked/waiting counts
- current quest (first non-completed)
- next actionable item (first open step chain-wide, with
  its real href + readiness reason)
- evidence links (quest hrefs + progress)

Creating with an unknown quest id refuses; a deleted quest
renders as MISSING (never silently dropped, never invented).
Refresh audits via `campaign.updated`. API + `/campaigns`
page (trail chain ✓↓●↓○ with links) + morning CURRENT
CAMPAIGN section (only when campaigns exist) + mobile
campaign panel.

## Game state

`game.py::game_state()` composes one read-only view:
world (living state), campaigns, current quest (campaign
first, else first open quest), presence-as-stakes (same
items/hrefs/priority, game framing words, original band kept
on each item), craft (quest-linked entities), symbiosis
(open proposals as seedlings), nodes (awake/quiet),
energy, workshop (fabrication activity), discoveries.
Failing sources degrade to explicit empty. Served at
`GET /api/v1/game/state` (GET only — POST is 405) and
rendered at `/game`. The game layer approves nothing and
executes nothing.

## Symbiosis as progression

Display only: VERIFIED reads strong, SUPPORTED growing,
PROPOSED a seedling (uncertain until reviewed). Strength
bars on the symbiosis page, legend panel, seedling wording
in the game view. States never promote silently.

## Craft as gameplay

The craft tree keeps its evidence-backed states; the page
gains game framing (what ✓/!/○ mean, campaign and game-view
cross-links) and the game view shows quest-linked chains
with stage glyphs.

## Living world

`living_bg()` gains five clamped signals from real stores:
research (flow quickens), fresh candidates (discovery
pulse), verified links (faint mycelium threads), active
fabrication (warm spores), offline nodes (field dims).
Single rAF loop, same reduced-motion early return, subtle
by design. Motion never claims specific events happened.

## Visual identity

Original solarpunk-workshop accents in `ui.py`: pixel-step
corners, solar/leaf marks, quest-trail chain, campaign
cards, strength bars, companion blocks on guide cards.
Warm soil/moss/amber/spore palette (already the house
style). Usability primary; no copied artwork.

## Guide companion

Guide items gain BLOCKED BY / UNLOCKS / EVIDENCE (real
label+href pairs, rendered only when present), plus
campaign-context cards (🗺 WHAT/WHY/NEXT/BLOCKED
BY/UNLOCKS/EVIDENCE over the live chain). No hallucinated
advice — every link opens a real record.

## Labels

Campaigns/quests/craft/symbiosis/stakes: REAL derived
state. Background motion: ambient, not data. Printer
transport: UNAVAILABLE. Fab execution: SIMULATED. WEB_PUSH:
UNAVAILABLE. Energy-aware routing: FUTURE.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/living-principles.md">
# Living Principles

These principles are the decision compass for Mycelium AI. They are derived from the [origin story](origin_story.md), not a marketing layer added afterwards. A contribution that conflicts with them needs an explicit discussion.

1. **Waste is a resource in the wrong place.** Prefer repair, reuse and modest requirements over premature replacement.
2. **Hardware deserves a second life.** A useful feature must remain usable on old laptops, mini PCs and low-power devices whenever practical.
3. **Technology should increase autonomy.** A local community must retain meaningful control over its data, tools and ability to repair them.
4. **Knowledge should be open and shareable where responsible.** Keep provenance, consent, privacy and licences intact.
5. **Energy is a real constraint.** Make consumption visible; defer non-urgent work when power is scarce and always allow a person to override automation.
6. **Local-first is a capability.** The system should continue to serve a local purpose when the internet or a cloud provider disappears.
7. **Technology supports life.** Measure success by the benefit to people, animals and ecosystems—not merely throughput, novelty or growth.

## A practical decision check

Before merging a meaningful feature, ask:

- Does it solve a real local problem more simply than the alternative?
- Can someone in a small community install, understand and repair it?
- Does it introduce a new dependency, data exposure or energy cost?
- Is there a safe offline and low-resource path?

The answer does not need to be perfect. It does need to be visible.
</file>

# Living Solarpunk World (BIG #44)

The workshop as a place: original pixel-solarpunk visuals
over real Mycelium state. Architecture stays authoritative;
every visual object maps to a real record or derived state,
every object links somewhere real, empty stores render
empty. No XP, no scores, no invented activity.

## World objects

`world.py`: NODE, PROJECT, MACHINE, ENERGY, CAMPAIGN,
CRAFT, DISCOVERY, SYMBIOSIS, RESEARCH, PRESENCE — each with
glyph + words (never icon-only), state, activity,
attention, trust where applicable, href, and an accessible
text line. Collectors are bounded and best-effort; unknown
kinds fall back to PRESENCE rather than inventing a shape.

- Nodes: awake/quiet, connected hardware counts, VERIFIED /
  OBSERVED / ADVERTISED trust (quiet nodes never read
  verified), current task or idle/quiet activity, telemetry
  freshness.
- Campaigns: live counts, current quest, next action,
  blocked marker.
- Energy: only with records; solar ☀ flow, battery 🔋
  store, machine ⚙ activity, grid 🔌 link; UNKNOWN stays
  a word, never a zero.
- Discoveries: open proposals as seedlings (uncertain until
  reviewed). Research: dossiers with open-question counts.

## HUD

`world_hud()`: campaign, quest, attention counts, nodes
awake/total, busy nodes, open discoveries — live store
counts, never scores. Rendered on `/world` (hud-cell row)
and `/mobile` (World block, shared NOW/WAITING/AVAILABLE/
DISCOVERED/OFFLINE vocabulary).

## Symbiosis network

`symbiosis_network(entity)`: PROJECT root with branch
children grouped ENERGY/MACHINE/MATERIAL/FINANCE/…,
each with state, strength (established/growing/seedling),
predicate and world href. Without a focus entity the world
shows open seedlings. Display only — statuses never change
here.

## Craft world

Vertical IDEA→…→PROJECT chain for the focused entity with
✓/●/○/! evidence states from `stage_states`. Completion is
never invented.

## Living background

Two new clamped signals join the existing five: solar
production records lift bright energy spores; presence
NEEDS tint a few spores amber as subtle world emphasis.
One rAF loop, same reduced-motion early return, same
ambient honesty.

## Graph glow

Hardware overlay nodes already carry `verified` from the
human-link store (BIG #43); the graph renderer now draws
them with a thicker stroke, glow ring and `verified-glow`
class. Verified connections read stronger; advertised ones
never do.

## Guide as explanation

Quiet/offline node cards carry last heartbeat, last known
task, what restores availability, and evidence links (node
reality + /nodes). The world links "Why? Ask the guide";
reasoning lives in the guide, not the world.

## Labels

World objects/HUD/network/craft/energy/stakes: REAL derived
state. Background motion: ambient, not data. Printer
transport: UNAVAILABLE. Fab execution: SIMULATED. WEB_PUSH:
UNAVAILABLE. Energy-aware routing: FUTURE (explicitly not
implemented here).
</file>

# Living Workshop (BIG #10)

Eén werkplaats-beeld: uniforme wereldgrafiek + interactieve
workshop-UI + 3D-foundation met transform-voorstellen.
INVENTory blijft de bron van de waarheid; alles anders is
een projectie (overlay), nooit een tweede waarheid.

## Uniforme wereldgrafiek

`build_world_graph` legt overlays over de INVENTory-grafiek:

- missies en agent-nodes (bestaand, BIG #4)
- camera-observaties en fabrications (bestaand)
- **registry-nodes** (`type: node`) en **printers**
  (`type: printer`) — nieuw in BIG #10, alleen tellen en
  korte labels, geen dumps

Elke overlay is begrensd (MAX_NODES/EDGES) en faalt
afzonderlijk zonder de basisgrafiek te breken.
`GET /api/v1/world/graph` serveert het geheel; de
interactieve pagina staat op `/workshop/graph`.

## Workshop-pagina's (server-rendered, geen framework)

- `/workshop` — overzicht: taken, fabrications, grafiek-
  ingang, 3D-ingang
- `/workshop/graph` — entity/depth-formulier + node/edge-
  tellingen met overlay-herkomst
- `/workshop/3d` — mesh-preview, transform-voorstel
  (scale/translate/rotate/mirror, factor-begrensd),
  optioneel lokaal persisteren als werkbestand

## 3D-transform als voorstel

`POST /api/v1/fab/transform` geeft altijd eerst een
preview (driehoeken afgekapt, geen verrassingen). Met
`persist: true` ontstaat een lokaal afgeleid STL-werkbestand
(`fab-derived-*`), direct gevalideerd. Registratie in
INVENTory loopt daarna nog steeds via de BIG #5
file-proposal-flow — een werkbestand is geen bewijs, geen
printopdracht, geen waarheid.

## Toekomst-domeinen (alleen extensiepunten)

`GET /api/v1/domains` somt `health`, `skills`, `ingestion`
op als gecontracteerde placeholders: naam, status,
capabilities, expliciete `requirements`-tekst. Geen
Garmin/Instagram/native apps, geen CAD-kernel, geen
printer-SDK — alleen de plek waar zo'n domein later mag
landen zonder de kern te breken.

# Memory (BIG #11-15, Phase 1) — IMPLEMENTED

Ten typed memories over the event/state architecture, never
one text blob: fact, episodic, project, preference, skill,
health, observation, research, relationship, derived.

## Truth tiers

`user_fact > verified > observed > external_source >
ai_inference > ai_suggestion`. AI output enters at the
bottom and never auto-promotes: `verify_memory` needs a
human approver plus human_verified provenance. Deletion is
a tombstone (row + links preserved).

## Retrieval

Lexical + recency + importance + project relevance, with an
optional semantic re-rank over the shortlist through the
existing Ollama embedding provider (lexical stays the
fallback; no second search engine). Bounded, budgeted.

## Consolidation — PARTIAL (proposal only)

`propose_consolidation` returns candidates + dedup count +
structural contradiction flags and stores nothing.
Contradictions stay side by side for human review. The
periodic scheduled run exists as a job (`memory_
consolidation`) but proposes; automatic merging is FUTURE
and must keep the no-silent-overwrite rule.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/mission-templates.md">
# Mission templates V2 (BIG #42)

Reusable mission chains built ONLY on existing mission /
approval / task infrastructure. Templates compose safe
operations; they never bypass gates.

## New templates

- `idea_to_verification` (10 steps): readout (idea) →
  research → analysis (candidate) → proposal (project) →
  readout (materials) → analysis (node choice) → fabricate →
  camera_observe → analysis (verification). Fabrication and
  observation start only after explicit mission approval, as
  with any hand-built mission.
- `project_finance_energy` (5 steps): readout (project) →
  analysis (finance) → analysis (energy) → research (gap) →
  proposal (next action). No automatic bookings, no invented
  measurements — unknown stays UNKNOWN.

## Guarantees

- Every step kind is an existing `VALID_STEP_KINDS` member
  (asserted in tests); instantiation runs the same mission
  validation as hand-built missions.
- No generic workflow executor exists: the catalogue is
  closed (8 templates), placeholders are plain `{goal}`
  substitution, consequential steps keep their YES gates.
- Quest states: template-driven missions surface in quest
  trails like any other mission (READY/ACTIVE/WAITING/
  BLOCKED/COMPLETED/FAILED derived from live records).

## Bounded mesh workflows

`POST /api/v1/workflows/preview` (dry run, creates nothing)
and `POST /api/v1/workflows/dispatch` (max 6 steps) chain
pinned mesh delegations — research on Node A, camera work on
Node B, compute on Node C — through the existing task queue:
validate → auth → eligibility precheck → create → assign per
step, coordinator authoritative, nodes pull-based. A failed
step stops the workflow; queued steps keep their own
lease/claim lifecycle and stay visible (never silently
dropped). Same closed contracts as `/mesh/delegate`: no
wildcards, no shell, no secrets, no target drift.
</file>

# Mobile Mycelium (BIG #36)

The phone is the living command surface of Mycelium — a
surface over the coordinator, not a second application.
`/mobile` answers "What can I do right now?" and "Is
Mycelium waiting for me?" from live backend state only.

## Home order (small screens first)

NOW → WAITING FOR YOU → ACTIVE → INPUT → GUIDE ME →
how-it-works → CAMERA → CONTINUE ELSEWHERE → CRAFT →
SYMBIOSIS → NODES → RECENT → remember/queue → workbench →
status. Same backend and gates as desktop.

## Input lifecycle

"Wat wil je doen?" posts to `/web/chat` (the existing
coordinator entry). Quick actions link existing routes.
State shown: INPUT → PROCESSING → NODE → RESULT, with
RESULT in events/activity and NEEDS YOU pointing at YES
buttons. Oversized input refuses with a redirect, never a
500.

## Approval triage

`approval_cards()` unifies desktop actions, write proposals
and missions into cards with WHAT / WHY / SOURCE / SCOPE /
what YES does / what YES does NOT do. Actions: YES and NO
post to the existing gates (`/web/desktop/.../decision`,
`/web/writes/.../approve`, `/web/missions/.../approve|...`);
OPEN links the detail page; DEFER is an honest non-action
(open later, nothing changes). Replayed YES is harmless
(idempotent states); wrong response text never approves.

## Notifications

IN_APP only (`notification_cards()` + `?node=` per-node
view). Every notification carries a deeplink computed from
`related_mission` / `related_entity` / `related_task` or its
type (approval→agents, candidate→knowledge,
research→research, camera→cameras, connection→symbiosis,
fabrication→fabrication, nodes→nodes, morning→morning).
Tapping opens the real object. WEB_PUSH stays UNAVAILABLE
(capability endpoint says so).

## Camera from the phone

Counts (inbox/sessions/observations/waiting candidates) +
the honest chain FILE → SESSION → OBSERVATION → DESCRIBE →
REVIEW → CANDIDATE → LINK → YES, with Insta360 live
transport labeled UNAVAILABLE and the inbox as the real
path. No native upload is claimed.

## Continue elsewhere

CONTINUE ELSEWHERE surfaces the existing packet-v2: goal,
missions, entities, memories, open questions + COPY PACKET
(Markdown), JSON and continuation links, plus the 3D
packet. Models work; Mycelium keeps state; no secrets
inside. Works across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Codex,
OpenCode, Ollama.

## Guide, craft, symbiosis, nodes, progress

- GUIDE ME: live guide cards (kind/glyph/what/why/next).
- CRAFT: presence checklists with ✓/○ linking to craft
  trees.
- SYMBIOSIS: PROPOSED items with WHY/SOURCE/STATUS;
  YES runs the guarded knowledge flow.
- NODES: status + WHAT IT CAN DO + the
  PHONE→COORDINATOR→NODE(S) mesh path (read-only BIG37
  prep; coordinator authoritative, no shell, no wildcard).
- ACTIVE: quest progress from mission/fab-job states only.

## Notifier (OpenCode/terminal)

`scripts/mycelium-notify.py` now covers the full run
lifecycle: `start`, `status` (PROGRESS), `need`/`waiting`
(WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL), `done`, `failed`. Terminal bell +
OSC 9/99 + ASCII fallback; no service, no credentials.
Long-term: OpenCode → Mycelium event → notification →
phone/web shows "Approval required" (IN_APP; no web push
needed).

## Security

Mobile shares desktop boundaries exactly: same gates, same
exact YES, same validation. Tested: fake notification/
mission/approval/entity IDs, unauthorized + replayed YES,
malformed packet, oversized input, hostile content (escaped
on render), traversal, unknown camera ids.

## REAL / TEST / SIMULATED / UNAVAILABLE

REAL: dashboard, triage, deeplinks, camera counts, packet
handoff, guide/craft/symbiosis/nodes/progress panels,
IN_APP notifications. TEST: synthetic adapters (labeled).
SIMULATED: printers (unchanged). UNAVAILABLE: web push,
Insta360 live transport, native upload, STT.
</file>

# Mycelium V1 (BIG #23–#28)

First genuinely usable Mycelium: open it, ask in plain Dutch,
watch it work safely until it needs you.

## What Jelles can do from the Command Center (/world)

Type plain language. Deterministic routing (never the LLM)
maps it to one brain — the existing chat endpoint — plus safe
actions:

| Say | Happens |
|---|---|
| “Onderzoek mijn camper.” | Research mission (read-only template) → pending YES → runs to next gate |
| “Kijk wat er nog openstaat voor INVENTory.” | INVENTory research mission |
| “Maak een overzicht van mijn lopende projecten.” | Project-overview mission |
| “Wat heb je vannacht gevonden?” | Morning report (did / discoveries / waiting / agenda / health) |
| “Controleer mijn openstaande missions.” | Mission cards with exact wait reasons |
| “Wat staat er vandaag op mijn agenda?” | Upcoming ICS events |
| “Stop.” | Pauses/cancels running missions safely |
| “Ga verder…” | Resumes read-only-safe missions via the bounded loop |

API twin: `POST /api/v1/command`.

## What Mycelium does automatically

Read-only plan steps (project/git/INVENTory readouts, local
analysis when Ollama answers), bounded retries with backoff,
explicit CONTINUE/RETRY/REPLAN/WAIT decisions, episodic
memories on terminal states, startup recovery scan,
research-candidate follow-ups. Morning report summarizes it
all in a warm tone.

## What still requires Jelles

Every YES: plan approval, desktop input (per action),
writes, proposals, prints, robot/drone moves, credentials,
publishing, purchases, outreach. Voice never approves
physical actions. Stale approvals never reused after restart.

## Status honesty

REAL: chat→mission→tick→observe→decide→memory chain,
screenshot observations (approved), ICS agenda import,
bootstrap idempotency, recovery scan, mission cards.
SIMULATED: printer pipeline (metadata only). TEST: camera
fixtures. UNAVAILABLE: Garmin (no OAuth, honestly reported),
live web research (no transport — missions wait instead of
faking), n8n auto-install (disk-space discipline; system
useful without it). FUTURE: UI grounding/OCR layer,
research-node routing, voice/vision wearables.

## Pages

/world (Command Center) · /missions (+ cards) · /projects ·
/memory · /research · /morning · /agenda · /devices ·
/workshop · /fabrication · /physical (via API matrix) ·
/integrations (n8n plane) · /mobile
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/nutrition.md">
# Nutrition (BIG #11-15, Phase 2) — IMPLEMENTED

MEAL → INGREDIENT → PORTION → NUTRIENT → DAILY TOTAL →
WEEKLY TREND over an extensible nutrient model (21
nutrients: macros, micros, vegan-critical B12/iron/
iodine/omega-3). No giant hardcoded food database; foods
are user/recipe/label entries with per-100g profiles.

## Rules

- AI may propose values (`ai_proposal` source), but source
  and verification stay visible on every number.
- Vegan-first with explicit evidence: `vegan`/`non_vegan`
  claims require an ingredient/label/source note; a meal
  folds to its weakest claim (unknown beats vegan).
- Coverage answers only adequate/possibly low/possibly
  high/unknown against configurable reference targets,
  always showing source, population/context,
  calculation and uncertainty. Illustrative defaults are
  labelled as such and overridable per call.
</file>

# The conversation where Mycelium AI began

> Preserved transcript of the conversation that gave the project its direction.
> It contains character-encoding artefacts from the copied chat; they are intentionally left intact for provenance and can be cleaned later from a better source copy.

wat is er allemaal nodig om mijn eigen llm of kleiner model te maken om zelf lokaal te runnen en hoe kan ik het beste computers, laptops, smartphones, tablets, rasberry pi's te verbinden om samen workloads te verminderen

Dat is een interessant project, en het is zeker haalbaar. Je hoeft niet direct een gigantisch model zoals GPT-4 of Llama 3 405B te bouwen. Voor de meeste hobby- en professionele toepassingen is het veel realistischer om:

GPT-achtig model vanaf nul	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	miljoenen euro's aan hardware

Voor de meeste mensen is een combinatie van Llama, Qwen, Gemma of Mistral met eigen training de beste keuze.

Bij heterogene apparaten (zoals telefoons en Raspberry Pi's) is dit vooral geschikt voor lichte taken, omdat de traagste apparaten de totale snelheid kunnen beperken.

Mijn aanbeveling

Als je serieus een lokaal AI-platform wilt bouwen, zou ik beginnen met:

Één krachtige AI-server (Ryzen 9 of Threadripper, 128 GB RAM, RTX 4090 of beter).
Een 10 Gbit-netwerk voor snelle gegevensuitwisseling.
Een NAS voor datasets, modellen en back-ups.
Ollama of vLLM om modellen lokaal te draaien.
LoRA/QLoRA om bestaande open modellen aan jouw eigen data aan te passen.
Ray of DeepSpeed zodra je meerdere GPU-machines wilt laten samenwerken.

Daarmee krijg je veel meer rendement dan door veel zwakkere apparaten te combineren. Een Raspberry Pi, smartphone of tablet kan wel waardevol zijn voor ondersteunende taken (monitoring, data verzamelen, edge-inferentie of taakverdeling), maar zal een krachtige GPU nauwelijks ontlasten bij het trainen van een LLM.

Als je ambitie hebt om echt een eigen lokaal AI-cluster te bouwen, kan ik ook een complete architectuur ontwerpen (hardware, netwerk, software en taakverdeling) die schaalbaar is van ongeveer €2.000 tot een professioneel cluster van €25.000 of meer.

Dankjewel dat je dit deelt. Er zitten eigenlijk twee verschillende dingen in je verhaal.

Het eerste is dat je een sterke morele reactie hebt op hoe de wereld nu werkt. Het tweede is dat je daar niet alleen boos of verdrietig over wilt zijn, maar er iets constructiefs tegenover wilt zetten. Dat tweede vind ik belangrijk, omdat het richting geeft.

Je noemde ook dat je op de dag van die beslissing aan zelfmoord dacht. Ik ben blij om te lezen dat je erbij zegt dat dit nu niet speelt. Als dat ooit weer verandert of die gedachten terugkomen, hoop ik dat je er niet alleen mee blijft lopen maar iemand erbij betrekt die je vertrouwt of professionele hulp inschakelt. Je hoeft zulke momenten niet alleen te dragen.

Wat mij opvalt, is dat je woorden gebruikt als:

afval

lokale gemeenschappen

# Mycelium AI - Project Genesis

Je helpt mij een langdurig open-source project te bouwen genaamd:

MYCELIUM AI

Het doel is een solarpunk, gedistribueerd AI-ecosysteem bouwen waarin afgedankte hardware, duurzame energie, lokale productie en open kennis samenkomen.

## Kernidee

Mycelium AI is geïnspireerd door natuurlijke myceliumnetwerken: veel kleine verbonden onderdelen die samen een veerkrachtig geheel vormen.

Het project probeert niet de grootste AI ter wereld te bouwen.

Het doel is:

- lokale gemeenschappen versterken;
- afhankelijkheid van gecentraliseerde Big Tech verminderen;
- oude hardware een tweede leven geven;
- AI toegankelijk maken;
- kennis lokaal beschikbaar maken;
- duurzame energie optimaal benutten;
- technologie inzetten voor mens, dier en ecosysteem.

## Filosofie

Ontwerpbeslissingen moeten zoveel mogelijk voldoen aan deze principes:

1. Afval is een grondstof op de verkeerde plek.
2. Hardware verdient een tweede leven.
3. Technologie moet autonomie vergroten.
4. Kennis moet zoveel mogelijk open en deelbaar zijn.
5. Energiegebruik moet bewust en duurzaam gepland worden.
6. Lokale systemen moeten kunnen functioneren zonder constante afhankelijkheid van centrale diensten.
7. Technologie moet het leven ondersteunen.

## Eerste technische visie

Het systeem bestaat uit verschillende soorten nodes:

### Seed Nodes
Kleine apparaten zoals Raspberry Pi's, oude laptops en mini-pc's.

Taken:
- monitoring;
- lokale API's;
- taakverdeling;
- lichte AI;
- sensoren.

### Worker Nodes
Sterkere apparaten.

Taken:
- scraping;
- OCR;
- transcriptie;
- data-analyse;
- embeddings;
- vectorisatie;
- modelondersteuning.

### Core Nodes
Krachtige systemen of gehuurde GPU-cloud.

Taken:
- modeltraining;
- zware inferentie;
- fine-tuning.

## Belangrijke eigenschappen

Het netwerk moet:

- hardware automatisch kunnen herkennen;
- taken kunnen verdelen op basis van capaciteit;
- energiegebruik kunnen meenemen;
- offline/local-first kunnen werken;
- modulair uitbreidbaar zijn.

## Mogelijke toekomstige toepassingen

- lokale AI-assistenten;
- circulaire economie;
- recyclingprojecten;
- 3D-print filament uit gerecycled plastic;
- lokale voedsel- en landbouwkennis;
- waterkwaliteit monitoring;
- energiebeheer;
- onderwijs;
- makerspaces.

## Eerste ontwikkelfase

Begin klein.

Bouw eerst:

1. Een centrale repository structuur.
2. Documentatie.
3. Een simpele node-client.
4. Een coordinator/server.
5. Een systeem waarmee nodes zichzelf aanmelden.
6. Een taakverdelingssysteem.
7. Logging en monitoring.

Gebruik voorlopig eenvoudige, onderhoudbare technologie.

Voorkeur:
- Python
- Docker
- Linux
- SQLite/PostgreSQL
- FastAPI
- eenvoudige webinterface

## Belangrijk

Help mij niet alleen code schrijven.

Denk mee als technische medeoprichter.

Vraag:
- waarom bouwen we dit?
- is dit de eenvoudigste oplossing?
- past dit bij de filosofie?
- kunnen we dit toegankelijk maken voor mensen zonder technische achtergrond?

Maak keuzes die een kleine gemeenschap thuis kan uitvoeren.

De eerste versie hoeft niet indrukwekkend te zijn.

De eerste versie moet bestaan.

En nog één ding, speciaal voor jou.

Bewaar alsjeblieft ook de menselijke kant van dit moment. Niet alleen de technische ideeën. De reden waarom dit project betekenis kreeg, is niet omdat er een slimme architectuur voor een AI-cluster bedacht werd. Het begon bij iemand die naar de wereld keek, daar pijn over voelde, en besloot om niet alleen boos te blijven maar iets te bouwen.

Dat is waardevolle informatie voor een project.

Misschien wordt dit ooit een README. Misschien een documentaire. Misschien blijft het gewoon een persoonlijk experiment. Alle drie zijn prima.

En nog even terugkomend op wat je eerder schreef over die zware gedachten: ik ben echt blij dat je hier nu zit en over bouwen praat. Mocht zo'n moment ooit weer terugkomen waarin het te donker wordt, probeer dan alsjeblieft niet alleen met die gedachte te blijven zitten — zoek iemand in je omgeving op of neem contact op met hulp. In Nederland kun je bijvoorbeeld ook 113 Zelfmoordpreventie bereiken via 113 of 0800-0113.
