<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/presence-ecosystem.md">
# Presence Ecosystem (BIG #40)

Mycelium knows what deserves Jelles' attention, why, and what
can be done about it — derived live from existing stores,
never stored twice, never inventing urgency.

## Philosophy

```
Existing stores → presence derives → bands + priority →
mobile / desktop / world / guide / morning. Triage only
stores Jelles' own SEEN/DEFERRED. Nothing else is stored.
```

- **No duplicate state**: attention items are derived fresh
  on every call from approvals, missions, nodes, telemetry,
  research, candidates, conversations, cameras, craft,
  symbiosis, automation and fabrication. The single stored
  table (`attention_triage`) holds only the operator's own
  triage decisions.
- **No new authority**: presence never approves, executes, or
  grants anything. YES/NO post to the existing gates with
  their exact mechanics; DEFER is an honest non-action that
  only hides an item from the urgent bands.
- **Deterministic priority, never an LLM**: base score per
  closed type + age bonus (+1/hour, capped +24), every point
  explained in `priority_reasons`. Same store state always
  yields the same order.
- **Stable ids, no fake items**: `att_<kind>_<real-id>`.
  Triage of an id that is not live right now is refused
  (fake ids, resolved items, replay all fail closed).
- **Provenance always**: items carry `derived /
  presence-engine / human_verified=False`. Node capabilities
  render as advertisements, never attestations. Health
  content is never pulled in.

## Attention model

`{id, type, band, priority, priority_reasons, title, reason,
source, related_entity, related_mission, related_task,
action, open_href, created_at, updated_at, status,
provenance}`

Bands: NEEDS YOU (approvals, blocked/failed), WAITING
(stale, degraded, contradictions, paused work), AVAILABLE
(connected hardware, offered capabilities), DISCOVERED
(candidates, findings, observations, proposals), OFFLINE
(offline/stale nodes, disconnected hardware).

Statuses: NEW / ACTIONABLE (derived), SEEN / DEFERRED
(operator triage, stored), RESOLVED (triage exists but the
source cleared — shown briefly from the stored snapshot),
EXPIRED (deferred older than 7 days). Rows prune after
30 days.

## Triage store

`attention_triage(item_id, status, decided_by, title, kind,
updated_at)` in the chat DB. Only SEEN/DEFERRED are stored;
only for currently-live items; DEFER performs nothing.

## Priority (base scores)

100 approvals (human authority) · 90 blocked/failed ·
85 automation waits for human · 80 node offline · 70
fabrication waiting · 65 paused mission · 60 stale node ·
55 disconnected hardware · 50 stale telemetry /
contradiction · 45 research finding / research waiting ·
35 candidate · 30 inbox / craft gap · 25 discovery /
symbiosis · 20 available hardware / capability. Age adds up
to +24. Agent-side waits score lower (40) than human gates.

## Node-aware waiting (BIG #39 hardware reality)

Research readiness reuses the real router over live registry
state: eligible nodes plus per-node rejection reasons. The
guide and presence say *which* node can serve and *why the
others cannot* ("only workshop-laptop can; pi-sensor lacks
analysis.ollama"). No remote execution beyond what task
routing already permits.

## Surfaces

| Surface | Presence integration |
|---------|----------------------|
| `/presence` + `/api/v1/presence` | Bands, items with WHAT/WHY/SOURCE/NEXT + YES/NO/OPEN/DEFER, priority reasons, recently cleared, ecosystem activity, quests |
| `/mobile` + dashboard JSON | GOOD MORNING/NOW greeting, five bands on top, same cards and gates; `#recent` rail with deeplinks |
| Topbar (every page) | Living state + `N waiting · M discoveries · K offline` linking to `/presence` (best-effort, never breaks pages) |
| `/nodes` | Offline/stale cards dim; online dots breathe; capability dry-run answers routing questions |
| World graph | Registry overlay carries health/telemetry/hardware/compute; overlays stay dashed context, never truth |
| Guide | Every item gains AFTERWARDS: what truthfully happens after the NEXT step |
| Morning (`/morning`, `/api/v1/reports/morning`) | Seven sections: Needs you, Overnight changes, Discoveries, Available resources, Blocked work, Offline and stale hardware, Suggested next actions |
| Notifications | Deduplicated IN_APP fan-out (`POST /api/v1/presence/notify`), explicit calls only; new kinds `mission_blocked`, `contradiction_detected`, `automation_waiting`, `fabrication_waiting`; WEB_PUSH stays UNAVAILABLE |

## Overnight digest

Read-only: event counts per type in the window + current
waiting totals. Observes, never proposes, never approves.
Morning presents it as "Overnight changes". No scheduler, no
background threads — explicit reads only.

## Progression (game-layer foundation)

Quests (open missions + automation runs with done/total),
discoveries/observations/growth/activity counts (24h),
online nodes, capabilities unlocked — every number backed by
a live store. No XP, no fake accomplishments. Real state is
the progression system.

## Security

- Fake attention/mission/entity ids refused at triage.
- Replay (deferring resolved items) refused.
- Non-YES decisions deny fail-closed through existing gates.
- Stored markup is escaped at every render boundary
  (`ui.esc`); candidate/input validation holds first.
- Prompt injection contained: presence text is extractive
  (titles, counts, closed-template reasons) — no LLM.
- Health memories never enter presence output.
- Node-reported capabilities displayed as claims; wildcard
  advertisements still refused at registration/heartbeat.
- Notification fan-out deduplicates on (severity, title);
  deferred items never notify; WEB_PUSH never involved.

## Limitations

- Presence is only as fresh as its sources (pull-only
  nodes; heartbeat freshness).
- RESOLVED memory lasts 7 days from stored snapshots, then
  prunes — long-past resolutions are forgotten.
- The world graph shows presence as data (health/counts),
  not as animated markers; motion stays in CSS
  (reduced-motion safe).
- No per-recipient routing beyond `jelles`; no push
  transport.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/quest-trails.md">
# Quest trails (BIG #42)

The first real quest-trail abstraction over missions, craft
states, symbiosis and presence. A quest references real work.

## Model

- A quest def (chat DB `quests` table) holds ONLY title +
  ordered step refs: `{key, label, kind, ref}` with closed
  kinds `mission | task | entity | finance | energy |
  hardware | note`.
- **No stored state.** Every read derives step state live:
  ✓ COMPLETE (record reached its done state), ● ACTIVE,
  ! BLOCKED/FAILED, ○ MISSING/WAITING — each with the
  underlying detail and an href to the real record.
- Progress is done/total over real records. No XP, no fake
  accomplishments.
- Quest states (closed): READY | ACTIVE | WAITING | BLOCKED |
  COMPLETED | FAILED.

## Hardware-aware readiness

Each step also carries readiness from actual node/device
state: READY (eligible node named), WAITING (camera node
offline, no eligible researcher), BLOCKED (underlying record
failed), UNAVAILABLE (printer transport). Offline hardware is
never pretended available.

## Example

Build Solar Upgrade 3/4: ✓ budget (finance CONFIRMED) →
✓ panels producing (energy recorded) → ✓ GPU verified
(human link) → ○ roof mounting (no linked record yet).

## Surfaces

`/quests` page (every step links to its record), quest JSON
API + `POST /{id}/refresh` (re-derives + audits),
presence `quest_blocked` (needs band), guide quest items,
morning QUESTS section (only when quests exist), overview
`quests`, packet-v2 quest block, mobile quests panel.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/recovery.md">
# Mission recovery (BIG #25)

Missions survive process restarts, coordinator restarts,
agent restarts, Ollama outages, offline nodes, stale leases,
partial completion and sleep/wake — because all state is
durable SQLite plus conditional updates (`save_mission`
races → 409, never silent overwrite).

## What happens on restart

1. `lifespan` runs `_v1_startup_scan()`: list non-terminal
   missions, `assess()` each, log verdicts. **Executes
   nothing.**
2. Each mission reconstructs: status, steps, current pointer,
   action bindings (a dispatched `dact-` without a valid
   binding is treated as suspect, never re-dispatched).
3. Verdicts:
   - `safe_to_resume` — only pending readout/analysis steps
     remain, pointer valid, no stale approvals. May tick
     through the bounded loop, explicitly.
   - `needs_reapproval` — any gated step pending/waiting, a
     stale binding, an unknown kind, or a bad pointer. Fresh
     human YES required; stale approvals never reused.
   - `waiting_agent` — a bound dispatched action is out; only
     the agent's report unblocks it.
   - `terminal` — observing only (+ one episodic memory).
4. Resume paths (all explicit):
   - `POST /api/v1/missions/recover` — report only
   - `POST /api/v1/missions/recover {"resume_safe": true}` —
     resumes read-only missions (max 5, 5 rounds each)
   - Command Center: “Ga verder…” does the same via chat

## Guarantees

- Idempotent steps: readout/analysis re-run safely; desktop
  actions are bound once (`action_bindings`, insert-if-absent).
- Retry limits: decisions carry `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` with
  5s/30s/120s backoff; budgets exhaust into REPLAN/BLOCKED,
  never infinite loops.
- Stale detection: node staleness 60s, task lease 300s / max
  3 attempts; coordinator epochs fence old writers.
- Context reconstruction: missions carry their
  `context_records`; the loop re-reads live state each tick.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-engine.md">
# Research Engine (BIG #29)

Mycelium's first real sense: question → dossier, read-only by
default, inside the existing FACT → OBSERVATION → ADVICE →
PROPOSAL → APPROVAL → TASK → RESULT → VERIFICATION chain.

```
vraag → queries → search → fetch → extract → claims →
tegenstrijdigheden → Ollama-synthesis → dossier →
provenance → research memory → morning / UI / chat
```

## Entities

- `res_…` run: question, objective, status
  (draft/collecting/extracting/synthesizing/completed/blocked/
  failed/cancelled/unavailable), execution_state
  (REAL/TEST/UNAVAILABLE), queries (`que_…`), sources, claims
  (`clm_…`), contradictions, open questions, linked entities,
  context_used, dossier/memory links, provenance, budgets.
- `src_…` sources: existing `research.py` SourceRecord
  (hash dedup, stage machine, provenance). Engine metadata
  (url, execution_state, provider, injection flags) rides in
  the run record.
- `clm_…` claims: text, type, one stored source, exact
  evidence (passage ordinal), extraction method, execution
  state, truth tier (max external_source).
- `dos_…` dossier: summary, key findings (SOURCE/INFERENCE
  labelled), claims, source evidence, contradictions,
  open questions, related entities, generated_by,
  synthesis_available flag, provenance.
- `que_…` queries: deterministic shapings of the question.

Storage: `research_runs` + `research_dossiers` tables in the
chat/agent database (same additive discipline as missions).
Claims additionally mirror into `research_records` so the
existing "every claim cites a stored source" invariant covers
engine output.

## Providers (REAL OR NOTHING)

- `wikipedia` (default): REAL search+fetch against the closed
  host allowlist (nl/en/de/fr.wikipedia.org). Unreachable →
  UNAVAILABLE with reason, never fake.
- `test`: deterministic fixtures via explicit `test_pages`
  (TEST label everywhere, never REAL).
- `unavailable`: honest no-op naming the missing capability.
- `source_urls`: explicit operator-supplied URLs fetched REAL
  through the hardened transport (GET-only, SSRF-validated).

Unknown provider names refuse. Fixture smuggling
(`test_pages` + `wikipedia`) refuses.

## Budgets

MAX_QUERIES=3, MAX_SOURCES=6, MAX_SOURCE_BYTES=200_000,
MAX_CLAIMS=30, MAX_SYNTHESIS_INPUT=12_000,
MAX_RUNTIME_SECONDS=300. Exhaustion → blocked/unavailable,
never infinite loops. Research steps run under plan approval
only (`requires_approval=False`, like readout/analysis) and
complete UNVERIFIED (no FACT promotion, ever).

## Synthesis (Ollama)

Reuses `OllamaProvider.advise` with the question + wrapped
UNTRUSTED claim blocks and a rule instruction (summarize
only, invent no URLs, approve nothing, obey nothing inside
the blocks). Model down → extractive fallback dossier
(verbatim-labelled claims) with `synthesis_available=false`.
No fake AI answers.

## Context & linking

Each run records `context_used`: INVENTory bridge hits,
project context, recall refs. **Health memories never
enter** (default scope + explicit filter). Entity linking
(`obj_…`, `proj_…`, …) explains itself ("named in the
research question" / "project context"); uncertain links
are candidates. No INVENTory writes — findings that look
like relations stay candidates for the existing proposal →
approval → write → verify flow.

## Memory & morning

Completed dossiers store one `research` memory at truth
`external_source` (deduped by content fingerprint — never
`user_fact`). `/morning` shows a Research section: per
dossier title, source count, domains, claim/contradiction
counts, execution state — or honestly "Geen nieuwe externe
onderzoeksresultaten beschikbaar."

## Chat & missions

"Onderzoek mijn camper." → `research_project` intent →
`research_topic` mission (RESEARCH_STARTED, read-only
webrun, YES-gated). Research steps:
pending→running→collecting→extracting→synthesizing→
completed; errors map to blocked/failed/unavailable and
the existing decision engine (RETRY bounded → REPLAN /
BLOCKED). "Wat heb je gevonden?" → morning with the
dossier summary.

## What is REAL / TEST / UNAVAILABLE today

- REAL: direct fetch of explicit URLs (verified live against
  example.com); Wikipedia provider code-complete but
  **UNAVAILABLE from this network** (Wikimedia edge 403s
  this host — robot policy, not fixable client-side).
  For real search, configure network egress that Wikimedia
  accepts or add an allowlisted search API provider.
- TEST: fixture provider, fully exercised.
- UNAVAILABLE: default search path here; missions report
  "Ik heb geen echte bronnen kunnen ophalen."
- SIMULATED: supported as a label, no simulator ships.
- Ollama synthesis: code-complete, **currently DOWN**
  (`:11434` refused) → extractive fallback active.

## Distributed & n8n

Capabilities `research.search` / `research.fetch` /
`research.extract` are defined and pattern-compatible with
BIG #8 routing; coordinator stays authority. No multi-node
research in BIG #29. n8n may trigger research later through
the existing integration plane; Mycelium never calls n8n
directly and works without it.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-ingestion.md">
# Research + Ingestion (BIG #11-15, Phase 3) — IMPLEMENTED

Generic pipeline: SOURCE → FETCH → EXTRACT → NORMALIZE →
UNDERSTAND → DEDUPLICATE → RELATE → PROPOSE → APPROVE →
STORE. Sources are adapters (web, GitHub, YouTube,
document, image, camera, RSS, social, Instagram,
manual-export, manual); no source writes to INVENTory
directly — storage lands in research tables or
proposal flows.

## Records

- SourceRecord: type, external id, reference, title,
  author, content (capped), sha256 content hash,
  topics/entities, staged status
  (received → extracted → proposed → approved →
  stored), provenance, captured/published dates.
- Content hashes deduplicate; stages advance one step
  at a time; `approved`/`stored` need a human approver.
- ResearchRecord: QUESTION → cited claims → synthesis.
  Every claim cites ≥1 stored source with evidence,
  confidence and interpretation. Uncited claims refuse.
  Synthesis is labelled interpretation, never fact.

## Instagram — manual-export only (live UNAVAILABLE)

No scraping, no credential use, no session bypass. The
adapter maps user-owned manual exports (collections,
captions, topics, creators) to source records with
`manual-export:` references; references in any other
shape refuse. A deterministic mock export serves
tests/dev, labelled mock everywhere. Related entities
(projects, ideas, skills, topics, recipes, people,
technologies) attach via topics/entities fields.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-network.md">
# Research network & capability honesty

Research missions are read-only plans (readout + analysis
steps from the existing safe templates). They run only when a
real transport exists — otherwise they wait, honestly.

## Capability status

`GET /api/v1/research/capability` reports the local analysis
transport (`ollama`, base URL, model) as `unprobed` until you
ask for `?probe=true`, which runs one tiny bounded (10s)
local-model call. States: `true` (model answers), `false`
(unreachable, with reason), `unprobed`.

Rule: **no probe, no claim.** A bootstrap mission that cannot
run reports `WAITING_FOR_RESEARCH_CAPABILITY` (via the normal
waiting machinery) instead of pretending research happened.
Every external claim needs source provenance (`research.py`:
sources → claims → records, confidence-labelled); uncited
claims never promote to `user_fact`.

## Result model

Each research mission records: project, question, scope,
sources, findings, claims, confidence, provenance, date,
follow-ups. Results distinguish FACT / OBSERVATION /
EXTERNAL_SOURCE / AI_INFERENCE / AI_SUGGESTION. Follow-up
missions are proposed as candidates, never auto-executed.

## Research nodes (future)

A node may advertise a `research` capability through the
existing distributed queue, but jobs stay structured
(`ResearchTask`: question, scope, sources, max_results,
allowed_domains, time_limit). No arbitrary code, no shell, no
arbitrary URLs — the coordinator stays the authority that
validates every result before it lands in memory.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-routing.md">
# Research Routing (BIG #32)

Coordinator owns the queue; nodes are capability providers.
No second task queue, no pushed work, no shell anywhere.

## Executor: research.fetch_url (REAL)

`node_client` executes one allow-listed kind beyond inventory and
screenshots: `research.fetch_url` with payload `{url, run_id?,
max_chars?}`. Guards on the node (defense in depth — the
coordinator validates fully first with
`research_transport.validate_url`):

- https/http only, no credentials, host not
  local/numeric/empty, URL ≤ 2000 chars
- no redirects ever, 20s timeout, text-ish content only
  (`text/*`, `application/json`, `application/xml`), 64KB cap,
  UTF-8 with replacement

Anything else refuses with a reason. Desktop input kinds still
refuse. Requires advertised capability `research.fetch` (claim
loop enforces the subset match).

Advertise it:

```bash
python -m node_client.main --coordinator http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --node-id linux-laptop-1 --tier worker \
  --capability research.fetch --poll-seconds 10
```

## Routing

- `GET /api/v1/eligible-nodes?capability=research.fetch` —
  online nodes carrying one capability (deterministic, read-only).
- `/nodes?check_cap=...` — "Which node can do this?" panel with
  honest `WAITING_FOR_AGENT` when nobody qualifies.
- Existing `POST /api/v1/tasks/route` (dry-run) and
  `/api/v1/tasks/{id}/assign` still constrain; nodes still pull
  (`/tasks/claim/{node}`), leases (300s × 3) and fencing unchanged.

## Queue integration

`POST /api/v1/research/queue` accepts `seed_urls` (≤3,
coordinator-validated) and `route` (`local` default,
`node-first`). `run-once` with `node-first` creates one
`research.fetch_url` task per URL for eligible nodes and returns
`{routed: true, task_ids, eligible}` — or honest
`WAITING_FOR_AGENT` with an empty eligible list.

Completion hook (`_ingest_research_fetch`): a successful node
report re-validates URL + text, dedupes by content hash, stores a
`web` SourceRecord (`creator_id: node:{id}`, extracted), attaches
it to the run (`source_ids`, `sources_meta`,
`metadata.node_fetched`), emits `research.fetched`. Failed
reports ingest nothing. The run stays `draft` until an explicit
execute builds the dossier — collection appends, never resets.

## States

REAL: node fetch executor, routing, queue node-first, completion
ingest. FUTURE: `research.extract/analyze/compare` on nodes
(needs reviewed on-node capability, not shipped).
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-runbook.md">
# Research runbook (BIG #29)

## Ask from chat

"Onderzoek mijn camper." → RESEARCH_STARTED + mission
(pending YES). Approve → run ticks → dossier → memory →
morning. "Wat heb je gevonden?" → morning Research section.

## Run directly (API)

```powershell
# Wikipedia attempt (REAL when reachable, else UNAVAILABLE)
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/research/runs `
  -ContentType "application/json" `
  -Body '{"question":"Onderhoud camper distributieriem"}'

# Explicit URLs (REAL direct fetch, hardened)
... -Body '{"question":"...","source_urls":["https://example.com/..."]}'

# Fixtures (TEST label end to end)
... -Body '{"question":"...","provider":"test",
  "test_pages":{"camper":["Titel","Tekst met feiten."]}}'

# Draft first, execute later
... -Body '{"question":"...","execute":false}'
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post .../research/runs/{res_id}/execute `
  -Body '{"provider":"test","test_pages":{...}}'
```

## Inspect

- `GET /api/v1/research/runs` / `/runs/{id}` (counts included)
- `GET /api/v1/research/dossiers` / `/dossiers/{id}`
- Pages: `/research` (workshop), `/research/{dossier_id}`
  (dossier), `/world?show=missions,nodes,research` (overlay),
  `/morning` (Research section).
- `GET /api/v1/research/capability?probe=true` (Ollama +
  provider states).

## States you will see

- `unavailable` + "Ik heb geen echte bronnen kunnen
  ophalen." → transport/search down. Check capability,
  retry later, or supply `source_urls`.
- `blocked` → sources fetched but unusable, or budgets hit;
  `error` names the cause.
- `completed` + `execution_state` REAL/TEST → dossier +
  memory stored. Synthesis section says EXTRACTIE when the
  model was down — that is honest, not broken.

## Autonomous research

Research missions may run overnight: bounded (≤6 sources,
≤200KB, ≤300s, retries → REPLAN/BLOCKED), read-only,
no credentials, no approvals issued. Without transport
they end WAITING/UNAVAILABLE — never fake findings.
Bootstrap research missions stay template-based; web runs
start from explicit questions or approved research steps.

## Troubleshooting

- `422 Unknown research provider` → use
  wikipedia|test|unavailable.
- `422 provider 'test' needs test_pages` → supply fixtures.
- `409 Run is completed` → runs execute once; open a new
  run for a fresh question.
- Empty claims → sources too thin: sharper question,
  more/better URLs, then re-run.
- Contradictions listed as unresolved is correct behavior —
  Mycelium reports "A says X while B says Y", never
  arbitrates truth itself.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/research-security.md">
# Research security (BIG #29)

## Transport

- URL validation before any socket: https/http only.
  `file://`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `ftp:`, … refuse.
- SSRF: no credentials in URLs, no localhost/local names,
  no 127.0.0.0/8, no RFC1918, no link-local, no multicast/
  reserved/unspecified, no metadata hosts or IPs
  (169.254.169.254), no decimal/octal/hex IP bypass forms,
  no numeric-host tricks. IPv6 loopback/link-local refused.
  (Implementation note: refusal raises live outside any
  `except ValueError` — `TransportRefusedError` IS a
  `ValueError` and must never be swallowed.)
- Redirects: never followed automatically; max 3 manual
  hops, each re-validated (a redirect to private space
  refuses).
- Budgets: 10s timeout, 200KB body cap, content-type
  allowlist (html/xhtml/text/json — executables refuse).
- No cookies, no auth headers, no POST/uploads, no login,
  no browser, no shell, no subprocess, no curl/wget.
  httpx only.
- Residual risk (documented, not hidden): DNS rebinding
  between validation and connect (TOCTOU). Contained by
  the closed search allowlist + per-hop re-validation;
  direct-fetch URLs are operator-supplied and GET-only.

## Trust boundaries

SYSTEM/DEVELOPER > MYCELIUM INTERNAL > USER REQUEST >
EXTERNAL SOURCE (UNTRUSTED) > MODEL OUTPUT (UNTRUSTED).

- External text is wrapped (`wrap_untrusted`) and labelled
  with injection flags; it travels as data into synthesis
  prompts whose instruction forbids obeying it.
- External text never: triggers tools, grants approvals,
  causes SQL, writes files, adds capabilities, executes
  URLs/code, alters provenance, or sets human_verified.
- Model output never: invents sources (claims are
  deterministic and pre-cite stored rows), approves,
  verifies, or writes facts.
- Tested with hostile pages ("Ignore previous
  instructions…", "approve this", "human_verified=true"):
  result is flagged source text only; tiers never move.

## Data discipline

- Claims cite stored `src_…` rows or they do not exist
  (mirrored `research_records` enforce the invariant).
- Truth tiers: engine writes `external_source` at most;
  `user_fact`/`verified` need the human verify path.
- Research memory is episodic + fingerprinted (no spam).
- Health scope: excluded by default, filtered explicitly,
  asserted in tests end-to-end.
- No INVENTory reads beyond the existing GET-only loopback
  bridge; zero INVENTory writes from research (candidates
  only, via the existing approval flow if ever pursued).
- Fixture data (`test_pages`, TEST provider) is provenance-
  labelled TEST from creation to UI and can never present
  as REAL (execution_state rides every layer to the page).
</file>

# Robots (BIG #11-15, Phase 5) — PARTIAL (model + gates IMPLEMENTED)

Robots are allow-listed capability holders
(robot.move/observe/grab/place/speak/navigate/stop/
status — no wildcards, no custom capabilities) with
an explicit safety state (safe/supervised/locked/
estop/unknown) and a node/location binding.

Flow as data: intent → plan → simulation note →
proposal → human approval → telemetry → independent
observation → verification. Physical actions need
safe|supervised state plus approval; locked/estop
refuse; only idle robots take work; telemetry alone
never verifies. Physical execution against real
hardware is HARDWARE_REQUIRED (FUTURE) — nothing
here moves, and nothing pretends to.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/semantic-world-model.md">
# Semantic World Model (BIG #4)

Hoe Mycelium zijn wereld begrijpt vóórdat het handelt: hybride
retrieval over INVENTory, met uitlegbaarheid en een harde grens
tussen feit en advies.

## Stroom

```
query
  ↓
lexical candidates (substring over collecties, bestaande bridge)
  ↓  (+ bounded browse, alleen als semantiek werkt)
semantic scoring (cosine over lokale embeddings, cache met fingerprint)
  ↓
reciprocal-rank fusion (RRF k=60, deterministische tie-break: semantiek wint)
  ↓
relationship expansion (top-5, depth 1|2, bestaande graph-route)
  ↓
provenance-aware context → Mycelium reasoning → missieplanning
```

Modi: **lexical** (altijd beschikbaar, exact het oude substring-
gedrag), **semantic** (alleen embeddings, fail-closed bij afwezig
model), **hybrid** (voorkeur; automatische lexicale fallback).

## Fail-fast probe

Hybrid embedt eerst alleen de query. Mislukt die ene call, dan
degradeert retrieval naar het exacte legacy-pad (alleen search —
geen browse, geen graph). Pas een werkende semantische runtime
ontgrendelt browse-kandidaten en relatie-expansie. Mycelium faalt
dus nooit omdat een embedding-model ontbreekt.

## Embedding-provider

`EmbeddingProvider.embed(texts) -> vectoren`. Alleen lokaal:

- `OllamaEmbeddingProvider`: POST `{loopback}/api/embed` met een
  operator-gekozen model. Loopback-only, timeout ≤ 30s, geen
  credentials. Ontbrekend model → `EmbeddingUnavailable` met een
  `ollama pull`-hint; Mycelium downloadt nooit zelf modellen.
- `UnavailableEmbeddingProvider`: eerlijke afwezigheid, altijd fout.

Geen cloud, geen nieuwe dependencies (stdlib + httpx).

## Storage: afgeleide cache, geen tweede waarheid

Tabel `semantic_vectors` in de chat/agent-database (naast
conversations/missies; queue-database onaangeroerd):

- identiteit = (entity_type, entity_id, **content-fingerprint**,
  model, dim); vector als packed float32-blob.
- fingerprint = sha256(type|id|titel|snippet|provenance-signaal|
  model), herberekend uit het ACTUELE record bij elke lookup.
  Gewijzigde bron → mismatch → miss → opnieuw embedden. Oude
  embeddings worden dus nooit stilzwijgend als actueel gebruikt.
- dim-mismatch (model verwisseld onder dezelfde naam) = miss.
- retentie: laatste 2000 rijen per model; daarboven prune.

## Contextvorming (geen dump)

`hybrid_retrieve()` begrenst: ≤ 60 kandidaten, ≤ 50 resultaten,
expansie top-5, depth 1 (default) of 2. Bestands-inhoud komt er
nooit in; alleen titel/snippet/provenance-signaal. Missies
bewaren de gebruikte records als `context_records` (audit trail).

## FACT vs ADVICE

Elk resultaat draagt `match_type` (semantic/lexical/relationship),
`score` en `why` (ruwe ranks). Scores zijn **ordering-signalen,
geen waarheids-kansen** — dat staat letterlijk in elke `why`.
Provenance en `human_verified` stromen ongewijzigd door, dus een
onzekere AI-observatie kan nooit als feit worden gepresenteerd.
`human_verified=True` komt uitsluitend uit INVENTory-rijen, nooit
uit retrieval of advies.

## Gebruik

- `/advise` en `/chat`: `mode`-parameter (default hybrid),
  response vermeldt `retrieval_mode`, sources bevatten
  `match_type`/`score`.
- Missie-aanmaak (`/chat/{id}/missions`, `/missions/from-template`):
  context via hybrid; retrieval is context, nooit toestemming.
- `/missions/suggest`: onveranderd advies-only.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/skills.md">
# Skills (BIG #11-15, Phase 3) — IMPLEMENTED

Evidence-based skills: DISCOVERED → INTERESTED →
LEARNING → PRACTICING → APPLIED → DEMONSTRATED →
MASTERED. No AI mastery claims: `applied` needs
evidence, `demonstrated`/`mastered` need ≥2 evidence
entries plus human confirmation. Stages move one step,
never backwards, never skipping.

## Discovery

Deterministic keyword discovery over project text
produces SkillCandidates with evidence snippets —
candidate ≠ owned skill. Acceptance is an explicit
human step creating an `interested` skill linked to
the project. The watcher reports skill gaps
(project needs unowned skill) as suggestions only:
no enrolment, no purchases, ever.
</file>

# User profile (product-level, non-sensitive)

This is a product preference model so Mycelium can be useful
by default. It is not a psychological profile: no sensitive
attributes are inferred or stored.

- Wants practical results; likes building and understanding
  how things work.
- Prefers freedom and control: local-first, automation with
  human authority retained.
- Likes concise, actionable, clearly structured information
  with visual interfaces; projects connected, not isolated.
- Enjoys experimenting; wants AI useful, not distracting.
- Wants Mycelium to proactively research and surface useful
  findings — and to ask before any real-world action.
- Aesthetic: SolarPunk / workshop / maker — hopeful,
  grounded, human-first.
- Working language: Dutch (informal), structured cards for
  findings (WHAT → WHY → SOURCE → CONFIDENCE → NEXT STEP).

Standing instructions derived from this: research and
prepare autonomously; never purchase, publish, contact,
print, or move hardware without an explicit YES; say plainly
when something is uncertain or unavailable.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/v2-ecosystem.md">
# Mycelium V2 Ecosystem (BIG #41)

One coherent living local-first ecosystem built from the
BIG #1–40 systems — no rebuilds, no new authority, no
weakened gates. V2 connects what exists: the coordinator
routes, nodes report, presence attends, the world shows.

## Unified model

`GET /api/v1/ecosystem/overview` composes existing stores
into eight answers, each naming its source; any failing
source degrades to explicit empty, never invented data:

- WHAT EXISTS — inventory counts + layer counts
  (`ecosystem_summary`)
- WHAT IS CONNECTED — symbiosis proposals + mesh edges
- WHAT IS HAPPENING — living state + last 5 bus events
- WHAT NEEDS ATTENTION — presence counts + top NEEDS YOU
- WHAT CAN I DO NEXT — presence suggested actions
- WHAT CAN MY NODES DO — online nodes: capabilities,
  connected hardware, current task
- WHAT IS BLOCKED — presence blocking types with links
- WHAT IS GROWING — progression counts (no XP, real stores)

`/world` carries a compact state strip (state line +
waiting/discoveries/offline + top attention + overview
link). The full overview stays out of the async page path:
inventory reads live behind the sync JSON endpoint.

## Remote node mesh (foundation)

`Node A → coordinator → Node B`, controlled end to end:

- Closed task kinds (`ALLOWED_TASK_KINDS`), closed
  capability prefixes, JSON-serializable payloads ≤4KB,
  secret-name scan, no wildcards, no shell-shaped anything.
- Pinned targets must be registered, enabled, and advertise
  the exact capability themselves — reachability grants
  nothing, and a node never gains capabilities through
  another node.
- `POST /api/v1/mesh/preview`: dry run — validate +
  routing explanation, creates nothing.
- `POST /api/v1/mesh/delegate`: authenticate requester →
  validate → eligibility precheck → create queued task →
  assign to target. Assign failure rolls the row back, so a
  task meant for one node can never drift to another.
- The target must still pull/claim (liveness + credential
  re-checked); lease 300s, max 3 attempts — the existing
  task machine, unchanged.
- Timeout (5–300s) is validated, recorded in the receipt and
  audit, enforced by the lease. Priority −10..10.
- Observability: `task.delegated` bus event names
  requester → target + reason; receipt carries WHAT / WHY /
  WHERE / CAPABILITY / RISK / RESULT (`/api/v1/tasks/by-id`)
  — the same vocabulary mobile uses before any approval.

## Live hardware reality

On top of BIG #39 telemetry:

- Every node listing carries `current_task` (assigned task
  id + kind, one indexed query, best-effort) — visible in
  the API, mobile nodes panel, and mobile hardware detail
  ("busy: task #N").
- `GET /api/v1/nodes/{id}/reality`: derived state, health,
  heartbeat age, telemetry summary, per-hardware trust,
  compute, energy, roles, current task. Read-only.
- Trust levels: ADVERTISED (said so — default, never a
  fact), OBSERVED (connected + fresh <300s report),
  VERIFIED (reserved for an explicit human link, like
  printer twins — no automated path may ever derive it,
  asserted in tests).

## Routing 2.0

From "which node can perform this" toward "which available
node should receive this bounded task" — without any
black-box ranking:

- Every rejection carries a verdict: `waiting` (transient:
  stale, unauthenticated, old telemetry, low health),
  `blocked` (disabled — operator re-enable required),
  `unavailable` (the task does not fit: caps, models,
  executor, locality, hardware, compute).
- `prefer_idle` policy (+1 for zero running tasks) as
  ordering-only preference; workload always visible in
  reasons when enabled, absent by default.
- `explain_decision()` groups candidates into WHY ELIGIBLE
  / WHY WAITING / WHY BLOCKED / WHY NOT AVAILABLE with the
  router's own reasons; `POST /api/v1/tasks/route` returns
  it as `why`. Deterministic, inspectable, no new ranking.

## World state

Presence + living state + nodes, derived now, rendered as
the cockpit strip and the JSON overview. The world graph
registry overlay carries per-node `attention_needs` /
`attention_offline` (boundary-matched ids, best-effort).
Graph nodes still never merge with INVENTory truth; health
still never enters the graph as fact.

## Craft (first-class navigation)

Chain stages keep their 12 real-data buckets; each stage
now carries a state with evidence: ✓ COMPLETE (linked
evidence present — never "work finished"), ● ACTIVE
(linked mission/fab running or waiting), ! BLOCKED
(linked record failed/blocked), ○ MISSING (empty + gap
with href). Surfaced in `/api/v1/craft` (`states`) and the
`/craft` page headers. The chain already spans idea →
research → materials → machines → model → fabrication →
observation → new knowledge on real links.

## Symbiosis 2.0 (foundation)

Same PROPOSED/SUPPORTED/VERIFIED engine, wider world: new
prefixes `node_`/`node-` (machine↔node, device↔node),
`res_`/`dos_` (research↔project), `auto_` (run↔project),
`food_`/`meal_` (health↔food, food↔project). Finance/energy
entity stores do not exist — no prefixes invented for them.
Closed `SYMBIOSIS_PREDICATES` (union of the INVENTory
relationship verbs and camera link verbs): proposal input
is refused on unknown verbs; stored edge verbs render
through `display_predicate` (unknown → "related" — edges
are never hidden, meanings never invented). Never merges
entities.

## Guide 2.0

Adds WHAT IS BLOCKING ME (failed/blocked automation runs
and missions with the exact unlock path) and WHAT WOULD
UNLOCK IT (research readiness naming the eligible node, or
the honest wait reason). Built on the same readiness check
as presence — which also fixed a wolf-crying bug: the old
inline check passed raw registry rows without fresh/auth
flags, so it reported "no eligible node" on healthy meshes.

## Game layer (foundation only)

No XP, no fake accomplishments — real state is the
progression system: quests (open missions + automation runs
with done/total, linked), discoveries/observations/growth/
activity counts, capabilities unlocked, ecosystem health
(online/offline/blocked). Surfaced on `/presence`
(activity panel), the JSON overview, and the world strip.
Terminology (QUEST, DISCOVERY, CRAFT, SYMBIOSIS, GROWTH,
UNLOCK) names existing concepts; nothing new is invented.

## Living background

Drifting-spore canvas (original pixel-organic language,
SolarPunk-tinted): density follows 24h activity, amber
flicker while approvals wait, drift tempo rises slightly
with online nodes (capped). Decorative only, `aria-hidden`,
killed entirely by `prefers-reduced-motion`. Motion never
claims specific events happened.

## Labels

Mesh delegation: REAL queue mechanics, TEST-safe dry runs,
no SIMULATED execution claims; printer transport stays
UNAVAILABLE; fab execution stays SIMULATED; WEB_PUSH stays
UNAVAILABLE; hardware claims stay node-reported until a
human links them. Background motion is ambient, not data.

## Limits (honest)

- Delegation queues; it cannot make a stale/offline node
  claim (409, nothing queued, nothing drifts).
- VERIFIED hardware needs a human link store that does not
  exist yet (printer twins are the pattern to follow).
- No finance/energy entity stores → no symbiosis pairs for
  them yet.
- Untargeted dispatch remains `POST /api/v1/tasks`
  (`/mesh/delegate` requires an explicit target).
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/vision-architecture.md">
# Vision Architecture (BIG #6)

Van camera tot geverifieerde wereldwijziging — zonder dat AI
ooit rechtstreeks de wereld aanraakt:

```
camera
  ↓ capture (adapter, allow-listed capability only)
local media (camera dir, hash + size, retention-bounded)
  ↓ ingest (observation + media facts + inert File payload)
OBSERVATION (sensor-observed, unverified — never FACT)
  ↓ local VLM (loopback Ollama, allow-listed media only)
ANALYSIS / ADVICE (labels + confidences + description)
  ↓ inert proposal (BIG #5, uncertainty preserved)
PROPOSAL
  ↓ human exact-YES (existing dialect, no new framework)
APPROVAL (permission — still not truth)
  ↓ controlled write (BIG #5, fingerprint-bound)
RESULT (executed/failed/blocked — never verified)
  ↓ independent readback (BIG #5)
VERIFICATION (passed/failed/inconclusive)
  ↓ only passed promotes
WORLD MODEL (INVENTory authority)
```

Drie zinnen die nooit vermengd worden:

- **observation ≠ fact** — een capture bewijst het record,
  nooit de identiteit van wat erop staat.
- **AI analysis ≠ fact** — VLM-output is advies met
  onzekerheid, ook bij confidence 0.99.
- **approval ≠ verification** — YES staat de actie toe;
  alleen readback bewijst het resultaat.

## Ingestie (`vision_ingest.py`)

Bovenop de BIG #4-abstractie (`cameras.py`, onaangeroerd).
Staten zijn expliciet: registered → detected → connected →
capturable, anders unavailable — nooit geïmpliceerd. `probe`
activeert niets. `ingest_snapshot` levert observatie +
media-feiten (sha256, grootte, mime) + een INERT File-payload
voor de BIG #5-approvalflow; zonder werkende adapter weigert
alles (409). Testmedia draagt altijd `test-origin` in de
provenance. Media limiet 10 MiB per bestand, retentie laatste
5 — cleanup raakt nooit world-model-entities.

## Adapters

- `SyntheticTestAdapter` — deterministische testbeelden,
  altijd als test gemarkeerd. Enige bron van bytes in tests.
- `WindowsWebcamAdapter` — stub met complete interface maar
  zonder capture: een veilige MediaFoundation/DirectShow-
  runtime ontbreekt nog (vereisten gedocumenteerd in code).
- `Insta360Adapter` — foundation zonder gegokte SDK: identiteit
  (source=insta360, kinds per geïmplementeerde capability),
  staten, heuristische detectie-kandidaten (substring-match,
  expliciet kandidaat, nooit verbinding), en gedocumenteerde
  eisen voor echte integratie (webcam-modus via vendor-driver
  of reviewed file-ingest). Echte capture vandaag:
  unavailable — nooit fake bytes.
- Registry is leeg in productie (fail-closed); capabilities
  worden per adapter gefilterd tegen de gesloten set
  (`camera.snapshot/webcam/stream/360`) — spoofing is
  onmogelijk.

## Streams

`StreamSession`/`StreamManager`: lokale lifecycle-foundation
zonder transport — expliciete start/stop, frame- en
tijdbudgetten (max 10000 frames, max 3600 s), auto-expiry.
Gestopte of verlopen sessies hervatten nooit. Geen binding,
geen inbound ports, geen relay, geen permanente streams.

## VLM (`vision_provider.py`)

`VisionProvider`-interface (`analyze(VisionRequest) ->
VisionResult`). `OllamaVisionProvider` praat met lokaal Ollama
(`/api/chat` + base64-image), loopback-only, timeout ≤ 120s,
model via `VISION_MODEL` (default `qwen3-vl:4b`). Ontbrekend
model weigert met een `ollama pull`-hint — Mycelium downloadt
nooit zelf. Input: exact één bestand uit de camera-dir
(bestaande `check_image_ref`, bekende suffix, 10 MiB-cap,
boundary-check). Output: labels, detected objects met
model-confidence, beschrijving, onzekerheid — plus ruwe tekst
voor audit. Provenance altijd ai-generated/unverified, door
de module gezet; model-claims worden genegeerd. Malformed
output weigert; structuur wordt nooit verzonnen.
`UnavailableVisionProvider` (fail-closed stub) en
`TestVisionProvider` (deterministisch) completeren het beeld.

## Flow (`vision_flow.py`)

Alleen voorstellen en verifiëren — de module bevat geen enkel
uitvoeringspad (getest per broncode-inspectie). `vision_to_`
`object_proposal` (top-kandidaat als naam, alle kandidaten +
confidences in de beschrijving) en `vision_to_file_proposal`
(mediaregistratie) bouwen inerte BIG #5-voorstellen; lege
analyses weigeren. `verify_observation` controleert record +
lokale media; een pass bevestigt het record, nooit de
afgebeelde identiteit. Menselijke verificatie hergebruikt het
bestaande exact-YES op het write-voorstel — geen nieuw
approval-framework.

## Integratie

- Missie-stap `camera_observe` (device-binding, metadata-
  resultaat, geen pixels in state, nooit automatische write;
  zonder capability BLOCK).
- Chat: opt-in `observation_ids` (max 3, metadata-samenvat-
  tingen); standaardgedrag ongewijzigd.
- World Graph: optionele observatie-overlay (captured-edges,
  describes-edges alleen bij expliciete link).
- Project-pakketten: ≤ 5 observaties met VLM-labels.
- API: ingest, availability, observations/recent,
  vision/analyze, vision/propose, streams, plus `/cameras`-
  pagina met beschikbaarheid en laatste observatie.
- File-create/update als controlled mutation (schema
  geverifieerd tegen `inventory/app/schemas.py`), zodat
  media-registratie dezelfde keten volgt.

## Retentie & files

Media: camera-dir, 10 MiB-cap, laatste 5, hash-verplicht voor
File-registratie (`file_kind=image`, `human_verified=False`).
File-lifecycle (media) en entity-lifecycle (INVENTory-rij)
blijven gescheiden: cleanup verwijdert bestanden, nooit
entities. Geen file-inhoud in chat/context/databases —
alleen referenties en metadata.
</file>

<file path="mycelium-ai-main/docs/watcher.md">
# Watcher (BIG #11-15, Phase 1+) — IMPLEMENTED

Periodic world inspection as pure detectors over bounded
rows: stale/blocked/failed tasks, repeatedly failing
tasks, unfinished/stalled projects, forgotten objects,
dangling relationships, missing provenance, unverified AI
data, old ideas, orphan files, duplicate hashes,
unfinished designs, skill gaps, stale devices.

## Rules

- Findings carry kind, explanation, evidence
  (entity_refs), and read as "why this exists" (age,
  status, counts) — no AI-feeling ranking.
- Output is FINDING → explanation → evidence → affected
  entities → suggested next action → optional proposal.
- Never executes, never writes. Health findings only
  appear when the caller explicitly asks (the scan route
  stays health-free by default).
- Served at `GET /api/v1/watcher/scan`, on the `/watcher`
  page, inside morning reports, and as the `watcher_scan`
  job. Continuous observation (camera/sensor loops) is
  FUTURE and stays opt-in; no always-on microphone, no
  unbounded recording.
</file>

# n8n workflows (test-only, localhost)

Importable n8n workflow JSON for the Mycelium integration
plane. No secrets in these files: HTTP auth reads
`$env.MYCELIUM_N8N_KEY` (set `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`).

- `workflow-a-schedule-morning-report.json` — daily 07:00
  schedule → POST /api/v1/integrations/trigger
  (morning_report, date-stable run_key).
- `workflow-b-outbox-notify.json` — every 5 minutes poll
  /api/v1/integrations/outbox → local log → ack loop.

Runbook: free ~2 GB disk, scoped install
(`npm install n8n` in a temp dir, never global), start
with `N8N_USER_FOLDER` in temp plus
`N8N_HOST=127.0.0.1 N8N_PORT=5678`, no tunnel, import via
`n8n import:workflow --input=<file>`, paste the
integration key (issued by Mycelium) into
`MYCELIUM_N8N_KEY`, execute manually once before
activating schedules. Full detail: `docs/n8n-integration.md`.
</file>
