<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Decisions and questions.md">
# Decisions and questions

## Decisions in force

- Coordinator, INVENTory, and desktop scanner remain independent runtime areas.
- The vault stores human-authored project documentation, not live runtime state or secrets.
- LiveSync will use a separate CouchDB service and end-to-end encryption; service exposure is private and deliberate.
- CouchDB runs on this Windows PC and is loopback-bound. The existing Solarlab vault uses database `solarlab`; the Mycelium documentation vault must use a separate database.
- Android access will use NetBird-only HTTPS. A dedicated subdomain on `urbanmovementzeeland.nl` is acceptable; website and email records must remain untouched. The subdomain name itself can appear in public certificate-transparency logs.
- Node workers remain pull-only and capability-scoped.
- `/side` is frozen under the current repository instructions.

## Remaining steps before remote sync

- Open `Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/` as a separate Obsidian vault and configure its own LiveSync database.
- Verify a desktop note round-trip before treating the project vault as synced.
- Configure the NetBird account-owned private proxy, Hostinger DNS-01 certificate renewal, and private DNS. No public A/AAAA record or direct CouchDB exposure is intended.
- The account-scoped NetBird proxy token and Hostinger DNS API token still need to be created and stored locally in ignored configuration; never paste them into chat or tracked files.
- Choose a backup destination and retention policy for both vault content and CouchDB data.
- After sync works, choose the Windows node onboarding path to make easiest.

These steps do not block using either vault locally. CouchDB is currently responding on loopback.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/INVENTory and knowledge.md">
# INVENTory and knowledge

INVENTory is the canonical world-model service. Its records can describe objects, projects, ideas, relationships, events, hardware, sensors, cameras, locations, models, tasks, actuators, and files. The coordinator can read through a constrained HTTP bridge and can submit gated write proposals.

## Data rules

- INVENTory and coordinator have separate SQLite databases. Do not merge them or query one from the other directly.
- AI/sensor observations remain unverified until a human verifies them.
- Canonical entity tables are the source of truth; search indexes are derived.
- CRUD mutations append events.
- Hardware/device records are descriptions; their presence does not mean the device is controlled.

## Where Obsidian fits

Use this vault for explanations, architecture diagrams, operating procedures, decisions, and handoff notes. Use the runtime APIs for live entities, tasks, approval state, and device telemetry. The vault is not the new canonical store for those records.

Future integration should be a one-way, explicit export or context packet into the vault, with provenance and human review. Avoid an implicit bidirectional sync between notes and live operational records.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Nodes and devices.md">
# Nodes and devices

## What a node is today

A node is a worker process that registers, sends heartbeats, and pulls supported tasks from the coordinator. It does not open an inbound port for the coordinator. The current worker is Python-based and already uses cross-platform APIs for much of its telemetry, but the setup experience is not equally easy on every platform.

## Platform readiness

| Platform | Today | Sensible next step |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | CLI installer, diagnostics, optional user `systemd` unit | simplify the documented path and keep least-privilege defaults |
| Windows | worker code can run, but setup is mostly manual | guided per-user PowerShell installer, diagnostics, and optional Scheduled Task |
| Android | no supported persistent worker | start with the mobile web UI; investigate a limited Termux worker only after lifecycle and permission tests |

## Safe starter configuration

- Pick a unique node ID; reusing one overwrites its registration identity.
- Use a private connection such as a trusted LAN or tailnet; do not expose the coordinator publicly as a shortcut.
- Start with the narrow, documented capability set. Never grant wildcard, shell, or generic command execution.
- Store node tokens locally with OS-appropriate protection. Do not paste them into chat, commits, screenshots, or a shared vault.
- Remote-input capabilities are separate and must be explicitly enabled and probed on the node.

## Not yet delivered

- A polished Windows “two click” installer and managed restart flow.
- An Android-native/Termux node with a reliable foreground lifetime.
- General drag-and-drop files/tabs between nodes.
- A robust cross-device coauthoring protocol for simultaneous edits.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Obsidian LiveSync.md">
# Obsidian LiveSync

## Goal

Keep a human-readable Mycelium project vault available on Windows, Linux, and Android, while leaving runtime databases and credentials out of Obsidian. Self-hosted LiveSync is a community plugin, not an official Obsidian service. It supports CouchDB and end-to-end encryption; it is incompatible with official Obsidian Sync and should not share a vault with another sync writer.

## What is prepared here

`../ops/obsidian-livesync/` contains a CouchDB Compose file that binds to loopback only and requires credentials via an ignored `.env` file. The local CouchDB status endpoint answered on 2026-10-15, and an authenticated metadata-only check found the `solarlab` database with 7 documents. No document contents were read.

Obsidian 1.14.4 is running with **Solarlab** open. Self-hosted LiveSync shows end-to-end encryption enabled and an active connection to `127.0.0.1:5984`, database `solarlab`. This proves the desktop plugin is configured and the database exists; a controlled note round-trip has not yet been verified.

The prepared Mycelium documentation folder (`Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/`) is **not** the open Solarlab vault and has no `.obsidian` settings yet. It is not currently syncing. Keep it separate and give it its own LiveSync database, so Solarlab notes are not mixed into the project vault.

The CouchDB port remains bound to `127.0.0.1:5984`. NetBird is connected on this PC; one remote peer reports connected via relay while five of six are offline. The peer hostname resembles an Android device, but this was not confirmed on the phone. There is no account-owned private proxy or Android HTTPS route configured, so Android cannot reach CouchDB through LiveSync yet. The local CouchDB API is reachable; this execution environment cannot inspect Docker containers because access to Docker Desktop's named pipe is denied, so the exact container state is unverified.

## Safe bring-up sequence

1. Back up this vault. Do not sync the repository root or runtime data folders.
2. Keep the existing ignored `.env` file and its generated credential private. On a fresh checkout only, create `.env` from `.env.example` and choose a unique username and password.
3. `tools/start-local.ps1` opens Docker Desktop and starts the loopback CouchDB container when the engine is available. The port is bound to `127.0.0.1:5984`; it is not exposed to the LAN or internet.
4. In the intended Obsidian vault, install and enable **Self-hosted LiveSync**. For the first device, manual CouchDB setup works without a Setup URI: URL `http://127.0.0.1:5984`, credentials from `.env`, and a unique lower-case database name for that vault. Leave JWT and custom headers off. Use Internal API only if normal CORS access fails.
5. Enable end-to-end encryption and store the vault passphrase safely. Let LiveSync create/connect to the new database and initialise this first device as the source of truth. Keep a backup before confirming any server initialisation or overwrite prompt.
6. In the **Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault** vault, use a separate lower-case database name such as `mycelium`; never point two vaults at the same LiveSync database. Verify a harmless test note moves both directions before using this project vault as your source of truth.
7. Then use `Self-hosted LiveSync: Copy settings as a new Setup URI` for additional devices. Keep the Setup URI and its separate passphrase private.
8. Android requires a valid HTTPS endpoint. Set up the chosen NetBird private proxy and private DNS before remote use. Do not publish port 5984 directly. The subdomain may be listed in public certificate-transparency logs, but the service itself must remain NetBird-only.
9. Keep optional plugin/settings sync disabled until ordinary notes work.

## Collaboration expectations

LiveSync is for synchronising files across devices. It is not a transactional multi-user editing service. Concurrent edits can conflict and require human resolution. Use backups and agree on ownership for heavily edited notes; don't treat eventual sync as a lock or a substitute for review.

## Credential and recovery rules

- CouchDB administrator credentials belong only in the ignored `.env` file or a password manager.
- Keep the vault encryption passphrase separate from the Setup URI passphrase.
- Treat a Setup URI as sensitive because it contains encrypted connection configuration. Share its URI and passphrase through separate channels.
- Save the setup recovery code somewhere secure and independent of the vault.
- Never place `.env`, Setup URIs, tokens, passwords, or recovery codes in this vault.
- Back up both vault content and CouchDB data. Sync is not a backup.

## Private phone connection choices

NetBird-only HTTPS is the selected route. The PC is connected, and one remote peer is connected through a relay; this confirms mesh connectivity, not access to CouchDB. Android cannot reach the LiveSync service yet because the plugin needs an HTTPS URL and CouchDB is bound only to the PC's `127.0.0.1:5984`.

The suitable NetBird design is an account-owned BYOP cluster with the **Private** capability, a NetBird-Only service, and DNS-01-issued static TLS certificates. NetBird's current guide supports this without opening router ports or publishing public A/AAAA records: private DNS directs authorised NetBird peers to the proxy's NetBird address. The proxy still needs a safe upstream path to CouchDB; keep CouchDB itself off the LAN and internet. NetBird's shared clusters do not currently advertise the Private capability, so the dashboard's “NetBird-Only Access” option requires an account-owned cluster.

A dedicated subdomain under `urbanmovementzeeland.nl` remains acceptable, but do not change the business website/mail records. Hostinger DNS-01 will create temporary `_acme-challenge` TXT records using a narrowly scoped API credential. The wildcard/base name may appear in public certificate-transparency logs; individual service names covered by a wildcard are not listed. No proxy route or DNS record has been configured yet.

## Upstream references

- [Self-hosted LiveSync quick setup](https://github.com/vrtmrz/obsidian-livesync/blob/main/docs/quick_setup.md)
- [Prepare your own CouchDB server](https://github.com/vrtmrz/obsidian-livesync/blob/main/docs/setup_own_server.md)
- [Plugin repository and compatibility notes](https://github.com/vrtmrz/obsidian-livesync)
- [NetBird reverse proxy and private access](https://docs.netbird.io/manage/reverse-proxy)
- [NetBird private proxy without public inbound ports](https://docs.netbird.io/use-cases/security/private-no-inbound)
- [NetBird proxy with LEGO DNS-01](https://docs.netbird.io/use-cases/security/private-proxy-with-lego)
- [LEGO Hostinger DNS provider](https://go-acme.github.io/lego/dns/hostinger/)
- [Tailscale HTTPS certificate requirements](https://tailscale.com/docs/how-to/set-up-https-certificates)
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Recurring goals and blockers.md">
# Recurring goals and implementation blockers

Audit updated: 2026-10-15. This note compares current source, the dated
`docs/DEVELOPMENT_STATE.md` journal, and the 15 milestone reports
`mycelium-ai-main/docs/BIG31-final-report.md` through
`BIG45-final-report.md`.

## What can be counted

The repository does not contain a complete export of every OpenCode or
Codex conversation, so it cannot support an exact count of how many times
Jelles explained each goal in chat. The counts below are **distinct
milestone documents containing a topic**, not the number of failed
implementations:

| Topic | Evidence in the repo | What the count means |
|---|---|---|
| City, town, and NPC work | 8 dated entries in `docs/DEVELOPMENT_STATE.md` cover Solar Punk/Town/NPC iterations from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-06. | At least 8 recorded build or repair passes, not 8 restarts from zero. |
| Ollama and vision | 6 of the 15 BIG31–45 reports mention Ollama or vision. | Provider work was revisited across milestones; the reports do not imply each pass failed. |
| Node onboarding | 3 of the 15 reports mention `node_client` or bootstrap. | Bootstrap exists, but a report mention is not evidence that a device remains online. |
| Printing | All 15 reports mention a printer or printing. | This is a repeated status topic. The code still marks real transport unavailable or execution simulated; it is not 15 completed real-print attempts. |
| Background scheduler | BIG38 explicitly records no background scheduler; the current code and `CURRENT_STATE.md` show the new safe scheduler. | Earlier behavior was intentionally on-demand. The read-only scheduler is a new, narrow change. |

## Why it kept feeling “almost done”

### The work landed in separate layers

Several milestones completed data models, routes, or UI controls before
the corresponding local service, worker, credential, or hardware path was
available. A button can be real while its downstream transport is still
`UNAVAILABLE`; a simulated print pipeline is useful preparation, but it
is not a physical print. Older milestone documents often say “DONE” for
their layer, while the current system still has a wider integration gap.

### Services and workers can be independently offline

The coordinator, INVENTory, Ollama, Hermes, CouchDB, and node workers are
separate processes with separate health conditions. On 2026-10-15 the
coordinator, INVENTory, Hermes, Ollama, scheduler, and CouchDB HTTP status
answered locally. The registered node was still reported stale. Obsidian
was connected to the separate Solarlab vault, not the prepared Mycelium
vault; Android had no private HTTPS route. Docker CLI access was denied in
the check, so container state was not independently confirmed. This is why
some model/UI work can be real while node execution and project-vault sync
are still incomplete.

### Nodes deliberately have limited authority

Nodes poll the coordinator and can claim only advertised capabilities.
The current registry had one stale node; no connected worker was available
to claim the queued research task. File transfer between nodes is not
implemented. A truly unattended Windows installer also needs a safe way
to persist its node token, but the repository contract forbids secret
storage and this choice still needs a deliberate policy decision.

### Hardware is kept behind separate gates

The print workflow prepares artifacts and simulates execution, while real
printer transport and print-arm automation remain unavailable. Filament,
printer state, and camera verification must be live and fail-closed before
an automated print path is safe. Existing policy keeps physical actions
out of automated test runs and behind explicit approval.

### Runtime reloads and model availability have caused false “broken” states

The dated journal records a stale Uvicorn process returning 404 for a new
route, Ollama stopping when its service window disappeared, and a local VLM
default model that was not installed. The current vision flow now uses
`qwen3.5:4b`, ignores system proxies for loopback requests, caps generation,
and preserves inline model descriptions. A synthetic screen observation
now passes through the same `_hermes_screen_summary` path used by Mos.

## Current repairs in this pass

- The coordinator starts a fixed scheduler for four read-only jobs and
  exposes process status at `/api/v1/jobs/scheduler` and `/system`.
- Mos can receive opt-in text-only screen context from the local VLM. The
  live synthetic check returned `REAL`; it did not send raw pixels to
  Hermes.
- The live model-route page now returns `200`; only code routes are
  unavailable because the current Python environment cannot import
  `code_worker`. Package discovery includes that package in source now;
  the active process has not been reinstalled or restarted since the fix.
- The per-user startup script attempts all local services independently,
  opens Docker Desktop, and starts loopback CouchDB when the engine is
  ready. It continues when one service is unavailable.

## Practical next order

1. Open `Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/` as its own Obsidian vault, configure
   its own CouchDB database, and prove one note round-trips on desktop.
2. Configure the selected NetBird-only HTTPS route and prove that same note
   round-trips with Android; keep CouchDB loopback-only.
3. Decide how node tokens may be stored before creating unattended node
   installers or auto-start workers.
4. Reconnect one real node and prove a bounded harmless task end to end.
5. Keep printer automation in simulation until live condition sensors,
   print transport, arm behavior, and visual empty-bed verification are
   independently proven.
6. Make `/solarpunk` status reflect real node/model/task signals before
   expanding the scene or adding more NPC activity.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Roadmap.md">
# Roadmap

## Priority 1 — Make it understandable and recoverable

- **Ready locally:** the project documentation vault exists, CouchDB answers on loopback, and Obsidian's separate Solarlab vault has an active encrypted connection to database `solarlab`.
- **Not yet proven:** a note round-trip in the Mycelium documentation vault. `Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/` is not the currently open Solarlab vault and has no Obsidian settings.
- Finish one vertical slice: open the project folder as its own vault, configure a distinct `mycelium` LiveSync database, verify a desktop note round-trip, then connect Android through a private NetBird HTTPS route.
- **Proven locally:** Mos can receive an opt-in, text-only screen summary through `qwen3.5:4b`; a parser fix preserves descriptions when the model combines a label and sentence on one line.
- Keep runtime databases separate and backed up.

## Priority 2 — Easy, trustworthy node onboarding

- Windows guided installer and diagnostics; optional per-user Scheduled Task.
- Bring Linux scripts and docs into one canonical path.
- Show exact capabilities and connection scope before starting a node.
- Android remains a dashboard until a bounded background worker can be supported and tested.

## Priority 3 — Make the interface feel alive through real signals

- Improve `/solarpunk` district population and clarify active/idle/blocked/offline evidence.
- Connect activity, node presence, pending approvals, and model availability to visible status with timestamps.
- Improve responsive/mobile navigation and simple cross-linking to the relevant action.
- Keep `/side` frozen unless that boundary changes explicitly.

## Priority 4 — Real homelab workflows

- Define device identity, capability grants, revocation, and tailnet connection policy.
- Deliver safe remote file/tab handoff only after protocol, authentication, audit, and user-visible consent are designed.
- Build the print queue workflow in simulation first; require printer state, filament/bed conditions, camera verification, and fail-closed human escalation before any real automation.
- Test local webcam/vision flows with clear recording indicators and bounded retention.

## Priority 5 — Agent collaboration and swarms

- Persist scheduler/automation state in the existing canonical coordinator model after schema reality is verified.
- Use bounded small-agent jobs and explicit resource budgets, not uncontrolled background model fan-out.
- Show provenance, parent/child tasks, model, cost/latency, and stop/cancel controls.

## Not a near-term goal

Merge the coordinator and INVENTory databases, launch a general shell-capable agent, or make all nodes fully remotely controllable. Those choices increase coupling and risk without solving the first usability gaps.
</file>

# Mycelium, in one place

> A living field guide to the Mycelium AI coordinator, INVENTory, and the devices that may join them.

Mycelium is a local-first workshop for people and AI agents to observe, organise, and carry out useful work. The goal is a connected homelab where local models and small computers cooperate, while people stay in charge of consequential actions.

## Navigate

- [[Vision and principles]] — why this exists and what good should feel like.
- [[System map]] — the actual services, boundaries, and data flow.
- [[What works today]] — usable features and honest limitations.
- [[Nodes and devices]] — what a node is and how onboarding should evolve.
- [[INVENTory and knowledge]] — what the world model stores and how it is protected.
- [[Obsidian LiveSync]] — the planned self-hosted vault sync setup.
- [[Roadmap]] — a sequenced path from the current build to the homelab vision.
- [[Recurring goals and blockers]] — what has been revisited, what stopped integration, and what is now fixed.
- [[Decisions and questions]] — choices we have made and questions still open.

## A useful mental model

**INVENTory describes the world. The coordinator routes work. Nodes volunteer bounded capabilities. Views help a person understand and steer the system.** They are separate services connected through deliberate APIs; this vault documents them and does not replace their databases.

## Current status

- Coordinator: `mycelium-ai-main/`, local web UI on port 8000.
- INVENTory: `inventory/`, independent world-model API on port 8080.
- Desktop scanner: `Mycelium/agent/`, separate local scanner/UI on port 8787.
- Local start scripts: `tools/start-local.ps1` and `tools/install-autostart.ps1`.
- Coordinator scheduler: four bounded read-only checks; status at `/system` and `/api/v1/jobs/scheduler`.
- Node worker: pull-only client; Windows/Linux core support exists, but onboarding is uneven. Android is not yet a supported background node.

## The one active outcome

Make this project vault usable on your devices before adding another integration:

1. Open `Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/` as its own Obsidian vault. The currently open vault is **Solarlab**; it is configured for CouchDB database `solarlab`. This project folder is separate and has not been configured for LiveSync.
2. Configure this project vault with its own CouchDB database and verify one harmless note syncs from desktop to CouchDB and back.
3. Add the private NetBird HTTPS route, then verify that same note reaches Android and returns to desktop.

Keep Solarlab separate. This avoids accidentally mixing or syncing its files with the Mycelium project notes. The local CouchDB endpoint is answering; the note round-trip and Android route are the remaining sync checks.

See [[What works today]] for current boundaries. This vault is a project guide, not a live status dashboard.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/System map.md">
# System map

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Person[Person] --> UI[Coordinator UI :8000]
  UI --> C[Coordinator API, task queue, read-only scheduler]
  C -->|loopback HTTP bridge| I[INVENTory API :8080]
  N[Pull-only node workers] -->|register, heartbeat, claim| C
  C --> H[Local Hermes :8642]
  C --> O[Local Ollama :11434]
  S[Desktop scanner :8787] -. separate runtime .-> Person
  V[Obsidian project vault] -. documentation and shared context .-> Person
  L[CouchDB LiveSync] -. encrypted vault sync .-> V
```

## Runtime ownership

| Component | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| Coordinator | routing, proposals, queue execution, local agent-facing surfaces, bounded read-only status schedule | INVENTory entities or arbitrary access to connected nodes |
| INVENTory | canonical world-model records and their event history | task execution or hardware control |
| Node worker | its local telemetry and explicitly enabled executors | coordinator state or an inbound server |
| Desktop scanner | its own scan/index files | writes into user projects or INVENTory |
| Obsidian vault | human-readable project notes and decisions | runtime state, task queues, credentials, or a replacement database |
| CouchDB | LiveSync transport/storage for the vault | coordinator or INVENTory data |

## Important boundaries

- Coordinator and INVENTory communicate over a constrained localhost HTTP bridge; they do not share a database or import each other's code.
- Runtime databases live outside this vault and must use their configured paths.
- A node initiates outbound polling. Current node behavior is not general remote desktop or file transfer.
- The background schedule only inspects watcher, node-health, queue, and research-source state. It does not create tasks, dispatch nodes, call models, or touch hardware.
- The `/side` experience is frozen by project instructions; it is not edited as part of this effort.

See the repository's `AGENTS.md` and `PROJECTATLAS.md` for the full executable architecture contract.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/Vision and principles.md">
# Vision and principles

## The direction

Mycelium should feel like a hopeful, active workshop for a real homelab: the person can see which devices and agents are present, what they are doing, what is waiting, and why. A digital resident should have a useful role grounded in real services or hardware, not pretend activity.

The long-term picture includes local-first agents that can hand bounded work to other agents, live presence across devices, deliberate remote access, local camera understanding, and carefully gated physical workflows such as print queues. These are goals, not claims about the current build.

## Design values

1. **Truthful presence.** “Working” means a real task or observable activity exists. Unavailable means unavailable.
2. **Local by default.** Local Hermes and Ollama are preferred. Online models are an explicit model/provider choice.
3. **People keep agency.** Proposals are reviewable; sensitive, physical, and desktop-input actions remain gated.
4. **Small capabilities.** A node offers specific capabilities; no wildcard or general shell execution.
5. **Recoverable data.** Backups before sync, migration, or destructive actions.
6. **Connected, not entangled.** Services can cooperate over APIs without merging databases or creating ambiguous ownership.
7. **Useful calm.** The interface should make the next action clear, show live signals, and avoid decorative activity that looks real but is not.

## Ethical operating line

- Do not enable camera, microphone, desktop input, fabrication, or other hardware actions without clear user intent and a visible status.
- Make node capabilities visible and revocable.
- Keep the default node pull-only and never imply that the coordinator can reach into a machine.
- Local model use does not automatically make every data flow safe; show where prompts and files go.
- Keep a human review step for external sharing, irreversible changes, and real-world actuation.
</file>

<file path="Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/What works today.md">
# What works today

This is a code-informed orientation, not a promise that every optional dependency is online at all times.

## Usable surfaces

- Coordinator web UI and API on port 8000. The `/solarpunk` view links out to work areas, displays resident status, camera scan controls, a town message field, proposal/activity feed, and a gated delegation form.
- The visible task system can queue bounded work, and a pull-only node can claim supported work when registered and online.
- Local model and vision paths can operate through Hermes/Ollama when those services and the selected model are available.
- The coordinator now starts a bounded background scheduler for read-only watcher, device-health, queue-summary, and research-source checks. These checks do not create tasks or call models/hardware.
- Solar Punk City now refreshes NPC activity/status every five seconds while the tab is visible, reports the last successful connection, and avoids an overlapping request when a slower response is still in flight.
- Mos's chat has an opt-in **Scherm betrekken** checkbox. It sends a text-only summary from the latest saved screen observation through the local vision model; the raw image does not enter Hermes chat. A synthetic end-to-end observation returned `REAL` using `qwen3.5:4b` on 2026-10-14.
- INVENTory on port 8080 stores world-model records independently.
- The desktop scanner is a separate app on port 8787.
- The per-user startup shortcut runs `tools/start-local.ps1`, which attempts the coordinator, INVENTory, Ollama, Hermes, Docker Desktop, and loopback CouchDB without stopping the remaining startup attempts when one service is unavailable.

## Live service snapshot — 2026-10-15

- Coordinator `/api/v1/health`: healthy; background scheduler: enabled and running.
- The live `/api/v1/models/routes` returns HTTP 200 and shows local chat, summary, vision, and embedding routes. Code routes are honestly marked unavailable because the running environment cannot import `code_worker`; package discovery now includes it, but the live environment has not been reinstalled or restarted since that packaging fix.
- Hermes gateway: `REAL` (v0.21.5). Ollama: reachable with five models, including `qwen3.5:4b`.
- Node registry: one node is registered but stale; no online worker can claim queued work right now.
- The live API reports five task records, matching the root `data/mycelium.db`; `mycelium-ai-main/data/mycelium.db` has zero. This suggests the running process resolves its relative DB path from a different working directory or explicit environment. I have not restarted it or changed either database, because that could switch which records the UI sees.
- Coordinator, INVENTory, Hermes, and Ollama answered their local health/API checks. The scheduler reports enabled and running; Ollama exposes five installed models, and vision reports the local Qwen3.5:4b model. This confirms reachability, not that every workflow or hardware path works.
- CouchDB `/_up` answered `ok`; a metadata-only check found database `solarlab` with seven documents. Document contents were not read. Docker CLI access to the Desktop named pipe was denied, so container state was not independently confirmed.
- Obsidian 1.14.4 is open on the **Solarlab** vault. Self-hosted LiveSync reports E2EE enabled and active connection to `127.0.0.1:5984`, database `solarlab`. The prepared `Mycelium-Knowledge-Vault/` folder is not open and has no `.obsidian` settings; it is not syncing yet.
- NetBird reports connected on this PC. One remote peer is connected through a relay and five of six peers show as not connected; the connected peer hostname looks like the Android phone, but the service route is still missing. CouchDB is bound to this PC's `127.0.0.1`, and no private HTTPS proxy is configured. Android LiveSync therefore cannot reach CouchDB yet. No controlled note round-trip or second-device sync has been verified.
- The VLM verification used a synthetic gradient image and temporary database; it did not inspect the user's live screen or camera.

## Earlier UI inspection: `/solarpunk`

The page is understandable as a workshop: navigation, residents, room scan, activity, and proposal controls are all visible. It currently showed **0 districts**, six residents marked awake, one offline item in the header, two old queued research tasks, and a camera marked ready with zero stored frames. The “working” header reflects the displayed app state; the page itself explains that resident work follows real queue tasks. That is a good honesty cue, but the current scene has little evidence of a living, connected city yet.

## Current limits

- The UI is server-rendered and has mixed interaction patterns. The `/solarpunk` page has some live polling, but not a unified real-time event stream across the product.
- Node setup is uneven: Linux has an installer, Windows is mostly manual, and Android has no supported background worker.
- A coordinator restart needs a database-path check first: the active instance and the documented project-local database appear to point at different files.
- The live coordinator currently has one registered node, but it is stale; the queued research task has no active worker to claim it. No all-purpose node-to-node file transfer exists.
- Node operations are not arbitrary remote control. Remote desktop actions are a separate opt-in capability family; they should not be confused with basic node onboarding.
- Hardware and printing paths fail closed when adapters or dependencies are absent. A real printer/camera run is not part of normal automated verification.
- Obsidian LiveSync currently connects the separate Solarlab vault to local CouchDB. The Mycelium project vault still needs its own configuration and database, then a harmless note round-trip.
- Android still needs the selected NetBird-only HTTPS route to CouchDB. The port is loopback-only; do not expose 5984 directly.

## How to try safely

1. Start local services with `tools/start-local.ps1` and check coordinator `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/jobs/scheduler`, Hermes `/api/v1/hermes/status`, Ollama `/api/tags`, and `/api/v1/vision/capabilities`.
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/solarpunk`; inspect the nodes and activity views before delegating work.
3. Keep tests on temporary databases; do not send live hardware actions through tests.
4. For remote nodes, use a private network and only the capability list required for that device.
</file>

<file path="ops/obsidian-livesync/README.md">
# Local CouchDB for the Mycelium Obsidian vault

This folder contains the local CouchDB service for Self-hosted LiveSync. It is intentionally loopback-only. The current container requires authentication for all data/admin routes (`/_up` is the status-only exception) and has CORS enabled for Obsidian's desktop/mobile app origins. Compose itself does not configure remote access, HTTPS, backups, or a vault database; those need separate setup.

## Startup and credentials

`tools/start-local.ps1` opens Docker Desktop and runs `docker compose up -d` here once the Docker engine is available. The per-user Windows Startup shortcut runs that script at sign-in. CouchDB's local status endpoint answered during the 2026-10-15 check; container state was not independently inspected because this shell could not access Docker Desktop's named pipe.

The local `.env` contains the generated CouchDB admin credential and is ignored by Git. Keep it in place and private; do not copy `.env.example` over it. If setting up a fresh checkout without `.env`, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and choose a unique username and password before starting CouchDB. On this PC the file grants read access only to the Windows account that runs the startup task and full control to the local setup account, so Compose can load it at sign-in.

## First desktop connection

In the Self-hosted LiveSync CouchDB form, use:

- URL: `http://127.0.0.1:5984`
- Username and password: the `COUCHDB_USER` and `COUCHDB_PASSWORD` values in this folder's `.env`
- Database name: a unique lower-case name for the active vault, for example `solarlab`
- Use Internal API: leave off initially; CORS is configured for Obsidian desktop
- JWT authentication and custom headers: leave off

Use the manual first-device setup if no Setup URI exists yet. Let the plugin create or connect to the database, enable end-to-end encryption, and keep the vault encryption passphrase safe. Back up the vault before initialising it. After ordinary note sync works, use the Obsidian command palette command `Self-hosted LiveSync: Copy settings as a new Setup URI` for another device. Protect the Setup URI and its passphrase separately. Android requires HTTPS; this local service is reachable only from this PC until a private HTTPS route is deliberately configured.

CouchDB's configuration API persists the current CORS/authentication settings in the container's local configuration. If the container is removed and recreated, run LiveSync's server-requirements check or upstream provisioning before connecting again.

## Manual start and status

```powershell
Set-Location ops/obsidian-livesync
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:5984/_up
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5984/_utils/` on the host to check the CouchDB admin UI. The port binds only to `127.0.0.1`; do not widen it to the LAN or internet. Android Obsidian needs HTTPS, so remote LiveSync still needs a private HTTPS endpoint over a trusted mesh network. That endpoint is not configured yet.

## Stop and backup

```powershell
docker compose stop
```

Back up `couchdb-data/` while CouchDB is stopped, and keep a separate backup of the Obsidian vault. Sync is not backup. Restore must be tested before relying on it.

`couchdb-data/` and `.env` are local runtime data and credentials; they are not project source and must not be committed.
</file>

<# test-fast: run alleen de direct geraakte test(s) + directe dependencies.
Gebruik: .\tools\test-fast.ps1 -Project inventory -TestPath tests/test_objects.py
         .\tools\test-fast.ps1 -Project coordinator -TestPath tests/test_missions.py -K some_name
Bestaande pytest, geen nieuwe infra. Output kort (-q, --tb=short). #>
param(
  [ValidateSet("inventory", "coordinator", "agent")]
  [string]$Project = "inventory",
  [string]$TestPath = "",
  [string]$K = "",
  [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 300
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
if ($Project -eq "agent") { $projDir = Join-Path $root "Mycelium/agent" }
elseif ($Project -eq "inventory") { $projDir = Join-Path $root "inventory" }
else { $projDir = Join-Path $root "mycelium-ai-main" }

# Tmp-DB discipline: raak nooit echte data aan (zie AGENTS.md).
$tmp = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
if ($Project -eq "inventory") { $env:INVENTORY_DATABASE_PATH = Join-Path $tmp ("inv_fast_{0}.db" -f $PID) }
else {
  $env:MYCELIUM_DATABASE_PATH = Join-Path $tmp ("myc_fast_{0}.db" -f $PID)
  $env:MYCELIUM_CHAT_DATABASE_PATH = Join-Path $tmp ("myc_chat_fast_{0}.db" -f $PID)
  $env:INVENTORY_DATABASE_PATH = Join-Path $tmp ("inv_fast_{0}.db" -f $PID)
}

$args = @("-q", "--tb=short")
if ($TestPath -ne "") { $args += $TestPath }
if ($K -ne "") { $args += @("-k", $K) }

$sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
Push-Location -LiteralPath $projDir
try {
  & python -m pytest @args
  $code = $LASTEXITCODE
} finally { Pop-Location }
$sw.Stop()
Write-Output ("test-fast [{0}] exit={1} duur={2:N1}s" -f $Project, $code, $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)
exit $code
</file>

<# test-full: volledige suite, alleen op expliciet verzoek of voor milestone.
Gebruik: .\tools\test-full.ps1 -Project inventory
         .\tools\test-full.ps1 -Project all
Duurt minuten (coordinator ~1860 tests). Niet als standaard-verificatie. #>
param(

  [string]$Project = "inventory"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$tmp = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()

$globalCode = 0

foreach ($p in $targets) {

    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    $sw.Stop()
    Write-Output ("test-full [{0}] exit={1} duur={2:N1}s" -f $p, $code, $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)
    if ($code -ne 0) { $globalCode = $code }
  } finally { Pop-Location }
}
exit $globalCode
</file>

<# Update de lokale stack: fast-forward pull + dependencies.
   Doet nooit force/reset en commit/pusht niets. Na afloop zelf
   herstarten (vensters sluiten + tools/start-local.ps1). #>
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot

Set-Location -LiteralPath $root
git pull --ff-only
if (-not $?) { throw "git pull weigerde (geen fast-forward?) — handmatig oplossen, niets geforceerd." }

foreach ($proj in @("inventory", "mycelium-ai-main")) {
  $venvPython = Join-Path $root "$proj\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"
  if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $venvPython) {
    & $venvPython -m pip install -e (Join-Path $root $proj)
  } else {
    Write-Output "Geen venv in $proj — sla pip over (handmatig: pip install -e ./$proj)"
  }
}
Write-Output "Update klaar. Herstart de twee uvicorn-vensters voor het nieuwe gedrag."

<file path="AUTOPILOT_ROADMAP.md.txt">
# MYCELIUM AI — AUTOPILOT ROADMAP V1

## 0. Doel

Maak van de huidige Mycelium AI + INVENTory codebase een daadwerkelijk bruikbaar systeem waarin:

* de bestaande backend-functionaliteit bereikbaar is via UI;
* Research → Mission → Node execution daadwerkelijk end-to-end werkt;
* Mycelium als persoonlijke AI/coördinator bruikbaar wordt;
* INVENTory als wereldmodel bruikbaar wordt;
* projecten, research, missions, objects en relaties samenkomen;
* de game/living-world laag uiteindelijk een Terraria/Ori-achtige interactieve interface krijgt;
* agents zelfstandig verder kunnen bouwen zonder voortdurende menselijke begeleiding.

De agents moeten niet proberen alles tegelijk te bouwen.

**Werk altijd vanuit de huidige code als source of truth.**

---

# 1. ABSOLUTE REGELS

## 1.1 Geen destructieve refactors

Agents mogen:

* nieuwe bestanden toevoegen;
* bestaande functies uitbreiden;
* kleine gerichte wijzigingen maken;
* tests toevoegen;
* UI koppelingen toevoegen;
* adapters bouwen.

Agents mogen NIET zonder expliciete reden:

* bestaande subsystemen volledig herschrijven;
* databases verwijderen;
* bestaande API's breken;
* bestaande veiligheidslagen omzeilen;
* authentication/approval gates verwijderen;
* willekeurige shell/RCE-functionaliteit introduceren;
* productiecode vervangen omdat een agent het "mooier" vindt.

---

## 1.2 Bestaande veiligheidsarchitectuur blijft leidend

Bestaande gates blijven intact:

* human approval;
* `YES` approval;
* mission status gates;
* lease;
* claim;
* attempt limits;
* ownership;
* capability checks;
* provenance;
* dispatchable kinds;
* fail-closed gedrag.

Agents mogen deze mechanismen verbeteren, maar nooit omzeilen.

---

## 1.3 Elke agent werkt in kleine verticale slices

Elke opdracht moet:

1. bestaande code inspecteren;
2. één duidelijk probleem kiezen;
3. implementeren;
4. tests schrijven;
5. relevante bestaande tests draaien;
6. `git diff --check`;
7. commit maken;
8. korte changelog/reportsamenvatting schrijven.

Geen enorme ongeteste wijzigingen.

---

# 2. HUIDIGE BASIS

# 22. AUTOPILOT WORK QUEUE

Agents trekken werk uit:

```text
AUTOPILOT_WORK_QUEUE.md
```

Elke taak bevat:

```markdown
## TASK-ID

### Goal
...

### Scope
...

### Allowed files
...

### Dependencies
...

### Acceptance criteria
...

### Tests
...

### Risk
LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH

### Status
TODO / ACTIVE / BLOCKED / DONE
```

Agents mogen zelfstandig TODO → ACTIVE → DONE uitvoeren.

Bij BLOCKED:

```text
BLOCKED
```

en naar een andere onafhankelijke taak.

---

# 23. DEFINITION OF DONE

Een taak is pas DONE wanneer:

* code werkt;
* relevante tests bestaan;
* relevante tests passeren;
* bestaande tests niet breken;
* `git diff --check` pass;
* geen security gate verwijderd;
* geen bestaande API onbedoeld gebroken;
* commit gemaakt;
* changelog bijgewerkt.

---

# 24. NACHTMODUS

Autonomous mode:

```text
while work_available:

    select_highest_priority_safe_task()

    inspect_current_code()

    implement_small_slice()

    run_targeted_tests()

    run_regression_tests()

    if pass:
        git diff --check
        commit
        update_work_queue()

    if fail:
        revert_unwanted_changes
        document_failure
        choose_next_independent_task()
```

Agents moeten **niet wachten op menselijke bevestiging voor normale codewijzigingen**.

Wel blokkeren bij:

* destructive migration;
* data deletion;
* security downgrade;
* approval bypass;
* public deployment;
* secrets;
* irreversible external actions.

---

Elke autonome cyclus eindigt met:

```text
AUTOPILOT_CHECKPOINT.md
```

Met:

```text
START COMMIT:
END COMMIT:

TASKS COMPLETED:
- ...

TESTS:
- ...

NEW FEATURES:
- ...

KNOWN FAILURES:
- ...

BLOCKED TASKS:
- ...

NEXT PRIORITIES:
- ...

REGRESSION STATUS:
PASS / FAIL
```

<file path="MYCELIUM_CANVAS_DIRECTION.md">
# INVENTory Infinite Canvas — future direction (NOT in scope)

Status: **FUTURE / ARCHITECTURAL DIRECTION ONLY.**
Date recorded (UTC): 2026-09-25.
Priority rule: this canvas must NOT restructure the roadmap. Current priority stays: close existing backend/UI gaps and make the end-to-end journey (HOME → READY → WORLD → CHAT → ADVISE → MISSION → APPROVAL → TASK → EVENT) genuinely usable.

## Concept (one paragraph)

A future additive UI layer: an interactive digital workshop for projects, ideas, research, inventory, missions and knowledge — inspired by Obsidian-style graphs, infinite-canvas tools and Terraria-like spatial exploration. It visualizes the existing world model; it never becomes a second source of truth.

## What the investigation found (CODE > TESTS > DOCS, read-only 2026-09-25)

- **Nodes ready:** all 11 INVENTory entities carry `name` + `description` + `provenance` (`inventory/app/schemas.py`); all 16 Mycelium overlay types already emit `{id, type, label, source, metadata}` (`mycelium-ai-main/coordinator/app/worldgraph.py:50-62`).
- **Edges ready:** 10 directed relationship predicates incl. `part_of/contains/became/led_to/produced_by/stored_in` (`inventory/app/schemas.py:535-546`); overlay edges (`uses_context, researches, remembers, may_relate_to, captured, HAS, PROVIDES`, …); mission→task binding via `tasks.mission_id`; research claim/source/contradiction links; events are timeline markers, not edges.
- **Spatial gap:** zero coordinate/position fields anywhere (locations explicitly "no GIS, no 3D, hierarchy via relationships"). Layout must stay client-side ephemeral until/unless a persisted-layout step is approved.
- **UI starting point:** world-graph SVG in `coordinator/app/ui.py` (`graph_panel`, `GRAPH_JS`) already pans/zooms/selects/filters over `build_world_graph` data (depth 1–2, 200 nodes/400 edges). Missing only: unbounded viewport + node dragging + search-to-focus. No `<canvas>` graphs, no JS graph libs anywhere.

## Guardrails (binding)

1. Additive only — builds on the existing world graph, relationships, overlays, project/workspace data.
2. Do NOT replace `/world`. Do NOT redesign the backend for the canvas now. Do NOT build the canvas until the current journey is genuinely usable.
3. Canvas stays read-only with deep links to existing `/web/*` gates; existing approval/provenance model unchanged.
4. No new frontend framework when it happens (extend the existing SVG approach first).
5. Persisted layout is the first and only backend-adjacent step, and only after ephemeral dragging proves valuable.

## Roadmap placement (when it happens, max 8 steps)

1. `GET /canvas` read-only page reusing `_graph_data` + `graph_panel`, unbounded viewport.
2. Client-side node dragging + search-to-focus. (MVP ends here.)
3. Workspace/area grouping (`project_ref`, `loc_`/`contains` rings).
4. Mission quest-trails + task delegation edges.
5. Research/memory/candidate overlay layers.
6. In-canvas gate buttons posting to existing `/web/*`.
7. Persisted layout (only backend-adjacent step).
8. Terraria skin (tiles/sprites/ambient) over unchanged node data.

Ladder it grows into: World → areas → objects → projects → machines → materials → missions → crafting → real-world actions — each rung a rendering rule over existing predicates/overlays, never a migration.

## Explicitly out of scope

New node/edge tables, position columns, framework additions (React/d3/cytoscape), realtime collaboration, world-gen/sprites/game loop, canvas-resident editing, 3D merge, live camera streams, offline/PWA, touching `/world`.
</file>

# PROJECTATLAS — Mycelium AI + INVENTory (BIG50)

Stand: 2026-09-25, werkboom bovenop `81db8aa`, uncommitted BIG46–55.

| A3 | node_client worker | `mycelium-ai-main/node_client/` | Generieke node: heartbeat, claim, `research.fetch_url`/`system_inventory` uitvoeren | Werkend | — | pull-only claim/complete | A2 |
| A4 | code_worker | `mycelium-ai-main/code_worker/main.py` | Bounded code.*-worker via lokale OpenCode-run | Werkend, live bewezen (BIG47/48) | — | `code.review/patch/test`, allowlist-calls | A2, lokale `opencode`-binary |

## 2. Welke game-data al gebruikt wordt

- `/play`: `game_state()`, missions, candidates, observations, inbox, notifications, bus-events, fungi-netwerk, forge-stores, INVENTory-tellingen, `play/status`-snapshot, `play/code-task`, `play/mission`, sessies.
- `/side`: candidates (discovery), advise, research queue/run-once/dossiers/plan, `play/mission`, quests, sessies (zone `side`), XP localStorage-only.
- Beide: geen tweede truth; sessie-positie is het enige game-eigendom (server-side rij, geen entiteit).

## 3. Overlapclusters (mogelijk dubbel — bewijs vastgelegd, niets hernoemd)

| Cluster | Leden | Canonieke bron | Bewijs van grens |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 plannen vs missies vs runs | `plans.py` Plan (inert) / `missions.py` Mission (uitvoerbaar) / `automation.py` AutomationRun ("NO second mission engine" :8) / `jobs.py` job_runs / research runs `res_` | Per doel: uitvoerbaar werk = **Mission**; research = **run**; automatisering = **AutomationRun** | Verschillende tabellen; `task_queue_bridge.py:12` markeert staged-grens expliciet |
| C2 taken (3 systemen) | queue-`tasks` (int-id, queued/assigned) / `CoordinatorTask` (data, approved, nooit queued) / INVENTory-`task_` (remote world-model) / quest-`task`-steps (alleen refs) | Uitvoerbare taken = **queue-`tasks`**; `CoordinatorTask` = vertaalvoorstel | `proposal_tasks.py:17-19`, `task_queue_bridge.py:12` |
| C3 projecten (3) | remote `proj_` (A1) / lokaal `ProjectContext prj-` / `project_package`-projectie (geen store) | Wereldwaarheid = **INVENTory `proj_`**; lokaal alleen context | `project_package.py:14` (geen store) |
| C4 kennisgeheugen (3 paden) | candidates `cand_` / memories `mem_` / research records+dossiers | Feit = **memory**; kandidaat/dossier = voorfase | `promote_candidate`, `remember_dossier`, `mirror_record` met fingerprint-dedup |
| C5 gamepagina's | `/play` (top-down runtime) / `/side` (side-view slice) / `/game` (hub) / `/canvas` (workbench-lens) | Primaire runtime = **`/side`** (BIG51-gebruikerskeuze, zie §6); `/play` behouden; `/game` = hub | Verschillende presentatie, zelfde stores; géén derde game-ervaring gebouwd |

## 4. Aantoonbaar missend / gesimuleerd / offline / niet-aangesloten

- Printer/fabricage: SIMULATED slicer, geen printer/adapter → UNAVAILABLE; `paho-mqtt` ontbreekt stock (`REALITY_MAP §C`, code-bewijs). Fysiek printen = BLOCKED achter exact-YES + hardware.
- CAD-runtimes (OpenSCAD/FreeCAD/Blender): UNAVAILABLE; alleen `procedural-test`.
- Camera live/VLM/GPU: geen capture-adapter → file-ingest only, VLM-fallback eerlijk.
- Research providers: `wikipedia` vereist internet (offline → eerlijke `ran:false`); `test` vereist fixtures; Instagram UNAVAILABLE (alleen manual/mock).
- Embeddings/STT/TTS/WEB_PUSH/Garmin-live/robots/drones: UNAVAILABLE/MOCK by design.
- INVENTory-bridge: GET-only loopback; `:8080` offline → alle world-data UNAVAILABLE (advise degradeert eerlijk).
- Game: geen XP-economie, geen multiplayer, geen SSE/polling, touch niet op hardware getest.

## 5. Statusmodellen (canoniek, voor game-weergave)

- Mission: `draft → pending_approval → approved → running → completed`, plus `paused/failed/cancelled/blocked`. Exact-YES enige approve-weg. Steps: `pending → dispatched → completed` (queue-pad) of inline runners.
- Quest: alleen def opgeslagen; state live afgeleid (`COMPLETE/ACTIVE/WAITING/BLOCKED/FAILED/MISSING`), `done/total` echt.
- Campaign: afgeleid over quests; seeds zijn draft-missies + koppelquests.
- Task: `queued → assigned → completed/failed` (lease/fencing/capability-gated); `staged` nooit claimbaar.
- Research run: `draft/collecting/…/completed/blocked/failed/cancelled/unavailable` + `execution_state REAL/SIMULATED/TEST/UNAVAILABLE`; alleen `draft/blocked/failed` herstartbaar. Plan vereist **completed dossier met inhoud**, anders 422.
- Candidate: `observation → candidate → supported (2 supporters) → promoted`; fact-tier eist `verified_by`.
- Approvals: mission-YES, write-YES (+fingerprint/TTL/revalidate), voice (nooit fysiek), promotion human `staged→queued`. Niets omzeild.

## 6. BIG51 — game-first productrichting (gebruikerskeuze, leidend)

De side-view game (`/side`) is de primaire Mycelium-ervaring: een
Terraria-geïnspireerde eigen gamewereld waarin echte projecten,
backend-mogelijkheden en voortgang begrijpelijk en bruikbaar zijn.
Deze keuze heeft voorrang op verouderde roadmaptekst (AUTOPILOT
P0–P3 "game last", ROADMAP-V2, BIG48 "`/play` = runtime",
CANVAS_DIRECTION "FUTURE"): die documenten blijven archief
(intentie op schrijfmoment), geen sturing.

Behouden architectuurregels (ongewijzigd, getest):

- Bestaande backend is leidend; de game is VIEW, geen tweede
  missie-/project-/task-/kennisdatabase (`play_journal()` is
  read-only rangschikking; sessie-positie blijft het enige
  game-eigendom).
- INVENTory blijft bron van waarheid via de read-only loopback
  bridge (GET-only, timeout ≤ 5s); offline → UNAVAILABLE, leeg →
  eerlijk leeg, nooit verzonnen.
- Approvals blijven intact: operationele missies met echte
  effecten alleen achter de bestaande exacte YES; XP is optionele
  beloning (localStorage), geen toegangspoort, geen bewijs van
  voortgang.
- Bestaande `/play-`, `/world-`, `/side-` en dashboardroutes
  blijven werken zolang nuttig; geen derde game-ervaring.
  Journal/Command Center (`GET /api/v1/play/journal` + in-game
  Journal-view) toont missions/quests/research/vondsten én echte
  `proj_`-records en onthouden `mem_`-records met bronrecord +
  deeplink.

## 7. Bronverwijzingen (routes/tests per model)

Zie subatlas: modellen+routes+tests zijn volledig geïnventariseerd in de BIG50-werknotities (missions/quests/campaigns/tasks/projects/research/knowledge/approvals met module-, regel- en testverwijzingen). Kernroutes: `POST /api/v1/missions`, `/approve`, `/tick`, `/dispatch`; `POST /api/v1/quests`; `POST /api/v1/campaigns`; `POST /api/v1/tasks`, `/claim`, `/complete`; `POST /api/v1/research/queue`, `/queue/run-once`, `/runs/{id}/execute`, `/dossiers/{id}`, `/{id}/plan`; `POST /api/v1/candidates`, `/support`, `/promote`, `/reject`; `POST /api/v1/play/mission`, `/play/code-task`, `/play/session`, `/play/position`. Game: `/play` (L18608), `/side` (L21275), `/game`, `/quests`, `/world`. Paginagroen: 55 HTML-routes in `coordinator/app/main.py`, 33 in `inventory/app/main.py`, `Mycelium/agent/agent_ui.py` (`:8787`).

## 3. Databases (SQLite WAL, tmp-discipline bij experimenten)

| DB | Env-var | Default | Opmerking |
|---|---|---|---|
| INVENTory | `INVENTORY_DATABASE_PATH` | `inventory/data/inventory.db` (gitignored) | `busy_timeout=15000` load-bearing; `*_fts` = afgeleide index (`rebuild_fts()`), nooit direct schrijven |
| Coordinator | `MYCELIUM_DATABASE_PATH` | `mycelium-ai-main/data/mycelium.db` | additieve idempotente migraties (`_ensure_*_columns`) |
| Chat | `MYCELIUM_CHAT_DATABASE_PATH` | `mycelium-ai-main/data/mycelium-chat.db` | apart van hoofd-DB |
| Agent | — (JSON) | `Mycelium/agent/{discovery.json,project_index.json}` | data, geen source; bridge dry-run only |

Strays (nooit openen): root `data/mycelium*.db`,
`data/inventory.db`, `mycelium-ai-main/data/inventory.db`.
Runtime-caveat (2026-10-14): the live coordinator on `:8000` reports
five task records, matching root `data/mycelium.db`; the project-local
`mycelium-ai-main/data/mycelium.db` has zero. The checked-in startup
script sets the project working directory, but the currently running
process appears to have been launched with a different cwd or explicit
database env var. Do not assume root DB copies are inactive until that
process and its environment are reconciled; do not overwrite either DB.
Let op: quests/campaigns/research-runs/dossiers/queue/workspaces/
candidates/automation-runs hebben routes+logica+tests maar deels
**geen `CREATE TABLE`** — geen restart-duurzaamheid aannemen.

## 4. API's (canoniek)

- INVENTory (`:8080`, prefix-IDs `obj_/proj_/idea_/rel_/evt_/hw_/sns_/cam_/loc_/mod_/task_/act_/file_`):
  CRUD objects/projects/ideas, relationships (geen PATCH/single-GET
  by design), read-only `GET /api/v1/events?entity_id&limit&since`,
  search (`sanitize_fts_query()`, alleen `SEARCHABLE_TYPES`),
  graph. Elke mutatie appendt een event (`_append_event()`).
  `mod_` = AI-model (géén 3D-model; 3D = `mdl_` in coordinator,
  `files/file_` met `file_kind=cad|mesh|gcode` is het 3D-register).
- Coordinator (`:8000`, 530 routes): missions
  (`POST /api/v1/missions`, `/approve` exact-YES, `/tick`, `/dispatch`),
  queue-taken (`POST /api/v1/tasks`, `/claim`, `/complete`;
  lease 300s, 3 attempts, staleness 60s), research queue/run-once/
  dossiers/plan, candidates (`/support`, `/promote`), controlled
  writes (`/api/v1/writes/*`), nodes/routing, vision, fab/prints,
  project-package, context-packets, automation-runs, game-state
  (`GET /api/v1/play/journal`, `play/session`, `play/position`).

## 8. 3D / workshop

Coordinator `coordinator/app/` `cad.py`, `fabrication.py`,
`fab_flow.py`, `workshop*.py`, `forge*`, routes `/api/v1/fab/*`,
`/api/v1/prints/*`, `/3d`, `/forge`. Keten: object → test-mesh →
validatie → File → test-slice → G-code-safety → File → fysieke
YES → gesimuleerde uitvoering → telemetrie + camera-verificatie.
Slicer gesimuleerd, geen echte printertransporten, geen
`safe_to_execute` nergens. Register: `files/file_`
(`cad|mesh|gcode`), coordinator-IDs `mdl_`.
Externe bibliotheekmodellen: operator downloadt handmatig naar de
bibliotheekmap (geen auto-download, geen credentials), scant via
`scan_library()` en legt herkomst + licentie vast met
`attach_library_license()` (`workshop3d.ModelLicense`: source_library,
source_url, author, license, commercial_use, remix_allowed,
attribution_required, original_model_url, imported_at). Vage namen
("open source", "free") en licentieloze externe herkomst worden
geweigerd; onbekende licenties houden alle flags op onbekend
(nooit aannemen). `library_file_fields()` propageert het blok naar
`file_`-metadata + description; INVENTory-schema ongewijzigd.
Importketen (operator-expliciet): `coordinator/app/library_sources.py`
(catalogus + Commons-zoekopdracht + `gate_import()` + begrensde
download) → `mdl_`-record → `file_`-voorstel via bestaande
`propose_inventory_write()` + YES-gate (`/writes`).
Routes: `GET /api/v1/workshop/libraries`, `POST .../libraries/search`,
`POST .../libraries/import`, `POST /web/workshop/libraries/import`;
`/3d` heeft een **Modelbibliotheken**-sectie (bronkaarten, zoeken,
licentie-chips JA/NEE/ONBEKEND, Importvoorstel-knop).
Geschikte bronnen zonder API-key: Wikimedia Commons API
(extmetadata-licenties), NIH 3D (licentie per entry lezen),
NASA 3D Resources/GitHub-mirror (zonder copyright). Details:
`mycelium-ai-main/docs/3d-model-libraries.md`.

## 11. Mycelium coordinator (samenvatting)

Missies (uitvoerbaar) vs Plan (inert) vs AutomationRun vs
research-run (`res_`) vs queue-`tasks` (int, queued/assigned) vs
`ctask-` (goedgekeurd voorstel, nooit queued) vs inventory-`task_`
(wereldrecord, executeert nooit) — bewust gescheiden tabellen,
niet unificeren. Een vaste coordinator-scheduler voert alleen
begrensde, read-only `watcher_scan` (10 min), `device_health` (5
min), `inventory_reconcile` (30 min) en `research_process` (60 min)
uit. Deze maakt geen queue-taken, dispatcht geen nodes, roept geen
modellen of hardware aan en keurt niets goed. Standaard actief;
`MYCELIUM_BACKGROUND_SCHEDULER=0` schakelt hem uit. Status via
`GET /api/v1/jobs/scheduler` en `/system`; eigen run-historie blijft
begrensd in bestaande `job_runs`. Missies, automation, research-queue
uitvoering en maintenance blijven expliciet. Ontbrekende providers
degraderen eerlijk.
`GET /api/v1/models/routes` currently shows the local Ollama routes;
`code` and `code-review` remain unavailable when the active Python
environment cannot import `code_worker`. Package discovery now includes
that package; reinstall/restart is still needed to apply the packaging fix.
Town (Solar Punk City): `town_chat.py` (gesprekken op bestaande
chat-tabellen, town-rol in sources, round-robin of targeted
`npc_id`, max 1 NPC-beurt) + `town_memory.py` (tabel
`town_memories`, recall belang+recency, reflect 409 zonder
model) + `ollama_chat.py` (lokale fallback: Hermes → Ollama
→ eerlijke noot; model via `OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL`, default
phi4-mini) + `town_actors.py` (NPC-aanwezigheid: tabellen
`town_actors`/`town_activity`; status verandert alleen op
echte signalen — queue-taken aan `town:{npc}` gebonden,
anders idle; walk-up chat binnen 100 eenheden) +
`town_proposals.py` (delegatie: voorstel met actie/
rechtvaardiging/blast-radius/confidence, exact-YES →
queue-taak met provenance `town:{npc}`; dial via
`TOWN_AUTONOMY`, default leeg, hardware/desktop nooit).
Residents-, activiteiten- en Bureaupaneel op `/solarpunk`.
NPC-status en activiteit worden daar vijfseconden ververst zolang de tab
zichtbaar is; de statusregel toont de laatste succesvolle verbinding.
Kijkrichting `a` persisteert mee (additieve `angle`-kolom op
play_sessions; callers zonder `a` laten hem staan). Forge heeft
een 3D-snapshot-preview-toggle (zelfde pinned three@0.160.0 +
fallback; 2D-editor blijft leidend) en BUILD-queuet mee
(prepare/slice/propose/preflight/enqueue als fetch-knoppen;
server blijft gaten). Insta360-frames 1-klik zichtbaar via
`GET /api/v1/cameras/observations/{id}/image`
(allow-listed read; "Bekijk beeld" in het scan-paneel).
Remote muis/toetsenbord loopt via `/nodes` (Digital-World-pad,
expliciete YES-sessie); vensters zijn titels-only, er is geen
file-transfer — dat is backend-werk, geen UI-werk.

## 1. What this repo is

Single root git repo, three runtime areas, no shared code or DB:

- `inventory/` — world-model store. FastAPI (`app/main.py`) + SQLite
  WAL on port **8080**.
- `mycelium-ai-main/` — coordinator (`coordinator/app/main.py`,
  ~26k lines / ~546 routes) + pull-only worker (`node_client/`) on
  port **8000**.
- `Mycelium/agent/` — local desktop scanner (Flask UI on **8787**),
  read-only toward user projects.

Trust order: `AGENTS.md` > `PROJECTATLAS.md` > code + tests >
lab journal (`AI_HANDOFF/PROJECT_STATE.md`) > roadmaps/READMEs
(snapshots, often stale).

## 2. What was built (Oct 2026) — reuse it, don't rebuild it

A town layer for NPC agents. All state lives in existing DBs
(additive tables in the chat DB, queue rows in the mycelium DB).
No second database, no scheduler, no background threads.

| Piece | Module | Routes |
|---|---|---|
| Town chat (round-robin or targeted `npc_id`, max 1 NPC turn, honest note without model) | `coordinator/app/town_chat.py` | `POST /api/v1/town/conversations`, `.../{id}/messages` |
| Town memory (`town_memories`, importance+recency, reflect 409 without model) | `town_memory.py` | `POST /api/v1/town/reflect` |
| NPC presence (`town_actors`/`town_activity`; status changes on real signals only — queued `town:{npc}` tasks — else honest `idle`) | `town_actors.py` | `GET /api/v1/town/actors` |
| Delegation (NPC drafts JSON spec → stored proposal with action/justification/blast-radius/confidence → literal `YES` queues one task; anything else rejects; second decision 409) | `town_proposals.py` | `POST /api/v1/town/npc/{id}/delegate`, `GET /api/v1/town/proposals`, `POST .../{pid}/decide`, `GET /api/v1/town/autonomy` |
| Autonomy dial (`TOWN_AUTONOMY="npc:kind"`, default empty; only `research.fetch_url`/`system_inventory`/`desktop_screenshot` may ever be listed; hardware/desktop-input never; auto-decisions logged as `standing-rule:TOWN_AUTONOMY`) | `town_proposals.py` | (same as above) |
| NPC chat chain (Hermes → Ollama → honest note; `OLLAMA_CHAT_MODEL`, default `phi4-mini`) | `hermes_npc.py`, `ollama_chat.py`, `hermes_bridge.py` | `POST /api/v1/hermes/chat`, `GET /api/v1/hermes/history`, `GET /api/v1/hermes/status` |
| Insta360 one-frame grab + 1-click view | `capture_probe.py`, `cameras.py` | `POST /api/v1/cameras/{id}/probe-grab`, `GET /api/v1/cameras/observations/{id}/image` |
| Forge 3D snapshot preview + BUILD queue buttons | `forge.py` | page `/forge`, actions via `/web/workshop/fabjobs/{id}/{action}` |
| Remote mouse/keyboard (opt-in node caps, explicit YES sessions) | `remote_input.py`, `node_client/` | UI on `/nodes`, API `/api/v1/remote-input/*` |

Tests: ~1950 coordinator (`pytest -v` in `mycelium-ai-main/`, tmp DBs
via env vars — never touch `data/*.db`), ~183 inventory, ~100 agent.
FAST after every edit (touched module only), FEATURE at feature
boundary, FULL only for milestones. See `docs/TESTING.md`.

## 3. Contract (non-negotiable unless the human says otherwise)

- No auto-approval, no scheduler, no background threads. Execution =
  proposal → exact-`YES` → execute → verify. Desktop input always
  exact-YES. Hardware fail-closed + mocked in pytest, never live in
  tests.
- Loopback only (`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`::1`); coordinator →
  INVENTory is GET-mostly over HTTP, never shared DB/imports.
- No credentials in code/docs/tests/logs. No shell/RCE.
- `/side` is frozen (read/test ok, never edit).
- Never commit/push/reset without an explicit order.
- Three.js only on `/homebase` + `/forge` preview (pinned
  `three@0.160.0` via unpkg + honest fallback); Canvas2D elsewhere.
- Living Principles (`mycelium-ai-main/docs/living-principles.md`):
  old laptops stay usable, energy visible, local-first, human
  overrides automation.

## 4. Why the game UI didn't land (honest retrospective)

The `/solarpunk` first-person raycaster works (movement, mouse-look,
NPC billboards, walk-up talk HUD, in-game chat — all proven with
headless-Chrome screenshots, zero JS errors) but never looked like
what the human wanted (GalaxyHQ/my-virtual-office polish). Causes:

1. **Fidelity gap**: flat-shaded Canvas2D + billboard sprites read as
   programmer art next to real 3D/pixel-art offices. More paint
   layers didn't close a taste gap.
2. **Label clutter**: 6 NPCs on one ray = overlapping name chips
   (later fixed with near→far declutter, but trust was gone).
3. **Stale pages**: inline-JS pages were browser-cached, so fixes
   didn't appear until hard refresh (later fixed with
   `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/solarpunk`).
4. **Model latency**: Hermes replies take ~30s+; the city feels
   asleep next to instant local UI.
5. **Empty world**: 0 districts until INVENTory has locations; NPCs
   700+ units from the old spawn (later fixed with a plaza spawn).
6. **Gateway limits**: the Hermes gateway offers chat only
   (`POST /v1/chat/completions` + `GET /health`, Bearer key,
   `X-Hermes-Session-Key` identity). No tools/tasks/presence — all
   "agentic" behavior (proposals, queue, dial, audit) is coordinator
   logic in §2. Don't expect it from the gateway.

## 5. Recommended ways forward with Hermes

- **A. Existing Hermes offices**: VirtOffice (3D, built for Hermes
  AgentOS subagents) or eliautobot/my-virtual-office (2D pixel,
  Hermes-supported). Point one at the gateway for presence, keep
  this coordinator beside it for memory/tasks/camera (§2 endpoints).
- **B. Keep the §2 backend, replace the frontend**: the endpoints
  are frontend-agnostic; any client can drive town life from them.
- **C. Extend the gateway first**: if agents must act (not just
  chat), the gateway needs tool/task/presence endpoints before any
  UI work matters.


"""Tests voor INVENTory M7.5 — File-entiteit (record only).

Uitsluitend tijdelijke databases via INVENTORY_DATABASE_PATH. Geen echte
gebruikersdata wordt geraakt. Een File-record beschrijft een artefact; deze
tests openen, kopiëren, importeren of lezen geen enkel bestand: alle
SHA-256-waarden zijn vaste teststrings, nooit berekend over echte data.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

SHA = "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
SHA2 = "5feceb66ffc86f38d952786c6d696c79c2dbc239dd4e91b46729d73a27fb57e9"


@pytest.fixture()
def client(tmp_path):
    os.environ["INVENTORY_DATABASE_PATH"] = str(tmp_path / "test_file.db")
    import importlib
    import app.database as db_mod
    import app.main as main_mod
    importlib.reload(db_mod)
    importlib.reload(main_mod)
    with TestClient(main_mod.app) as c:
        yield c


def make_file(client, **overrides):
    payload = {"name": "behuizing-v3.stl", "file_kind": "mesh",
               "mime_type": "model/stl", "sha256": SHA, "size_bytes": 1048576,
               "description": "behuizing werkplaats-controller"}
    payload.update(overrides)
    res = client.post("/api/v1/files", json=payload)
    assert res.status_code == 201, res.text
    return res.json()


def relate(client, from_id, predicate, to_id):
    res = client.post("/api/v1/relationships",
                      json={"from_id": from_id, "predicate": predicate,
                            "to_id": to_id})
    assert res.status_code == 201, res.text
    return res.json()


# =============================================================================
# CRUD
# =============================================================================

def test_create_file(client):
    record = make_file(client, metadata={"bron": "cad-programma"})
    assert record["id"].startswith("file_")
    assert record["name"] == "behuizing-v3.stl"
    assert record["file_kind"] == "mesh"
    assert record["mime_type"] == "model/stl"
    assert record["sha256"] == SHA
    assert record["size_bytes"] == 1048576
    assert record["metadata"] == {"bron": "cad-programma"}


def test_file_ids_unique(client):
    ids = {make_file(client, name=f"Bestand {i}")["id"] for i in range(5)}
    assert len(ids) == 5
    assert all(file_id.startswith("file_") for file_id in ids)


def test_list_files(client):
    make_file(client, name="a.stl", file_kind="mesh")
    make_file(client, name="b.gcode", file_kind="gcode", sha256=SHA2)
    res = client.get("/api/v1/files")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    names = {record["name"] for record in res.json()}
    assert {"a.stl", "b.gcode"} <= names


def test_get_file_detail(client):
    created = make_file(client)
    res = client.get(f"/api/v1/files/{created['id']}")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    assert res.json() == created
    assert client.get("/api/v1/files/file_bestaatniet").status_code == 404


def test_patch_file(client):
    created = make_file(client)
    res = client.patch(f"/api/v1/files/{created['id']}",
                       json={"description": "herziene versie",
                             "sha256": SHA2, "size_bytes": 2097152})
    assert res.status_code == 200
    updated = res.json()
    assert updated["description"] == "herziene versie"
    assert updated["sha256"] == SHA2
    assert updated["size_bytes"] == 2097152
    assert updated["name"] == "behuizing-v3.stl"
    assert client.patch("/api/v1/files/file_bestaatniet",
                        json={"description": "x"}).status_code == 404


def test_delete_file(client):
    created = make_file(client)
    assert client.delete(f"/api/v1/files/{created['id']}").status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"/api/v1/files/{created['id']}").status_code == 404
    assert client.delete("/api/v1/files/file_bestaatniet").status_code == 404

def test_invalid_sha256_rejected(client):
    for bad in ["", "xyz", "9f86", "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a0",
                "gf86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
                "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a0"
                "extra"]:
        res = client.post("/api/v1/files",
                          json={"name": "x.stl", "sha256": bad})
        assert res.status_code == 422, bad


def test_uppercase_sha256_normalized(client):
    record = make_file(client, sha256=SHA.upper())
    assert record["sha256"] == SHA

    assert client.post("/api/v1/files",
                       json={"name": "x", "sha256": SHA,
                             "file_kind": "spreadsheet"}).status_code == 422

def test_file_relationships(client):
    record = make_file(client)
    task = client.post("/api/v1/tasks",
                       json={"name": "Printen", "task_type": "other"}).json()
    obj = client.post("/api/v1/objects", json={"name": "Behuizing"}).json()
    rel_task = relate(client, task["id"], "uses", record["id"])
    assert rel_task["predicate"] == "uses"
    rel_obj = relate(client, record["id"], "related_to", obj["id"])
    assert rel_obj["predicate"] == "related_to"
    linked = {r["to_id"] for r in client.get(
        "/api/v1/relationships", params={"entity_id": record["id"]}).json()}
    assert obj["id"] in linked

def test_search_finds_file(client):
    record = make_file(client, name="Unieke Beugel", file_kind="cad",
                       mime_type="model/step")
    res = client.get("/api/v1/search", params={"q": "Unieke Beugel"})
    assert res.status_code == 200
    found = {(r["entity_type"], r["entity_id"]) for r in res.json()["results"]}
    assert ("file", record["id"]) in found
    res = client.get("/api/v1/search", params={"q": "model/step", "type": "files"})
    assert res.status_code == 200
    assert {(r["entity_type"], r["entity_id"]) for r in res.json()["results"]} == {
        ("file", record["id"])}


def test_graph_shows_file(client):
    record = make_file(client)
    obj = client.post("/api/v1/objects", json={"name": "Beugel"}).json()
    relate(client, record["id"], "related_to", obj["id"])
    res = client.get("/api/v1/graph", params={"entity_id": record["id"], "depth": 1})
    assert res.status_code == 200
    data = res.json()
    by_id = {n["entity_id"]: n for n in data["nodes"]}
    assert by_id[record["id"]]["entity_type"] == "file"
    assert by_id[record["id"]]["provenance"]["source_type"]
    assert obj["id"] in by_id
    res = client.get("/api/v1/graph", params={"entity_id": obj["id"], "depth": 1})
    assert record["id"] in {n["entity_id"] for n in res.json()["nodes"]}

def test_events_since_cursor_bounded(client):
    first = make_file(client)
    events = client.get("/api/v1/events",
                        params={"entity_id": first["id"]}).json()
    assert events and events[0]["event_type"] == "file_created"
    cursor = events[0]["timestamp"]
    # Nothing newer yet: empty page, no dump.
    assert client.get("/api/v1/events",
                      params={"since": cursor}).json() == []
    make_file(client, name="tweede.stl", sha256=SHA2)
    newer = client.get("/api/v1/events",
                       params={"since": cursor}).json()
    assert newer
    assert all(evt["timestamp"] > cursor for evt in newer)
    # Fail-closed on garbage; limit stays clamped.
    assert client.get("/api/v1/events",
                      params={"since": "geen-tijdstempel"}).status_code == 422
    assert client.get("/api/v1/events",
                      params={"since": cursor, "limit": 1}).json() != []
    capped = client.get("/api/v1/events",
                        params={"since": cursor, "limit": 5000}).json()
    assert len(capped) <= 500

# INVENTory

Een local-first wereldmodel-, geheugen- en herkomstsysteem voor de fysieke, digitale en mogelijk mentale werkplaats.

INVENTory houdt bij **wat er is en wat er gebeurt**: objecten, materialen, gereedschappen, machines, projecten, ideeën, bestanden, en relaties.

> **Status (bijgewerkt 2026-10-05):** Milestone 1A + 1B zijn de basis;
> M3+ entiteiten (hardware/sensors/cameras/locations/models/tasks/
> actuators/files), FTS5-search en graaf bestaan inmiddels
> (183 tests). De "M1B"-kop hierboven is historisch; actuele kaart:
> `docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` in de repo-root.

---

## Wat werkt (Milestones 1A + 1B)

### Milestone 1A — Fundament & Fysieke Objecten

- **Zelfstandige SQLite database** met **WAL-modus** (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) en connectie-timeouts.
- **Stabiele identifiers** met prefix `obj_...` (bijv. `obj_0192e8a1f4b8c9d2`).
- **Ingebouwd Provenance-fundament**:
  - Bronnen: `user-created`, `imported`, `ai-generated`, `sensor-observed`, `external-source`.
  - Strikte regel: AI-observaties zijn standaard **ongeverifieerd** (`human_verified = False`) totdat een mens ze bevestigt.
- **Object CRUD API**:
  - `GET /api/v1/health`
  - `GET /api/v1/objects`
  - `GET /api/v1/objects/{id}`
  - `POST /api/v1/objects`
  - `PATCH /api/v1/objects/{id}`
  - `DELETE /api/v1/objects/{id}`
- **Server-rendered Web UI**:
  - Overzichtstabel op `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` met herkomst-badges (`🤖 AI (unverified)`, `👤 User`, etc.).
  - Webformulier om direct nieuwe objecten in te voeren.
  - Detailpagina op `http://127.0.0.1:8080/objects/{id}` met volledige provenance-historie en ruwe JSON.
- **Geautomatiseerde testsuite** (`pytest`): 183 tests in 13 bestanden
  (telling 2026-10-05 via `def test_`). Oudere "35 tests in
  3 bestanden"- en "73 tests"-claims zijn vervallen; alleen dit
  reproduceerbare aantal geldt. Teststrategie FAST/FEATURE/FULL:
  zie `docs/TESTING.md` in de repo-root.

### Milestone 1B — Projecten, Ideeën, Relaties, Events (geïmplementeerd)

- **Project CRUD API** (`proj_...`-IDs, status `idea…archived`):
  - `GET /api/v1/projects`
  - `POST /api/v1/projects`
  - `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}`
  - `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}`
  - `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{id}`
- **Idea CRUD API** (`idea_...`-IDs, status `raw…converted`): zelfde vijf routes
  onder `/api/v1/ideas`.
- **Relationship API** (`rel_...`-IDs, 10 predicaten o.a. `used_in`, `part_of`,
  `contains`, `became`, `led_to`, `depends_on`, `produced_by`, `stored_in`;
  geen zelfreferentie):
  - `GET /api/v1/relationships`
  - `POST /api/v1/relationships`
  - `DELETE /api/v1/relationships/{id}`
- **Event-stream** (alleen lezen): `GET /api/v1/events` — registreert alle
  CRUD-overgangen met `entity_id`, timestamp en provenance.
- **Web UI-uitbreiding**: overzicht- en detailpagina's voor projecten en ideeën
  (`/projects`, `/projects/{id}`, `/ideas`, `/ideas/{id}`) plus relatiebeheer
  op de detailpagina's.
